items.label: 2A
items.claim: NIH/NHGRI's new 5-year Illumina consumables vehicle has used only about 6% of its $90M ceiling in roughly 4.5 months.
items.detail: IDV 75N98026D00035 (start 21 May 2026, sole source, one bid) showed $5.35M obligated as of the 8 Oct 2026 page update. That is a pace of about $14M a year against an average ceiling of $18M a year. A search snippet showed $1.30M earlier, so obligations are rising but small. This is only a weak read on government research demand, because it covers one institute's orders and no product detail is public.
items.why_new: The known list has no NIH/NHGRI Illumina IDV obligation-pace datapoint.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Harvard Bauer Core's NovaSeq X 25B 300-cycle lane price rose 17.8% in FY27 after a 17.4% cut in FY26, ending only about 2.7% below FY25.
items.detail: Search-result summaries give the 25B 300-cycle Harvard-account lane at $2,494 (FY25 Rates page), $2,059 (FY26) and $2,426 (FY27). The PO rate went $2,883 → $3,396 (+17.8%). The FY25→FY26 move is −17.4% and FY26→FY27 is +17.8%, so the net FY25→FY27 change is −2.7%. A core that passes through its reagent cost did not see falling Illumina 25B prices over the two years. I could not open the pages (403), so the figures are unverified and the FY25 figure is a single snippet. The FY25 NGS page showed conflicting 1.5B numbers, so the FY25 25B value is lower confidence.
items.source_name: Harvard Bauer Core price pages (FY25/FY26/FY27, search snippets)
items.why_new: The known list has only $2.06→$2.43. The FY25 $2,494 anchor and the round-trip framing are new.
items.verify_note: The FY26→FY27 move ($2,059→$2,426, +17.8%) is already known. The only new part is FY25 at $2,494 from a single snippet the item itself flags as low confidence, so FY26 looks like a one-year dip. The page returned 403 again and could not be verified. Core internal rates mix reagent cost with cost recovery.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: At Bauer the 25B-vs-10B per-read discount at 300 cycles narrowed from 36.8% to 26.2%, while at 100 cycles it widened from 40% to 45.5%.
items.detail: The 25B lane has 2.5B reads and the 10B lane has 1B reads. At 300 cycles, FY26 is $2,059/2.5 = $824 vs $1,304 per billion reads (−36.8%). FY27 is $2,426/2.5 = $970 vs $1,314 (−26.2%). At 200 cycles, $732 vs $1,234 (−40.7%) becomes $857 vs $1,193 (−28.2%). At 100 cycles, $604 vs $1,011 (−40.3%) becomes $561 vs $1,030 (−45.5%). The within-X volume step is shrinking in the long-read products the core mostly sells, which suggests that discount on the 25B is a policy variable rather than a fixed Illumina curve. This item fits the 'discounting by tier is not uniform' view and is neutral on a new 35B cut.
items.why_new: The full 10B/25B ladder across 100/200/300 cycles and the per-read gap by cycle count are new.
items.verify_note: The arithmetic is correct, but the label is wrong. A narrowing 25B discount at 200 and 300 cycles cuts against faster within-X deflation, and the 'policy variable' reading does not support 1B. It also duplicates F777 in per-read terms. The reads per lane (2.5B for the 25B, 1B for the 10B) are below spec (about 3.1–3.25B and 1.25B), though the ratios are unaffected.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: The full Bauer FY27 X ladder rose almost everywhere: 25B 200c +17.1%, 5B 300c +7.2%, 1.5B 300c +25.5%, 10B 300c +0.8%.
items.why_new: Only the 25B 300-cycle values were known. The other 11 rows are new.
items.verify_note: The figures were not verifiable (403). The percentages are internally consistent (for example 1.5B 300c $1,616→$2,028 = +25.5%). As the item itself says, core rates do not reveal Illumina's kit price, so this is weak evidence against 1B.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: At 100 cycles the Bauer 25B lane is now about $5.61 per Gb versus $6.04 a year earlier, a 7% fall, so shorter-read products are being repriced even as the 300-cycle lane rose.
items.detail: Using reads × cycles as the output proxy (2.5B reads × 100 = 250 Gb per lane, a conservative proxy), $1,511/250 = $6.04 (FY26) → $1,403/250 = $5.61 (FY27). At 200 cycles (500 Gb): $3.66 → $4.29 (+17%). At 300 cycles (750 Gb): $2.75 → $3.23 (+17.8%). Illumina spec output per lane is higher than this proxy, so the absolute $/Gb levels are overstated, but the year-over-year ratios hold. The 100-cycle cut is selective and likely lines up with a flow-cell price tweak, not a general decline.
items.why_new: This is a $/Gb per cycle-count derivation across the ladder. None existed.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Bauer's 5B flow cell at 300 cycles costs about $1.42 per million reads versus $0.97 for the 25B and $1.31 for the 10B in FY27, which keeps pricing steeply tiered by volume.
items.detail: FY27 300-cycle: 5B $799/562M reads = $1.42 per M reads; 10B $1,314/1,000M = $1.31; 25B $2,426/2,500M = $0.97. The 5B premium over the 25B is 46%. Illumina's volume-tier structure leaves big room for off-schedule discounting at top-end buyers, consistent with the thesis that large accounts get much lower net prices than small users.
items.why_new: The 5B row at Bauer was not previously known and the per-read tier comparison is new.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Harvard external (PO) pricing for the 25B 300-cycle lane is 40% above the internal account rate in FY27, versus 40% in FY26, so internal/external gaps in research are persistent.
items.detail: FY27: $3,396 PO vs $2,426 account (+40.0%). FY26: $2,883 vs $2,059 (+40.0%). Same ratio for the 10B 300c ($1,840 vs $1,314 = +40.0%). Research-core pricing is tiered 40% by buyer type, supporting the idea that the research buyer's price depends on negotiating position rather than a uniform list. It is not price pressure by itself.
items.why_new: A fixed 40% PO uplift at Bauer is new.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: A Harvard core raising its own 25B and 1.5B lane prices by 18–30% in FY27 shows no pass-through of research price pressure at a large academic account.
items.detail: The 1.5B lane rose 25–30% and the 25B 300c lane 17.8%, despite NIH funding strain. Either Illumina's list/contract costs rose (consistent with FY26 memory and freight cost-sharing commentary) or the core is correcting a below-cost FY26 rate (FY26 was −17% vs FY25). The latter fits a one-year promotional dip rather than a structural price decline. Unverified: no stated reason found because the announcements page was blocked.
items.why_new: This is the first multi-year (FY25→FY27) view of a Harvard core's X pricing.
items.verify_note: This adds no data beyond F766 and F768, and its explanation (Illumina cost rise vs a correction of a below-cost FY26 rate) is speculation with no stated reason found.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Bauer's X and 6000 rows could not be separated; the page snippets list only X Plus, NextSeq 1000, MiSeq and NovaSeq SP, suggesting the core no longer offers 6000 S4 lanes.
items.detail: Searches returned no Bauer NovaSeq 6000 S4 or S2 rate in FY26 or FY27. The older NGS page snippet (undated, probably FY24/25) lists NovaSeq SP alongside NextSeq 500. Absence in a snippet is weak evidence, and the page itself was not readable. Harvard (a large research account) therefore looks like a core with little or no 6000 tail, consistent with research being ~92% X.
items.why_new: The earlier known cores listed in the exclusion list include Harvard only at the 25B 300 level.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: A Spanish public research foundation (FRCB-IDIBAPS) is tendering NovaSeq X Plus 25B sequencing in competitive lots, including single-lane runs that do not fill a flow cell.
items.detail: TED 528143-2026 (30 Jul 2026) covers sequencing for lymphoid-neoplasm research projects, with an estimated duration of 760 days. One lot was sequencing 64 lanes on the X Plus 25B in batches of 8. Change notice 536530-2026 (3 Aug 2026) retitled the lots as 12 25B flow cells of 100 cycles and 100 independently processed 25B-300 lanes. This is the search-result snippet only, so value and award criteria are unread. Follow-on to the known IDIBAPS June 2025 award at €16,000 per 25B-300 flow cell.
items.why_new: This is a new 2026 re-tender by the same buyer, with a lot structure of 12 flow cells and 100 lanes. The known item is the June 2025 award only.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Bauer's 10B 300-cycle lane fell 4.4% from FY25 to FY26 and rose only 0.8% in FY27, so within-X steps move unevenly.
items.detail: The 10B 300-cycle lane on a Harvard account code was $1,364 (FY25, updated 1 Apr 2025), $1,304 (FY26) and $1,314 (FY27). On the page's 1B reads per lane that is $4.55, $4.35 and $4.38 per Gb. The FY26 100-cycle lane was flat ($1,005→$1,011) and the 200-cycle lane rose 1.8% ($1,212→$1,234). FY27 10B 300 is +0.8%, already known. The FY25→FY26 series is new.
items.why_new: Adds FY25 and FY26 10B values and $/Gb. F766-773 cover only FY26→FY27.
items.verify_note: The new FY25→FY26 10B 300c move (−4.4%, $1,364→$1,304) is followed by +0.8%, which is about −2%/yr. That is slow deflation, so the evidence cuts against 1B rather than supporting it. It is snippet-level and unverified.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Search snippets conflict with F766 on the FY26 25B move: the FY25 page appears to show the same $2,059 300-cycle lane, which would mean no FY26 cut.
items.detail: The FY25 page snippet (updated 1 Apr 2025) gave 25B 300-cycle at $2,059 (account) and $2,883 (PO), identical to FY26. F766 reports a 17.4% cut in FY26, which implies about $2,493 in FY25. One snippet may have mixed years or the 25B may have been repriced mid-FY25. On the stated numbers FY27 is $2,426 (+17.8% vs $2,059), or $3.23/Gb vs $2.75/Gb on 750 Gb. Needs checking against the page itself.
items.why_new: Flags a possible contradiction in the ledger rather than adding a new datapoint.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: The 10B-to-25B per-Gb premium at Bauer narrowed from about 1.58x in FY26 to about 1.36x in FY27, so the 25B is losing its price advantage rather than deflating.
items.detail: FY26: $1,304/300 Gb = $4.35/Gb for the 10B vs $2,059/750 Gb = $2.75/Gb for the 25B, a ratio of 1.58x. FY27: $1,314/300 = $4.38 vs $2,426/750 = $3.23, a ratio of 1.36x. The narrowing comes entirely from the 25B rise, which cuts against the idea that bigger flow cells keep pushing price per Gb down at core level. This assumes 1B and 2.5B reads per lane as stated on the page.
items.why_new: Gives $/Gb ratios; F767 gave only per-read discount percentages.
items.verify_note: The arithmetic checks out (4.35/2.75 = 1.58x; 4.38/3.23 = 1.36x). It sits within the known 1.03–1.60x US and Canadian core range (D042, D045). It rests on unverified snippet prices and below-spec reads per lane.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Taiwan's NHRI bought outsourced 30x genomes at about US$305 all-in in Oct 2024. After library prep and analysis, that leaves the Illumina-based vendor only about $1.0–2.0/Gb for reagents and margin, at or below the Open Offer top-tier net of $1.76/Gb.
items.detail: NT$1.47M / 150 = NT$9,800 per genome, or about US$305 at ~32 NT$/US$ (Oct 2024). Using TCAG's split (PCR-free prep ~US$100 and QC/analysis ~US$100–130; D043), about $75–205 remains for ~100 Gb, which is ~$0.75–2.0/Gb including the vendor's margin. That compares with ~$2.0/Gb list for the 25B-300, $1.76/Gb Open Offer top tier (D051) and $2.55/Gb Novogene lanes. Large Taiwanese service vendors therefore appear to buy X reagents at least near the best published net prices, which fits steep large-account discounts.
items.quote: 次世代全基因體定序150個
items.why_new: D070 used the NT$12,800 hospital price; the research award 23% lower squeezes the implied reagent price below the Open Offer top tier.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Outsourced WGS prices in Taiwan fell in one step from NT$24,000 (2023) to NT$9,800–12,800 (2024–25), then held flat at NT$12,800 across 2025–26 awards. That looks like a one-time NovaSeq X conversion step, not accelerating deflation.
items.detail: Taipei VGH paid NT$24,000 per WGS in the Jul 2023 contract and NT$12,800 in Feb 2025 (−47%; D068). NHRI paid NT$9,800 in Oct 2024. Kaohsiung VGH paid exactly NT$12,800 in Dec 2025 and Jan 2026 (F744), so there was no further decline over about 12 months. The same pattern shows up in Taipei VGH's flat NT$201,000 P4 price in 2025–26 (F713).
items.source_name: Taiwan e-Procurement (Taipei VGH, Kaohsiung VGH, NHRI)
items.why_new: Joins the 2023 price, the 2024 research price and the 2025–26 hospital prices into a time series showing a step and then a plateau.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: In Taiwanese research sequencing tenders, multi-bidder awards came in 19–28% below base price, while single-bidder awards with Illumina-only qualification clauses landed at 0–0.02% below base. Illumina spec clauses largely remove the research price fight.
items.detail: Multi-bidder awards: NHRI WGS NT$1.47M vs NT$1.82M base (−19%, 2 bidders, Oct 2024) and the Livestock Research Institute 2025 award NT$1,595,880 vs NT$2.22M base (−28%, 3 bidders). Single-bidder awards with Illumina clauses: Livestock Research Institute 2026 NT$2,499,500 vs NT$2.5M (−0.02%, requires an X Plus in Taiwan) and TMU WGS NT$3,057,600 = base (requires two or more Illumina high-throughput sequencers, re-tendered after failing). Research buyers get deep discounts only where vendors compete, and that competition is among Illumina-based vendors.
items.source_name: Taiwan e-Procurement (NHRI, Livestock Research Institute, TMU)
items.quote: 須具備二台(含)以上Illumina高通量次世代定序儀
items.why_new: Puts a number on the award-vs-base discount by bidder count and specification lock-in. That figure appears in no known item.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: On one price page, the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research (OICR) prices Ultima whole-genome sequencing about 63–65% below its Illumina whole-genome sequencing at every depth.
items.detail: OICR's research price page lists Illumina RUO FASTQ-only WGS at C$1,181 (30X), C$2,613 (80X) and C$3,794 (80X tumour/30X normal); these prices are valid as of May 2024. Its Ultima prices, valid as of May 2025, are C$435, C$920 and C$1,355 for the same services: −63%, −65% and −64%. The Illumina prices are a year older and may since have fallen, but OICR still lists them next to the Ultima prices. OICR is a cancer-genomics institute that also runs clinical work (the REVOLVE clinical panel and clinical tumour/normal WGS at C$4,266).
items.source_name: OICR Genomics, Clinical Reporting and Research Services price page
items.quote: valid as of May 2025
items.why_new: OICR is not in the corpus. It is the first core found that lists Illumina and Ultima WGS for the same services on one page.
items.verify_note: Checked on the OICR page. Illumina RUO FASTQ-only WGS prices are C$1,181 / 2,613 / 3,794 (30X / 80X / 80X tumour+30X normal), and plasma 30X is C$1,171 RUO / C$1,541 clinical, all 'valid as of May 2024'. Ultima WGS is C$435 / 920 / 1,355 with a 20-sample minimum for 30X and 80X, under a May 2025 header, for academic research use only. The −63% to −65% arithmetic is correct. Caveats: (1) the Illumina prices are a year older, probably reflect 6000-era or early-X costs, and have no sample minimum;

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Taichung VGH's outsourced NIPT contract more than doubled, from NT$9.5M (Oct 2023–Sep 2025) to NT$21.04M (Oct 2025–Oct 2027), and most of the new volume is in higher-priced expanded tiers.
items.detail: Award 112A-R07 (16 Oct 2023) was NT$9.5M for two years. Award 114Y-R11 (10 Nov 2025) was NT$21.04M for two years, so the annual run-rate went from about NT$4.75M to about NT$10.5M (+121%). The 2025 tender gives the estimated two-year volumes: 200 'simple' tests for NT$2.2M (NT$11,000 each, ~US$340), 440 'general' tests for NT$9.24M (NT$21,000, ~US$650) and 300 'plus/全方位' tests for NT$9.6M (NT$32,000, ~US$1,000). That is 940 tests in two years, or about 470 a year, and 79% of them are in the general or plus tiers. Expanded NIPT tiers usually sequence deeper per sample, so at this medical center NIPT looks like it is moving up-tier rather than maturing. There was one bidder (慧智基因) each time, and the 2025 award equalled the budget.
items.quote: non-invasive prental screening(plus)（全方位版）
items.why_new: The first NIPT tender series in the corpus. F744–F764 cover WGS and reagent tenders only.
items.verify_note: Checked. The award is NT$21,040,000, decided 23 Oct 2025 and published 10 Nov 2025, for 23 Oct 2025 to 22 Oct 2027. There was one bidder (慧智基因). Tier quantities and implied unit prices (200 at NT$11,000, 440 at NT$21,000, 300 at NT$32,000) match. The predecessor's NT$9.5M was not re-checked. Blended price is about NT$22,400 per test. In Gb terms the volume is trivial: ~470 tests a year at ~1–6 Gb each is under 3 Tb a year. This is test-mix evidence for one hospital, not material NIPT volume, so

items.label: 1C
items.claim: NTUH used up a NIPT contract meant to run to Dec 2026 in about two years, then awarded a new NT$9.32M lot for calendar 2026 alone, which implies its annual NIPT spend roughly doubled.
items.detail: TH120730 was awarded 17 Jan 2024 at NT$9,545,000, with a term from 18 Jan 2024 to 31 Dec 2026 (about NT$3.2M a year if spread over the full term). TH140450 was awarded 3 Nov 2025 at NT$9,324,500 for 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2026 only. If the first contract's ceiling ran out by the end of 2025, spend was about NT$4.8M a year in 2024–25 and is budgeted at about NT$9.3M in 2026 (~+95%). This is our inference from the overlapping terms, because the notices give no test counts. Both awards went to a single bidder, 台灣尖端先進生技醫藥, at 96–97% of budget.
items.quote: 第二代非侵入性產前染色體檢測一批
items.why_new: A new NTUH NIPT series. Earlier NTUH items in the corpus (F715, F752) are about WGS/WES reagents.
items.verify_note: Checked TH140450: NT$9,324,500, decided 3 Nov 2025, term 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2026, one bidder, budget NT$9,985,000. The first tender failed for lack of bidders. The notice does not mention TH120730 or say its ceiling ran out. The claimed doubling of annual spend is purely an inference from overlapping terms. The new contract could replace the old one for other reasons, such as a vendor or scope change. There are no test counts.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: NCKU Hospital's outsourced NIPT spend rose from about NT$1.49M a year (2023–24) to NT$2.79M a year (2025–27), and 71% of the new estimated tests are the 'advanced' tier.
items.detail: NCKU awards to Bionet (訊聯), all one year long unless noted, were: NT$2.28M (Apr 2020, 3 bidders), NT$0.999M (Apr 2022), NT$1.491M (Mar 2023), NT$1.494M (Mar 2024), a NT$0.93M bridge for 7–30 Jan 2025, and then NT$5.58M for Jan 2025–Jan 2027. The 2025 notice gives the estimate: 120 basic NIPT at NT$9,000 plus 300 advanced NIPT at NT$15,000, which is 420 tests over two years (~210 a year) at a blended ~NT$13,300 (~US$415). The run-rate is up ~87% on 2024 but is only ~22% above the 2020 level, so the series is volatile rather than steadily growing.
items.why_new: A new per-test NIPT price and volume series (2020–2027) at a southern medical center.
items.verify_note: Not re-fetched. The item itself says the series is volatile (the 2025–27 run-rate is only ~22% above 2020). About 210 tests a year is immaterial in Gb. It is useful only as more evidence of tier mix-up (71% advanced).

items.label: 1C
items.claim: At Taipei VGH's Taoyuan branch, the annualized outsourced NIPT spend roughly halved, from ~NT$1.82M a year (2020–21) to ~NT$0.93M a year (2023–26), even though the test menu widened from 15 to 26 items.
items.detail: TYVHD10905-1 (June 2020) was NT$2.8M for 18 Jun 2020 to 31 Dec 2021 (~18.5 months). TYD11211-11 (Dec 2023) was the same NT$2.8M, but for 27 Dec 2023 to 31 Dec 2026 (36 months), a −49% annual run-rate. Both went to one bidder (慧智基因). The 2020 notice lists the country of origin as Germany. At this community-level hospital, prenatal NGS self-pay testing is shrinking, consistent with NIPT saturation and Taiwan's falling births.
items.quote: 非侵入性產前染色體基因檢測第26項委外代檢
items.why_new: First dated evidence of NIPT outsourcing spend shrinking at a public hospital.
items.verify_note: Not re-fetched. The award is a ceiling amount, so a flat NT$2.8M spread over a longer term may reflect under-drawn ceilings rather than lower actual use. The 'country of origin Germany' detail is irrelevant. It is consistent with falling Taiwanese births, but the scale is tiny.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Taipei City Hospital's NIPT outsourcing ran at about NT$3.4M a year in Sep 2024–Dec 2025, about 20% below its 2023 one-year contract of NT$4.23M, and it needed a bridge and a follow-on extension.
items.detail: R111133 was NT$4.23M for 3 Jan 2023 to 2 Jan 2024 (one bidder). R113118 (Sep–Oct 2024) awarded three NIPS tiers totalling NT$4.266M (950K + 1.65M + 1.666M), with a term to 30 Jun 2027. A NT$159.5K bridge (R114133E, 10 Dec 2025 to 8 Jan 2026) shows that ceiling was used up after ~15 months, or ~NT$3.4M a year. A NT$2.295M follow-on (R113118-1, Feb 2026, under procurement-law Art. 22(1)(7)) then runs from Apr 2026 to Jun 2029, which is only ~NT$0.7M a year if spread evenly. The winner each time was 華聯生物科技.
items.why_new: A new municipal-hospital NIPT spend series. The run-rate is our derivation from contract terms.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Per Gb, OICR's Ultima wafer costs about 3.5–4.3x less than its NovaSeq X 10B lane. Per read the gap is about 2.1x.
items.detail: Both prices are valid as of May 2025. The X 10B 300-cycle lane (sequencing only) is C$2,734. At ~1.25B read pairs (~375 Gb, the 10B spec used by UMGC) that is ~C$7.29/Gb and ~C$1.09 per million reads. The Ultima wafer is C$5,130 (2-wafer minimum) for ~10B reads. At ~250–300 bp that is ~2.5–3.0 Tb, so ~C$1.71–2.05/Gb and ~C$0.51 per million reads. Calculation: 7.29/2.05 = 3.6x and 7.29/1.71 = 4.3x per Gb; 1.09/0.51 = 2.1x per read. OICR also calls itself Canada's first certified Ultima service provider.
items.source_name: OICR Genomics Ultima Sequencing page plus price page
items.quote: first Canadian Certified Ultima Service Provider
items.why_new: This is a new Ultima-vs-X lane comparison from one institution. The corpus Ultima comparisons are UMGC and Broad Clinical Labs.
items.verify_note: Prices checked: X 10B-300 lane at C$2,734 and Ultima wafer at C$5,130 (10B reads, 2-wafer minimum), both May 2025. The arithmetic is right, but the comparator is OICR's 10B lane, which carries the known 10B premium of about 1.4–1.6x over the 25B. Against a Canadian 25B lane (TCAG C$3.47/Gb) the Ultima per-Gb gap is only ~1.7–2.0x (see derived item). Ultima-vs-X lane comparisons at UMGC and Broad are already known. The new part is OICR as a certified Ultima provider.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: In the only contested NIPT award found in 2024–26, the winning outsourcer underbid its rival by 30% on the basic tier and 18% on the mid tier.
items.detail: In Taipei City Hospital tender R113118 (award 10 Sep 2024), 華聯生物科技 won NIPS1 at NT$950,000 against 台灣基康 at NT$1,350,000 (−30%), and NIPS2 at NT$1,650,000 against NT$2,000,000 (−18%). The hospital's floor price for the case was NT$2.6M against a budget of NT$4.59M. When a second bidder shows up, NIPT service prices fall sharply, which squeezes the lab's per-test reagent budget.
items.quote: 資格、規格合於招標文件規定，但非最低標
items.why_new: First bid-level NIPT price competition data in the corpus.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Taiwan's public-hospital NIPT outsourcing has lost competition: 8 of 9 awards in 2022–26 had a single bidder and landed at 95–100% of budget, against 3 bidders at NCKU in 2020.
items.detail: Single-bidder awards include NCKU 2022/23/24/25, Taichung VGH 2023 and 2025, NTUH 2024 and 2025, Taipei VGH 2025, NYCU 2024 (NT$3.708M vs NT$3.744M budget), Taoyuan VGH 2023 and Fengyuan MOHW 2022. Many followed failed first tenders (流標). Four local labs (訊聯 Bionet, 華聯, 慧智基因, 台灣尖端先進) split the market. In 2020 NCKU drew three bids (NT$2.28M, 2.56M and 2.796M). With weak buyer-side price pressure, NIPT providers here are not being forced to squeeze reagent suppliers.
items.quote: 本案係以廠商原始報價(未優惠)為預算
items.why_new: Covers the NIPT market structure. F763/F764 cover instruments and WGS only.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Taipei VGH's new three-year NIPT contract is NT$6.17M (~NT$2.06M a year), and two-thirds of the value is the 'advanced' tier.
items.detail: X11409E (awarded 3 Sep 2025, term Nov 2025 to Nov 2028) has 'classic' NIPT at NT$1.998M and 'advanced' at NT$4.176M (68% of value). It had one bidder (台灣尖端先進) and came in 2.6% below the NT$6.336M budget, after a failed first round. The notice tags item 1's origin as the USA, which may point to US-made test kits, but no platform is named. This is another case of medical-center NIPT value tilting to expanded tiers.
items.quote: 第二代非侵入性產前染色體檢查(進階款)
items.why_new: A new Taipei VGH NIPT award. Earlier Taipei VGH items cover WGS and reagent sets.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Smaller MOHW regional hospitals show NIPT outsourcing stalling: Fengyuan's last award was NT$983K for two years (2022–24) with no successor found, Nantou's 2020 tender failed three times, and Chiayi has only a 2025 quotation notice.
items.detail: Fengyuan Hospital FYH1110701 was an open contract of NT$983,000 for 18 Jan 2022 to 17 Jan 2024 (~NT$0.49M a year, one bidder: Bionet). The title search shows no later Fengyuan NIPT award. Nantou Hospital's '110NIPT' basic tender failed in Sep, Oct and Nov 2020. Chiayi Hospital (CHYI1142722) posted quotation notices in Jul 2025 with no award visible. Volume at this tier is tiny and not growing.
items.quote: 本案為開口契約，採購金額達契約金額即契約終止
items.why_new: New regional-hospital NIPT tenders, not previously in the corpus.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Across the four medical centers with comparable series (NTUH, Taichung VGH, NCKU, Taipei VGH), annualized NIPT outsourcing spend rose from ~NT$11–13M (2023–24) to ~NT$24.7M (2025–26), while two lower-tier hospitals shrank.
items.detail: Our sum of annualized run-rates is NTUH ~4.8→9.3M, Taichung VGH 4.75→10.52M and NCKU 1.49→2.79M. Taipei VGH's predecessor contract was not found, so its 2.06M a year is added only to the latest figure. Taoyuan VGH (1.82→0.93M) and Taipei City Hospital (4.23→~3.4M) fell. Spend is consolidating at flagship centers and shifting to expanded-panel tiers (11,000–32,000 NT$ per test). This is spend, not Gb. Expanded tiers likely raise Gb per test, which cuts against the idea that NIPT maturity drags on Gb.
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (via pcc-api.openfun.app), our aggregation
items.why_new: First cross-hospital NIPT spend aggregation. Prior NIPT evidence is US-only (expert, ACMG, Myriad, Medicare).
items.verify_note: This aggregates F779–F782 and is not independent evidence. The NTUH leg depends on F780's unverified inference. It measures spend, not Gb, and possible public NIPT subsidy changes in Taiwan were not controlled for. The combined volume is a few thousand tests a year, which is immaterial to Illumina's Gb (see derived item).

items.label: 1C
items.claim: OICR sells Ultima ppm-Seq cell-free WGS (an MRD-style method) at about a quarter of its Illumina plasma-WGS price per unit of raw depth, so new liquid-biopsy depth may land off Illumina.
items.detail: Illumina 30X plasma WGS is C$1,171 RUO and C$1,541 clinical (May 2024 prices). Ultima ppm-Seq cfWGS at 100X raw (30X ppm-Seq) is C$999 and at 200X raw is C$1,999, with a 6-sample minimum (May 2025). Per raw X: Illumina 1,171/30 = C$39; Ultima 999/100 = C$10, which is −74%. Deep cell-free genome work, the Gb-heavy MRD design the bull case relies on, is being priced on Ultima at a research cancer institute.
items.quote: Ultima ppm-Seq cfWGS 100X Raw (30X ppm-Seq)
items.why_new: The corpus has no public price for Ultima ppm-Seq cfWGS and no side-by-side with Illumina plasma WGS.
items.verify_note: Prices checked: Illumina plasma WGS 30X at C$1,171 RUO / C$1,541 clinical (May 2024), and Ultima ppm-Seq cfWGS at C$460 (30X raw), C$999 (100X raw) and C$1,999 (200X raw), 6-sample minimum, research only. Per raw X, Ultima is about C$10–15 vs C$39 for Illumina. The dates differ, and ppm-Seq is a different chemistry, so raw-X parity is approximate. It is research pricing at one institute, with no evidence of clinical MRD volume moving. It fits 1B or 2B as well as 1C.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: At UNMC, AVITI24 costs roughly 30–50% less per Gb than the core's own NovaSeq 6000 flow cells.
items.detail: UNMC internal prices: 6000 S4 200-cycle $19,905 (~1.6–2.0 Tb at spec ≈ $10–12.4/Gb); S2 300-cycle $14,785 (~1.0–1.25 Tb ≈ $11.8–14.8/Gb). AVITI24 2x150 High Output is $2,601 (~300–450 Gb ≈ $5.8–8.7/Gb). Yields are spec-based estimates, because the page gives no output. External rates carry a flat ~50% uplift (S4 $29,858; AVITI High $3,902).
items.source_name: University of Nebraska Medical Center Genomics Core pricing
items.why_new: This UNMC rate card is new (F365 covered only Nebraska subsidy cuts). It is a direct 6000-vs-AVITI comparison at one core.
items.verify_note: Prices checked: S4-200 is $19,905 internal / $29,858 external; S2-300 is $14,785 / $22,178; AVITI24 2x150 High Output is $2,601 / $3,902. The page gives no outputs, so the per-Gb figures depend on spec-based yield assumptions. The comparator is the 6000, not the X, so this says little about Illumina's current price gap. At a 25B rate of ~$2.5–3.5/Gb, the X would undercut this AVITI price.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: In 2025 the MIT BioMicroCenter still ran its in-house high-throughput work on the 6000, at about $9/Gb on an S4 lane, while stocking small 6000 flow cells only minimally.
items.detail: MIT price page (edited 15 Apr 2025), core-lab rates: S4 300nt lane $5,400 for 2B reads (~600 Gb ≈ $9.0/Gb), $7,560 for non-MIT users. AVITI 150PE full flow cell is $2,650 for ~800M reads (~240 Gb ≈ $11.0/Gb), so AVITI was not cheaper per Gb. SP 300nt, S1 and S2 kits are marked 'minimal inventory maintained'. The X is outsourced to a sister resource. This is a research 6000 tail at a top-tier university still selling 6000 data well above X prices.
items.quote: minimal inventory maintained
items.why_new: MIT is not in the corpus. It adds a dated research 6000-tail price point.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: UC San Diego's IGM core lists only Illumina sequencing, with no rival platform. Its outside users pay 37% more than UC users.
items.detail: IGM rates (PDF created 14 Oct 2025): 25B-300 lane $2,800 UC / $3,836 outside; 10B-300 lane $1,700 / $2,329; 1.5B-300 flow cell $3,200 / $4,384. Per Gb at ~1,000 vs ~375 Gb per lane, the 10B costs 1.62x the 25B ($4.53 vs $2.80). The sheet lists no AVITI, Ultima or AXELIOS. A large UC research core is all-Illumina at roughly $2.8/Gb.
items.source_name: UCSD Institute for Genomic Medicine rates
items.quote: Some rates pending committee approval.
items.why_new: UCSD IGM is not in the corpus.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: UMGC prices its AVITI 30x genome at about twice its Ultima genome, which shows a two-tier rival price structure below Illumina.
items.detail: UMGC per-sample human WGS, all-in including PCR-free library prep and analysis (undated live page): Ultima UG 100 30x $192 UMN / $221 external (24-sample batch); Element AVITI 30x $407 / $469 (4-sample batch); AVITI UltraQ $1,015 / $1,168. UMGC lists no NovaSeq X genome price. The corpus has the Ultima $221; the AVITI genome price and the 2.1x ratio are new.
items.quote: Offering the $221 human genome
items.why_new: The AVITI genome price at UMGC was not recorded. F409 gave only Ultima tiers.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: University of Iowa's microbiome core discontinued its Illumina MiSeq after 1 Feb 2026 and moved amplicon sequencing to AVITI24 at up to ~31% lower per-sample prices.
items.detail: On the core's 2026 price list, AVITI24 library prep plus sequencing is $45 / $35 / $28 / $24 per sample internal across batch sizes up to 380 samples. MiSeq was $46 / $40 / $35 for up to 140 samples. Largest batch: $24 vs $35 = −31%. The page says MiSeq 'will be discontinue after Feb 1st 2026', and the core chose AVITI rather than Illumina's MiSeq i100 replacement.
items.quote: Illumina MiSeq will be discontinue after Feb 1st 2026
items.why_new: This is a new, dated example of low-throughput research volume leaving Illumina when the MiSeq was retired.
items.verify_note: Checked. The page says 'Illumina MiSeq will be discontinue after Feb 1st 2026'. AVITI24 internal prices are $45 / $35 / $28 / $24 per sample (batches up to 380) and MiSeq internal prices are $46 / $40 / $35 (up to 140). The −31% figure compares the largest batch of each, which are different batch sizes. Like-for-like small batches are about flat ($45 vs $46). Treat this as a platform loss in low-throughput research amplicon work, not a large price gap.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: University of Michigan's Advanced Genomics Core says it is among the first academic Ultima UG 100 certified service providers, promising much cheaper sequencing to internal and external users.
items.detail: Search snippet only; the page returned 403. The AGC director says that as a certified provider the core will 'soon be able to offer significantly lower-cost sequencing'. Michigan's NGS page lists 10–12B reads per wafer, up to 3.6 Tb, and wafer sharing for 10x Flex libraries. This makes a third large Midwest academic core (with UMGC and Cornell) building Ultima capacity aimed at single-cell work.
items.source_name: University of Michigan Medical School Office of Research (search snippet)
items.quote: significantly lower-cost sequencing for both internal and external investigators
items.why_new: Michigan's Ultima install is not in the corpus. Seen in a search snippet only.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: French cfDNA NIPT volume was about 130K tests in 2022, about 20% of ~650K births, which suggests a mature, guideline-capped market.
items.detail: Le Quotidien du Médecin reported nearly 130,000 ADNflc exams in France in 2022, up from 21,161 in 2016 (known point). The HAS 2018 strategy offers the test only to women with a first-trimester risk of 1/1000-1/51, which caps eligibility. Only one year is confirmed, so the post-2022 trend and any flattening between guideline changes are untested. Search snippet only; I did not open the article.
items.source_name: Le Quotidien du Médecin (citing HAS / Agence de la biomédecine)
items.quote: près de 130 000 examens par ADNflc ont été réalisés en 2022
items.why_new: Gives a French 2022 national NIPT count, and no French NIPT series is in the known list.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: NCSU GSL now offers outsourced NovaSeq X sequencing with a $149 GSL processing fee, effective 24 Apr 2026.
items.detail: The page states the new service rates take effect 24 Apr 2026 and that outsourced NovaSeq X sequencing adds a $149 fee for GSL processing. Lane prices are not public, and the internal-rate sheet needs a Unity ID. Cornell's BRC similarly says it contracts external sequencing at low rates and no longer loads NovaSeq in-house (search snippet; date unseen). Two university cores moving X work to outside providers fits the research-customer price-sensitivity thesis, but neither source gives a price or an Illumina discount.
items.source_name: NCSU Genomic Sciences Lab pricing page
items.why_new: NCSU and Cornell outsourcing are not in the known core-facility list.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: NHRI, Taiwan's main public research institute and a NovaSeq 6000-only account, cut its S4 kit buying from 57 kits in 2020 to 16 in 2023 and then stopped. Its spend fell about 90% even though the price per kit fell about two-thirds.
items.detail: All of these awards are for NovaSeq 6000 S4 300-cycle kits bought straight from Illumina. Jul 2020: 32 kits for NT$17,337,600, priced in USD at 30.1, which is US$576K or US$18,000 per kit (09GD-0001, Illumina Inc Singapore). Dec 2020: 25 v1.5 kits for NT$10,797,000 at 29.5, which is US$14,640 per kit (09GD-0002). Dec 2023: 16 v1.5 kits for NT$2,929,920, or NT$183,120 per kit (about US$5,900 at ~31.1), sold by Illumina's Taiwan subsidiary 因美納台灣生物科技 (112A0C0676). Kit volume fell 72% (57→16) and spend fell 89.6% (NT$28.1M→NT$2.9M). No NovaSeq kit award appears for NHRI in 2024–26. The title search also shows no S4 buy in 2021–22, though NHRI did buy 'library and sequencing reagents' from Illumina in Jun 2022.
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (PCC) via g0v/openfun API
items.quote: NovaSeq 6000 S4 試劑組(300 循環) 32組
items.why_new: F712/D067 cover the Dec 2020 vs Dec 2023 per-kit fall only. The Jul 2020 US$18,000 point, the kit-volume series (57→16→0) and the −90% spend are new.
items.verify_note: Restates the known F712 and D067 (same tenders 09GD-0001, 09GD-0002 and 112A0C0676; per-kit price cut and 'far fewer kits'). The Dec 2023 award is confirmed at 16 S4 v1.5 kits for NT$2,929,920 from Illumina Taiwan. The unit price is derived, not published. The only new detail is the 57→16 kit count and that no award was found after 2023, and that rests on a title search.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: NHRI kept a four-unit NovaSeq 6000 fleet under a near-flat Illumina service contract for five years (about US$110K per unit per year). The award history shows no renewal after the contract ended on 13 Dec 2024.
items.detail: Restricted, single-bid awards to Illumina distributor 均泰生物科技 for 'NovaSeq 6000 定序系統 4台維護1年': NT$14.2M (term Dec 2019–Dec 2020), NT$14.0M (2020–21), NT$13.8M (2021–22), NT$13.8M (2022–23) and NT$13.8M (14 Dec 2023–13 Dec 2024). That is NT$3.45M per unit per year, about US$110K, and only −2.8% over four years. No later NovaSeq-titled service award exists for NHRI. This fits a research 6000 fleet being retired or taken off contract in late 2024, at the same time NHRI moved WGS to outsourcing (Oct 2024).
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (PCC) via g0v/openfun API
items.quote: Illumina NovaSeq 6000定序系統組4台維護1年
items.why_new: The five-year service-price series for a named four-unit 6000 fleet and its non-renewal date are new. F718 noted only that the NovaSeq tenders stopped.
items.verify_note: Checked the 2023–24 award: NT$13.8M, restricted tender, one bidder (均泰), term 14 Dec 2023 to 13 Dec 2024. The title says 4 units, but the quantity field reads 1. 'No renewal' rests on a title search, and a renamed tender could be missed. This is a research 6000 fleet, and research is already ~92% converted, so it says little about the clinical tail. The new and useful part is the ~US$110K per unit per year service price.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Taipei VGH's renewal of its two-year Illumina 'high-throughput sequencing reagent set' lot fell 41% in value, from NT$6.67M (Dec 2023) to NT$3.94M (Nov 2025). The distributor gave up a bigger cut to win it.
items.detail: 1120652Y item 1 had a 14 Dec 2023–13 Dec 2025 term, an estimated 29 sets, and was awarded at NT$6,670,000 after an original bid of NT$7,250,000 (−8%). The direct successor, 1140732E item 1, starts 15 Dec 2025 and runs to 31 Dec 2027. 均泰 bid the full NT$4,635,000 budget and was cut to the NT$3,942,000 floor (−15%). If the per-set price stayed near NT$230K (F717), contracted volume falls from ~29 to ~17 sets. Otherwise the per-set price fell sharply. items.claim: UC campus internal 25B prices differ by about 9%. UCSD IGM's 2025 sheet shows $2,800 and CAT now shows $2,551, so the aggregated account has the lowest price.
items.detail: A search snippet of UCSD IGM's 2025 rate PDF shows the 25B-300 lane at $2,800 for UC users and $3,836 for outside users. Against CAT's $2,551 that is -8.9% (-$249). Berkeley's $2,600 sits between the two. The price per Gb is about $2.92 at CAT and $2.97 at Berkeley on the stated 875 Gb of output. UCLA's external 25B-300 is $3,512 (1 Jul 2026). Intra-system price dispersion of this size, plus a UC-wide contract, makes consolidation onto the lowest-cost core likely.
items.source_name: UCSD IGM 2025 rates (search snippet, not opened); UCSF CAT
items.why_new: UCSD IGM appears in the known list only as 'lists only Illumina'. A UC internal price comparison across campuses is new.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: CAT's external premium over its UC rate grew from about 26% to 33% for non-profits while the internal price fell, and Berkeley charges external users only 15% more.
items.detail: The old CAT page shows external non-profit 25B-300 at $3,591 against $2,850 internal, a 26% premium. The current page states a flat 33% non-profit and 46.3% for-profit multiplier on UC rates, which gives about $3,394 and $3,732 for the 25B-300. That is about 5% below the old external price. Berkeley's external 25B is $2,990 against $2,600 internal, +15%. Many research buyers face a lower external price even when the headline premium widens, and Berkeley's narrow gap shows aggregation compressing the subsidy. The derived CAT external prices are my arithmetic, not published figures.
items.why_new: Known items cover internal/external gaps at Fred Hutch (76%), Harvard (40%), NCI (2x) and Oregon (36%). UC's gaps and their direction are new.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: The X 1.5B flow cell at CAT is priced much higher now than on the older page (+28% at 300 cycles, +46% at 100 cycles). The deflation is concentrated in the large flow cells.
items.detail: The older page shows 1.5B (2 lanes) at $1,824 / $2,357 / $2,582 for 100/200/300 cycles. The current page shows $2,665 / $2,906 / $3,302, which is +46% / +23% / +28%. The unit basis may have changed, since the older page's wording on per-lane versus per-flow-cell is ambiguous, so treat this with caution. If the basis is the same, the 25B/1.5B price ratio widened. That matches known Harvard Bauer FY27 increases on small cells (1.5B +25.5%). Smaller buyers are not seeing discounts, which fits the 'tiered' structure rather than across-the-board erosion.
items.source_name: UCSF CAT rate pages (old vs current)
items.why_new: Quantifies the 1.5B move at CAT. It adds an 'against' data point not in the known Bauer 1.5B +25.5% item.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Caris, an Illumina Open Offer customer, still describes its Arizona labs as running both NovaSeq 6000 and NovaSeq X as of its FY25 10-K (filed Mar 2026).
items.detail: Under 'Our Laboratory Infrastructure', the Caris FY25 10-K (filed 2026-03-03) says its labs use NovaSeq 6000 and NovaSeq X sequencing systems. It gives no migration timeline, no fleet counts and no cost-per-test saving. It is the only filing in the EDGAR full-text hits for 'NovaSeq 6000' from Jan 2025 to Oct 2026. That means no other named clinical lab disclosed a 6000 fleet in SEC filings in the period. This is consistent with a long parallel-running tail at a large clinical account that is on the Open Offer (price-protected) contract, although it quantifies nothing. The statement was read from a fetched copy of the filing and is paraphrased.
items.source_name: SEC EDGAR, Caris Life Sciences FY25 10-K
items.quote: NovaSeq 6000 and NovaSeq X sequencing systems
items.why_new: The known list had only Caris's 'over 50 NovaSeqs' (Mar 2025) and its Open Offer terms. This is the first named dual-platform (6000 plus X) statement in a 2026 filing.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: An Italian paediatric clinical hospital (OPBG, Rome) was still buying NovaSeq 6000 v1.5 kits in Jan 2026, at near-list prices of about 7.5-9.4 EUR/Gb on the S4.
items.detail: The OPBG annex (CUP B53C22006140001, posted 26 Jan 2026) lists NovaSeq 6000 v1.5 kits only, with no NovaSeq X or 25B lines. Unit prices (currency presumably EUR, not printed) are S1 200-cycle 5,566 (qty 2), S2 200-cycle 10,325 (qty 4), S4 200-cycle 15,067 (qty 4) and S2 100-cycle 8,691 (qty 2). That totals about 130K for 12 kits. On approximate spec output the price per Gb is about 16.7-20.9 (S1), 12.4-15.5 (S2) and 7.5-9.4 (S4), against about 2.0 EUR/Gb for the IDIBAPS 25B tender. This is a 3-4x gap, and it is the high-price, low-volume cohort the thesis says sits in the 41% of consumables revenue.

items.why_new: This is the first ex-US clinical hospital order for 6000 kits with explicit unit prices in Jan 2026; the known list has only US cores, tenders for X flow cells and Salk list prices.

It lists only NovaSeq 6000 v1.5 kits (S1-200 5,566 ×2; S2-200 10,325 ×4; S4-200 15,067 ×4; S2-100 8,691 ×2), with no X or 25B lines, plus Stranded Total RNA, RNA UD indexes, MethylationEPIC v2 and an FFPE restore kit. The 6000 kits total 130,082. No currency is printed. The prices are filled in for distributors to quote against ('RIFARSI FARE OFFERTA PER LE QUANTITA''; suppliers QUINTA/MASTRO), so they are reference prices, not awarded net prices. The CUP is a 2022 public-

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The OPBG order is too small to quantify a committed multi-year 6000 tail, which limits how much it supports 1A.
items.detail: The annex shows 2-4 kits per line, about 12 sequencing kits and roughly 130K in total. It states no multi-year term, minimum commitment or cycle count beyond the line items. The 'QUINTA' labels may mean a one-fifth extension (unverified). This looks like a small lab buying at near-list prices, and it shows nothing about how large clinical labs are converting.
items.source_name: Ospedale Pediatrico Bambino Gesù, tender annex
items.why_new: It quantifies how small this clinical 6000 purchase is, so the analyst does not over-read it as evidence of a large committed tail.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: In GEO, the NovaSeq 6000's share of plant and livestock series fell 96.7% to 81.5% to 72.3% (Q3'24, Q3'25, Q3'26). That is nearly the same decay as the human series, so the tail is not decaying evenly toward zero and is not special to non-human users.
items.detail: I counted series (gse) on 26 NovaSeq 6000 platform records and 23 NovaSeq X platform records for Zea mays, Arabidopsis, Oryza, Glycine, Bos, Sus and Gallus. Series counts (6000/X): Q3'24 89/3; Q3'25 123/28; Q3'26 107/41. The 6000 share is 89/92=96.7%, 123/151=81.5% and 107/148=72.3%. That is −24.4 pts over 8 quarters (−3.0 pts/qtr). Over the last year it is −9.2 pts, against −12.1 pts for the human series already known (81.6%→69.5%). In ag the X is converting slower than in human, but the 6000 is not entrenched in non-human research.
items.why_new: The known GEO cuts are human, mouse, rat and institutions. This is the first plants/livestock split of 6000 versus X series.
items.verify_note: The samples are small (~90–150 series a quarter across 7 ag/livestock species), the data are non-human research, and they do not bear on the clinical 6000 tail that 1A is about. D052 already shows GEO lags Illumina's reported X share by about two years. The claim as worded is also internally muddled.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: A hospital's 6000-only annual kit order would lose roughly half or more of its Illumina revenue if it moved to X 25B pricing, so the tail's remaining dollars are exposed to any conversion.
items.detail: The annex prices an indicative annual order of 2 S1-200 (EUR 5,566 each), 4 S2-200 (10,325), 4 S4-200 (15,067) and 2 S2-100 (8,691). That is 12 NovaSeq 6000 flow cells and EUR 130,082 (11,132+41,300+60,268+17,382). By Illumina's spec as I recall it (not re-verified here: S1 1.3–1.6B, S2 3.3–4.1B, S4 8–10B reads), that is about 54–68B clusters a year, or EUR 1.9–2.4 per million. The already-known 25B price of $0.68–0.97 per million clusters would price the same volume at about $37–66K. That is a 50–75% revenue cut if EUR≈USD or EUR=1.15 USD. The currency is not printed on the annex; EUR is presumed. This is one small account, not a company-wide estimate.
items.source_name: Ospedale Pediatrico Bambino Gesù (Rome), Allegato 1, CUP B53C22006140001
items.why_new: The known list gives only OPBG's S4 per-Gb range (F826). This adds the full four-kit price ladder, annual quantities and the account-level cost of converting to X.
items.verify_note: Not new. F826 (already verified) covers the same OPBG annex and its near-list 6000 prices. Applying the known ~60–75% X price gap to one account's kit order is a restatement of the known 3.4x ratio. Two more problems. First, the per-cluster comparison sets 200-cycle S kits against a 25B price that is mostly for 300-cycle kits. Second, an account this small would probably never buy an X (see F830), so the 'exposed dollars' framing does not hold. The arithmetic itself checks out: EUR 130,082 for 1

items.label: 1A
items.claim: A low-volume hospital 6000 owner has little reason to convert, since its whole annual volume fits in about two X 25B flow cells, so part of the tail may never move.
items.detail: The annex spend on 6000 kits is EUR 130K a year. That is about 19–22% of the derived company-wide 6000 pull-through of $670–700K per instrument (EUR≈USD to EUR=1.15 USD). The 54–68B clusters a year is roughly two 25B-class flow cells. Conversion would need an X Plus (about $1M, my assumption). The infungibility report of 6 May 2025 says the NovaSeq 6000 is 'already present' and that RNA workflows run on NextSeq 500/550 plus the 6000. This matches Thaysen's 'low-volume never-convert' cohort. It cuts against the thesis that the remaining 6000 volume converts on a roughly five-point-a-year path.
items.source_name: OPBG, Relazione di infungibilità prodotti Illumina Italy Srl (PNC project)
items.quote: infungibili perché destinati esclusivamente all'utilizzo su piattaforma NovaSeq6000 già presente in OPBG
items.why_new: The known list has the cohort-1 label but no account-level pull-through ratio from a procurement record.
items.verify_note: The arithmetic checks out. EUR 130K a year (~$140–150K) is ~20–22% of the derived $670–700K pull-through, and the volume is about 2–2.6 25B flow cells' worth of clusters. This is a concrete instance of Thaysen's known 'low-volume never-convert' cohort, which management already builds into its 15–20% clinical tail, so it adds an example rather than a new mechanism. The X Plus price of ~$1M is the finder's assumption. One site.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The 6000 price ladder is steep inside the platform: per-cluster cost on the S4 is about 55% below the S1, so tail customers on small flow cells are the highest-price volume.
items.detail: Using the spec read counts above, per million clusters: S1-200 EUR 3.5–4.3, S2-200 EUR 2.5–3.1, S2-100 EUR 2.1–2.6 and S4-200 EUR 1.5–1.9. S4 at the midpoint (1.70) against S1 at the midpoint (3.88) is a 56% drop. Against the UBS 25B figure of $0.68 per million clusters, S4 is about 2.2–2.8x. That matches the 2.45–2.82x Open Offer-based gap (F539) and falls below the roughly 3.4x revenue-per-Gb ratio. Small-flow-cell tail users therefore pay far above X rates per Gb, which supports the thesis that tail volume carries disproportionate revenue.
items.source_name: OPBG Allegato 1 (page 3, unit prices); my derivation
items.why_new: This is a new full-ladder per-cluster derivation. Prior items cover only the S4 and the Open Offer gap.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: A hospital buyer's annual sequencing quantities are explicitly non-binding, so any Illumina volume at this kind of account carries no committed floor.
items.detail: The capitolato (signed 27 Nov 2025) calls the quantities the 'presumed annual need', 'indicative and non-binding'. Illumina Italy must supply only what individual purchase orders request. The same wording appears in all five OPBG capitolati read (2024–2026). It sits alongside the known 90-day exits and no-minimum clauses at large US accounts. It shows that low-commitment contracts are the norm at the small end too. Volume can drop without penalty if research grants run out.
items.source_name: OPBG, Capitolato tecnico (Illumina consumables, CUP B53C22006140001)
items.quote: sono indicativi e non impegnativi
items.why_new: The known list covers commitments at large US customers only; this adds the public hospital contract form.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: OPBG's Illumina research purchases are funded entirely by time-limited grants, which makes 2027 research demand at Italian hospital units exposed to the end of the EU recovery-fund programme.
items.detail: The five OPBG capitolati read (Oct 2024–Jun 2026) all cite grant CUP codes: the PNC fund (DD 931 of 6 Jun 2022, CUP B53C22006140001) and PNRR M6C2 I2.1 (CUPs E83C22006360001, E83C24000770006 and E83C24000800006). None cites ordinary budget. A search snippet says the Commission's last PNRR payment request evaluation ends 30 Nov 2026, with the last instalment by 31 Dec 2026. Project-specific end dates were not verified. Reagent buying may be pulled forward into the funded window, with a cliff after.
items.source_name: OPBG capitolati; PNRR timeline from search snippet
items.why_new: The known list covers US/UK/Canada funding but not Italian PNRR/PNC grant dependence of research consumables.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: One OPBG research unit moved from NextSeq 500/550 kits to NextSeq 2000 kits within about 12 months, so mid-throughput legacy conversion continues at hospitals.
items.detail: Under CUP E83C24000800006 (Predictive Molecular Pathology unit), the capitolato signed 14 Mar 2025 buys NextSeq 500/550 Mid Output v2.5 (300 cycles) and High Output v2.5 (150 cycles) kits. The one signed 25 Mar 2026 buys NextSeq 1000/2000 P2 XLEAP-SBS 200 and 300 cycle kits. A separate unit (CUP E83C24000770006, signed 26 Mar 2025) still bought NextSeq 500/550 High Output v2.5 plus MiSeq kits. The XLEAP cut of 20–36% per read (F548) therefore reaches installed bases only as units convert. Prices were not in these two documents.
items.why_new: The known list has no hospital-level dated NextSeq 500/550-to-2000 migration.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Illumina's winning offers on small sole-source hospital buys land well below the hospital's own ceiling, which shows some concession even without competition.
items.detail: A search snippet of an OPBG technical-congruity act (CUP E83C24000770006, Aug 2025) records an Illumina Italy offer of EUR 24,544.50 against a ceiling of EUR 28,368.00. That is 13.5% below the ceiling (1−24,544.5/28,368). I did not open that document, so this is snippet-level. It fits budgets set above the final price (F714), not true price deflation.
items.source_name: OPBG, atto di congruità tecnica (search-result snippet)
items.why_new: The known list has Taiwan and Spain budget-versus-award gaps but no Italian hospital example.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Sequencing is only about half of a hospital research unit's Illumina bill, which fits the view that cost is not the only constraint on volume.
items.detail: The annex total is EUR 247,940: 6000 kits EUR 130,082 (52.5%), RNA total prep EUR 28,879 (4×7,219.80), RNA indexes EUR 1,422, MethylationEPIC arrays EUR 70,168 (10×7,016.82) and FFPE restore EUR 17,389. Arrays and library prep make up 47.5%. The line labels 'QUINTA' (160,383) and 'MASTRO' (87,557) are unexplained and probably are unit leads' surnames (my guess). Array-based epigenetics does not scale with sequencing Gb. This supports the idea that research budgets spread across prep and arrays, and does not show sequencing volume driving spend.
items.why_new: The known list has workflow-cost shares from experts but no actual procurement bill split.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: In Taipei VGH's single-bidder hereditary-disease sequencing channel, the contracted clinical Gb run-rate rose about 60% between contract generations, while annual spend fell about 16%, because genome volume doubled at a flat price.
items.detail: Prior contracts (X11220H, Feb 2024–Feb 2026; X11310H, Jul 2024–Jul 2026) ran per year about 78 WGS at NT$14,260, 144 WES+MT at NT$11,500 and 144 WES at NT$10,000. That is ~NT$4.21M/yr and ~10.7 Tb/yr at ~100 Gb per genome and ~10 Gb per exome. The successor (X11411V, from Nov 2025/Mar 2026 to Oct 2027) annualizes to 156 WGS at NT$14,260 and 144 WES+MT at NT$9,000. That is ~NT$3.52M/yr and ~17.0 Tb/yr: Gb +60%, spend −16%, and spend per Gb about −47%, driven mostly by the genome-for-exome mix. Caveat: the WES-only line may have moved to the separate Genomics BioSci contract (X11326H), so channel-level Gb growth may overstate the hospital-level change.
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (g0v mirror), Taipei VGH
items.quote: WGS全基因體遺傳性疾病基因定序 … 312 … 14,260
items.why_new: D068 covers only the Genomics BioSci channel. This is the second (台基盟) channel, with corrected annualized terms.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: UCSF CAT's internal 25B-300 lane fell to ~$2.62/Gb even though Illumina's 25B-300 list price rose ~3%, so the core's net reagent cost or its overhead fell, not the list price.
items.detail: CAT's UC lane rate went from $2,850 to $2,551 (−10.5%) on ~975 Gb per lane (3.25B clusters × 300 bases), which is $2.92 → $2.62/Gb. Over a similar window the 25B-300 catalogue list went from $16,000 (2024) to $16,480 (Jan 2025), or ~$2,000 → $2,060 per lane-eighth (D048). The core's mark-up over list per lane therefore shrank from ~$850 to ~$490. That fits a larger net discount to the core, though cutting overhead or a subsidy could also explain it. The 10B-to-25B per-Gb premium also narrowed from 1.57x ($4.60 vs $2.92) to 1.47x ($3.84 vs $2.62), in line with Bauer (F777) and Carver (D045).
items.source_name: UCSF CAT rate pages; Illumina catalogue (prior verified)
items.why_new: It is the first comparison of a core's lane-price cut against Illumina's rising list, and it corrects the yield from ~875 to ~975 Gb.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Natera's fixed-asset base and capex rose sharply in H1'26, which points to continued sequencing capacity build (and so Illumina volume) at the largest MRD and NIPT customer.
items.detail: Gross PP&E went from $352.3M (31 Dec 2025) to $450.9M (30 Jun 2026), +28%. Machinery and equipment went from $170.6M to $214.8M (+26%) and construction in process from $94.0M to $131.1M. H1 purchases of PP&E were $85.6M vs $47.7M in H1'25 (+79%). Depreciation was $13.1M in Q2'26 vs $8.9M a year earlier. Natera leased about 131K sq ft more in Austin between Mar and Dec 2025 (57.1K + 45.8K + 28.5K), running to Mar 2033. Accrued 'testing and laboratory materials' were $30.9M vs $12.4M at year-end. The caveat is that capacity can be bought ahead of volume. The filing does not say how much is sequencers.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Natera's hard supplier commitments fell while its capex rose, and no Illumina-named volume lock-in appears. This fits the view that Natera holds the bargaining leverage.
items.detail: Total material contractual commitments were $220.5M at 30 Jun 2026: material suppliers $120.3M (to Nov 2030), other suppliers $48.3M, cloud $22.7M, application services $15.9M, and a 'laboratory instruments supplier' $13.4M (to Dec 2027). The known figure of $256.9M with none named Illumina is about $36M higher, so commitments fell about 14% while capex rose 79%. Illumina is not named in any line. The Illumina supply agreement is the only large sequencing contract, and it has a binding fourth-month forecast of only ±25%.
items.why_new: This is the updated Q2'26 commitments table (the $256.9M figure is already known). The date of the $256.9M figure is unconfirmed.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Tempus is not building sequencing capacity at anything like Natera's or Caris's pace. Its fixed assets are flat even though its oncology tests are growing about 30%.
items.detail: Tempus's H1'26 purchases of PP&E were $14.3M vs $9.6M in H1'25 (+49% on a small base), plus $6.8M of capitalized software. Net PP&E was $89.1M at 30 Jun 2026 vs $89.2M at year-end. Diagnostics cost of revenue rose only 8% to $108.2M in Q2'26, while data and applications costs rose 40%. Compare Natera's capex of $85.6M and Caris's $32.4M over the same six months. A third large Illumina oncology customer is therefore growing volume without a matching physical capacity build.
items.source_name: Tempus AI 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 Jun 2026
items.why_new: The known list has Tempus job postings and oncology growth but no PP&E or capex comparison across the big labs.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Adaptive's 10-K shows a clinical MRD lab only partway through its move onto the NovaSeq X Plus, with the finish about two years out. Lab conversions run long.
items.detail: The FY25 10-K says Adaptive 'operationalized' the NovaSeq X Plus for clonoSEQ in H2'25 and expects to transition all MRD testing to it 'over the next two years.' That implies completion around 2027. The 10-K's supplier section names the Illumina NextSeq and NovaSeq X Plus as its sequencers, not the 6000, and Illumina is sole supplier of reagents and repair. Summaries say sequencing gross margin was 66% in FY25 vs 53% in FY24, and Q4'25 was 71%. The Q2'26 figure was 72% vs 64% (already known). Even a lab that skipped the 6000 and converted a smaller NextSeq base is still converting 12+ months after starting. This is consistent with conversion still dropping Illumina revenue per Gb in 2027. The margin figures come from earnings summaries, not the 10-K text I could read.
items.source_name: Adaptive Biotechnologies FY25 10-K; earnings summaries (vectorshift, MarketBeat)
items.quote: transition all of our MRD testing to the NovaSeq X Plus over the next two years
items.why_new: The known list has only Adaptive's 72% vs 64% margin; the two-year timeline and the FY25 66% vs 53% series are new.
items.verify_note: Quote verified. The 10-K names the NextSeq and the NovaSeq X Plus, not the 6000. So this is NextSeq-to-X conversion, which sits outside the 6000 HT mix metric that 1A is built on. It supports only the general point that clinical conversions take ~2 years and run into 2027. The 66%/53% margin figures are not in the 10-K text we read. The Q2'26 72% vs 64% is already known. The 10-K gives no FDA status for the X Plus for clonoSEQ.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: GeneDx expects its cost per test to fall in a 'step improvement' in 2027, and says genome cost is mostly reagents. That is a customer expecting cheaper reagents around when the 35B is due.
items.detail: On the Q2'26 call (3 Aug 2026), the CFO said cost per test would stay 'relatively flat' in H2'26 and then show 'step improvements in 2027.' Genomes currently cost nearly 2x as much to produce as exomes, 'largely' because of reagent costs, and GeneDx expects genome cost to fall as utilization grows and technology advances. The 10-Q also says it expects cost per test to fall long term from capacity utilization, automation and value engineering. Management ties the step to utilization, automation and technology, not explicitly to a price cut. But the 2027 timing matches the 35B flow cell roadmap (H1'27), and 6M exome/genome volume is +33%. Genome mix rising raises Gb per test, which partly offsets any price effect.
items.source_name: GeneDx Q2'26 10-Q and call (via MarketBeat/Quartr-type summary in search results)
items.quote: step improvements in 2027
items.why_new: The known list has the H2'26 flat cost-per-test guide; the 2027 step-down and the 'genome ≈ 2x exome, mostly reagents' attribution are new.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Guardant raised its Shield volume guide by about 17% and says a second, cheaper workflow went live in Aug 2026. Customer volume is strong, but cost per sample is being cut hard.
items.detail: Shield did about 66K tests in Q2'26 (+22K q/q, so Q1 was about 44K) vs about 16K a year ago. The FY26 guide rose to 270–285K from 230–245K. Q1+Q2 is about 110K, so H2 implies 160–175K, or 80–88K a quarter, 21–33% above Q2. A FDA-approved higher-throughput, lower-COGS workflow (methylation-only) goes live in August 2026 for new samples. COGS per test is about $410 now, targeted down 15% by end-2026 and to $200 by 2028. The Guardant360 Liquid move to the X saves about $200 per test. Non-GAAP gross margin was 67% vs 66%, with FY26 guided to 64–65% on 'lower second-half testing costs.' The release does not say what share of the Shield saving is sequencing. If any comes from shallower sequencing of fewer targets, Gb per test falls, which would trim the volume Illumina sees. Test volume itself is not the problem.
items.source_name: Guardant Health Q2'26 call transcript (Motley Fool)
items.quote: higher-throughput, lower-COGS Shield workflow
items.why_new: The known list has Shield at about 66K and COGS $410 vs ASP $800. The new items are the raised FY guide, the implied H2 run-rate, and the Aug 2026 low-COGS methylation-only workflow.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: BillionToOne's tests grew about 43% in Q1'26 with cost of revenue per test slightly down. The NIPT-led lab is still growing volume while cutting unit cost.
items.detail: Cost of revenue was $29.3M in Q1'26 vs $21.0M in Q1'25. Divided by about 188K and 131K tests (delivered-test counts as reported by the filing summary), cost per test is about $156 vs about $160, a roughly 3% fall, while tests rose about 43%. Gross margin was about 73% vs 64%, driven by ASP, 'COGS decreases' and efficiency. Purchases of PP&E were $4.5M vs $2.3M. Inventory was $19.2M vs $17.5M. Cost per test at about $156 total (all-in, not just sequencing) means very few Gb per test. NIPT-type volume growth therefore adds little Illumina volume. That is consistent with the thesis that test growth is not Gb growth. The test counts are my derivation and I did not confirm them in the filing's text.
items.why_new: The known list has BLLN tests +35% in Q2 and cost per test 'relatively stable', not the Q1 cost-of-revenue-per-test arithmetic or capex.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Canadian core Génome Québec CES advertises newly lowered NovaSeq X/25B-based prices, with human WGS at CAD 525 all-in.
items.detail: The CES page (footer 2026, undated) says it introduced lower prices as an early adopter of NovaSeq X and the 25B flow cell. It lists human WGS at CAD 525 for standard Canadian customers, with volume discounts on quote. TCAG's April 2025 list had human WGS at CAD 650 including library prep (90–100 Gb), so CES is about 19% lower, though dates and scope may differ. No prior CES price, per-lane price or rival-platform price was found.
items.quote: We have also introduced lower prices
items.why_new: The Canadian core WGS prices (CAD 525 at CES vs CAD 650 at TCAG) are not in the known core price list; the comparison is an unverified cross-core gap.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Taiwan's National Health Research Institutes (NHRI) has cut its outsourced Illumina-platform sequencing contract every year since 2023, and its 2026 Illumina lot budget is 37% below the 2023 award.
items.detail: The Illumina-platform lot (items 1–21) of NHRI's annual outsourced sequencing open contract was awarded at NT$13.99M (Aug 2023), NT$11.21M (Sep 2024, −19.8%) and NT$10.34M (Sep 2025, −7.8%). The Oct 2026 tender budgets Lot A (Illumina) at only NT$8.80M, 14.9% below the 2025 award and ~37% below 2023. The 2023 award came in at 68% of that year's lot budget, so the 2026 award could land lower still. Awards are open-contract ceilings, so actual drawdown and per-item prices are not shown. Contract winner each year: Genomics BioSci & Tech (基龍米克斯).
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (PCC) via g0v pcc-api; NHRI jobs 112B0E0461, 113B0E0232, 114B0E0213, 115B0D0286
items.why_new: F759/F799 cover NHRI's 2024 per-genome price and the end of its kit buying; this four-year outsourced-contract value series is new.
items.verify_note: Verified on PCC: the 115B0D0286 budget is NT$9,997,500, of which Lot A (Illumina) is NT$8,804,000 and Lot B (PacBio) NT$1,193,500. Bids open 14 Oct 2026, so there is no award yet. The award series is not re-checked. All figures are open-contract ceilings. A falling ceiling may reflect lower unit prices (Taiwanese outsourced WGS prices fell ~50% over 2023–25) as much as lower volume. This is a Taiwanese government institute, not a US NIH-funded buyer.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: NHRI's total MOHW-funded outsourced sequencing budget fell ~71% from 2021–22 to 2026, so the institute that stopped buying NovaSeq 6000 kits is also shrinking its outsourced replacement.
items.detail: Budgets: NT$35.0M (2021, 2022), NT$24.87M (2023, 2024, 2025), NT$9.9975M (Oct 2026 tender, Illumina NT$8.80M + PacBio NT$1.19M). Award totals: NT$31.39M (Apr 2021), NT$30.60M (May 2022), NT$17.97M (2023), NT$15.20M (2024), NT$14.33M (2025). The PacBio lot was flat at NT$3.989M for 2023–25, and its 2026 budget is NT$1.19M (−70%). Combined with F799 (S4 kit buying 57→16→0), NHRI's research sequencing spend is contracting on both channels, not just moving from kits to outsourcing.
items.why_new: The multi-year budget series for NHRI outsourcing (2021–2026) has not been reported; F718 only noted the shift to outsourcing.
items.verify_note: The 2026 budget total is verified at NT$9,997,500, and the −71% versus NT$35.0M is correct. This overlaps heavily with F845. Comparing a budget with a budget is fair, but the 2023–25 awards ran well below budget. The award-to-award decline from 2021 to 2025 is −54% (31.39 → 14.33). The 2026 award is still unknown.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: NHRI's outsourced Illumina sequencing lot had real competition only once (2023), and the winning margin was small: about 6% below the rival's bid.
items.detail: In 2023 two Illumina-based service providers bid for Lot 1: 基龍米克斯 at NT$13,985,910 won against 台基盟 at NT$14,949,500 (−6.4%), under a NT$14.4M base price. The 2024 and 2025 contracts were restricted follow-on awards (Art. 22(1)(7)), with each vendor taking its own lot unopposed. The 2026 tender returns to open, lowest-price bidding (opens 14 Oct 2026). So the year-on-year value declines happened without competitive rebidding, which points to volume or budget cuts rather than price competition.
items.why_new: The bidder spread and the restricted-renewal structure of NHRI's outsourcing contracts are not in the corpus.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: NTUH, Taiwan's flagship hospital, signed a NT$45M three-year MiSeq v3 reagent contract running to Aug 2027, so a retired legacy Illumina platform keeps carrying large, durable reagent spend.
items.detail: Job TD130370 (MiSeq v3 600-cycle reagent unit-price contract) has a budget of NT$47.4M and a base price of NT$45.0M. It was awarded 14 Aug 2024 at NT$45.0M to the Illumina distributor Genetech (均泰), the single bidder, after two failed rounds. The term is 1 Sep 2024–31 Aug 2027 and the origin is UK. That is ~NT$15M/yr (~US$0.47M/yr at ~32 NT$/US$) on a platform whose end of sale was 30 Sep 2025. Legacy-chemistry tails at large clinical sites look like multi-year contracted demand, not a fast fade.
items.why_new: No MiSeq reagent contract value or duration at a large hospital is in the corpus; D047/F494 cover MiSeq service plans only.
items.verify_note: This is the MiSeq, not the 6000. It shows only by analogy that legacy-chemistry tails carry multi-year contracted reagent spend at large clinical sites. The NT$45M figure is a 3-year ceiling for a unit-price contract, not guaranteed spend.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: In June 2026 NTUH locked in NextSeq 500/550 v2.5 high-output kits through July 2029, another legacy-chemistry tail contracted three years out.
items.detail: Job TD150300 (中通量300鹼基循環定序試劑組v2.5) has a budget of NT$4.90M and a base price of NT$4.508M. It was awarded 9 Jun 2026 at NT$4.41M to Genetech (single bidder, US origin), 10% below budget and 2.2% below base. The term is 1 Aug 2026–31 Jul 2029. v2.5 chemistry is the NextSeq 500/550 line, not XLEAP NextSeq 1000/2000, so the hospital is still running an older mid-throughput box under a fresh three-year commitment.
items.why_new: The new 2026–2029 NextSeq v2.5 contract at NTUH is not in the corpus (F719/F751 cover P1–P4 XLEAP kits).
items.verify_note: Duplicate of F861, which covers the same TD150300 award. It also mislabels the kit: 中通量 means MID-output v2.5, not high-output. NextSeq 500/550 is mid-throughput, not the 6000 tail.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Taichung VGH tried to lease a NextSeq 2000 system for three years with a NT$27.9M budget (~NT$9.3M a year), which shows bundled rental or subscription buying spreading to mid-throughput clinical boxes.
items.detail: Job 114X-R4 ('NextSeq 2000測序系統租賃', 3 years from acceptance) had a NT$27.9M budget and a NT$100K bid bond. It followed a Mar 2025 request for reference data (114P-11, '租賃三年期'). Round 1 failed on 8 May 2025 for lack of bidders and was re-tendered on 13 May 2025. No award notice appears under the title, so the outcome is unknown; the Sep 2026 P1 kit contract (F751) may be its successor. Annual value ≈ US$290K, far above a NextSeq 2000's ~US$300K purchase price spread over 3 years. That implies the rental bundles reagents, consistent with Illumina's subscription push (F560/F592).
items.why_new: There is no hospital-level Illumina rental tender with a dollar value in the corpus.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: A large private medical center used new 'Healthy Taiwan Deepening' grant money to buy a UK-origin low-throughput long-read sequencer and consumables, diversifying away from short-read Illumina.
items.detail: Cathay General Hospital's CGH115001 (低通量長片段核酸定序儀系統) was awarded 11 Feb 2026 at NT$1.78M to ANTEC Bioscience (single bidder, UK product origin, likely Oxford Nanopore; our inference). A companion consumables lot (CGH115002) followed, plus NGS chips with reagents at NT$196K × 10 (CGH115003, NT$1.96M) and sequencing reagents NT$1.635M (CGH115005, US origin). All of these were single-bidder awards after failed first rounds.
items.source_name: PCC via pcc-api; Cathay General Hospital CGH115001–CGH115005
items.why_new: Cathay General's grant-funded sequencing purchases are not in the corpus; F749/F750 cover CDC, NTUH and other ONT buyers.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: NTU Cancer Center's NT$5.85M tender for a benchtop mid-throughput sequencer failed twice in three weeks, a sign of weak vendor interest or spec problems in new mid-throughput clinical placements.
items.detail: PA2600139 (桌上型中通量次世代定序儀1組, lowest-price open tender, budget NT$5.85M ≈ US$180K) was posted 17 Sep 2026. It failed on 1 Oct (流標, no or too few bids) and was annulled on 7 Oct (廢標) on re-tender. A third round opens 13 Oct 2026. No brand is named. The outcome is the next datapoint on whether Illumina (NextSeq 2000) or Element (AVITI) wins a fresh mid-throughput clinical slot.
items.source_name: PCC via pcc-api; NTUH Cancer Center branch PA2600139
items.why_new: This is a live Oct 2026 tender not previously captured.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Taipei VGH pays NT$20,500 (~US$640) per outsourced 12 Gb RNA-seq sample under a single-bid 2026–28 contract, far from the 'insane discount' price behaviour assumed for research buyers.
items.detail: X11502H (核糖核酸測序12G分析, 2-year unit-price contract) has a budget of NT$477K and a base price of NT$420K for an estimated 20 samples. It was awarded May 2026 at NT$20,500 per sample (NT$410K total) to 圖爾思生物科技, the single bidder, after a voided first round. That is ~NT$1,700/Gb (~US$53/Gb) all-in, versus ~$50 per sample at cheap academic RNA-seq services (F727). Small hospital-research buyers are not price-shopping.
items.source_name: PCC via pcc-api; Taipei VGH X11502H
items.why_new: This is new hospital research RNA-seq unit pricing, not in the corpus.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: At Berkeley, a pooled UC account resells NovaSeq X lanes at only about 2-7% above UCSF CAT's internal rate, so aggregated UC demand is priced near cost.
items.detail: Berkeley's 25B 150PE lane is $2,600 (UC rate, work after 1 Jun 2026), against CAT's 25B-300 at $2,551, a +1.9% markup. The 10B 150PE lane is $1,535 against CAT's 10B-300 at $1,439, a +6.7% markup. Per Gb on Berkeley's spec of 875 Gb, the 25B is $2.97/Gb. The CAT page carries no date, so the comparison assumes the two prices are contemporaneous.
items.source_name: UC Berkeley QB3 Genomics rates; UCSF CAT rates
items.quote: all lanes are sent to the UCSF CAT Lab
items.why_new: Known list has Berkeley's 'small markup' with no computed markup percentages.
items.verify_note: Duplicate of F818, which is already verified with the same Berkeley-vs-CAT markups of ~2% and ~7%. A core reselling lanes near cost says nothing about Illumina's discounting accelerating.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Berkeley's external 25B lane ($2,990) is about 12% below CAT's implied non-UC price and about 22% below UCSD IGM's 2025 outside price.
items.detail: CAT states non-UC academic is +33% over its UC rate, so $2,551 x 1.33 = $3,393 implied. Berkeley external of $2,990 / $3,393 = -11.9%. UCSD IGM 2025 outside 25B-300 was $3,836, so $2,990 / $3,836 = -22%. UCLA TCGB external (effective 1 Jul 2026) is $3,512, so Berkeley is -14.9% against it. UC external prices differ by campus, which weakens an Illumina floor.
items.source_name: QB3, UCSF CAT, UCSD IGM, UCLA TCGB rate pages
items.why_new: New cross-campus external-lane arithmetic. Some inputs are snippet-level, and CAT's +33% is a stated multiplier, not a published price.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: UC campus external research lane prices are not collapsing. UCLA's external 25B-300 is $3,512 from 1 Jul 2026.
items.detail: UCLA TCGB external 25B lanes are $2,165 (100c), $3,202 (200c) and $3,512 (300c), and 10B 300c is $1,766. $3,512 per 875 Gb is $4.01/Gb. Rates are re-set each 1 July. Only external rates were visible, so no year-on-year change can be computed here. A search snippet gave UCLA's Mar 2024 25B-300 at $3,168, which implies +10.9% over 28 months, but that snippet is unverified.
items.why_new: Known list has UCLA at $3.51/lane, with no 100c/200c/10B rows and no trend against the Mar 2024 snippet.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: UC research-core pricing is tiered with large premiums for outsiders, so research pricing is policy-driven.
items.detail: Berkeley's 25B 150PE lane is $2,600 UC, $2,860 affiliate (+10%) and $2,990 external (+15%). CAT states +33% for non-UC non-profit and +46.3% for for-profit. Berkeley's rates 'change annually on July 1' by UC policy, so the 1 Jul 2026 reset is the date to check for Illumina-driven moves. The premium range across UC cores is 15-33%, against 40% at Harvard Bauer.
items.why_new: Adds the UC tier structure and the annual 1 July reset mechanism.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Berkeley's 25B lane is priced $2,600 for 875 Gb ($2.97/Gb), above CAT's stated 25B-300 UC rate of $2,551, so no further Berkeley-side cut shows up from consolidation.
items.detail: Berkeley passes CAT's price through with a markup rather than negotiating a lower one. The summer 2026 consolidation onto one partner did not produce a visible cut in Berkeley's resale rate. The Berkeley page carries no earlier version, so the before price is unknown. The archive was blocked, and the '?p=6524' URL (titled July 2024) returned the current content.
items.why_new: Tests the consolidation-implies-discounting idea. No evidence of acceleration was found.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Neither Berkeley nor CAT lists a NovaSeq 6000 row, and UCLA's page shows none, so the 6000 is already absent at UC cores.
items.detail: Berkeley sends all lanes to CAT, which lists only X Plus (25B, 10B, 1.5B). UCLA's current page has no S4 rows. Berkeley says it has no sequencer of its own. UC research 6000 volume has therefore already moved to X pricing, which fits the 'research is ~92% converted' view and offers no support for a research 6000 tail.
items.why_new: Confirms 6000 rows are absent at UC cores, which the known list covers only for UCLA and Northwestern.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: NHRI's total outsourced NGS ceiling fell about 68% from 2021 to 2026, and its own NovaSeq 6000 service and kit buying stopped at the same time, so this research account's Illumina-linked spend shrank sharply.
items.detail: Outsourced NGS awards were NT$31.39M (Apr 2021, single vendor Taiwan Genome Alliance), NT$17.97M (2023), NT$15.20M (2024) and NT$14.33M (2025). The 2026 budget is NT$9.9975M (Illumina 8.804M + PacBio 1.1935M). The budget held at NT$24.87M in 2023–25 while awards fell.
