In-house, the four-unit NovaSeq 6000 service contract cost NT$13.8M for Dec 2023–Dec 2024 and has no successor in PCC title searches. Derived: Illumina-linked spend was at least ~NT$27.8M a year in 2023–24 (13.8M service + 13.99M outsourced Illumina, before kits) vs ~NT$8.8–10.3M in 2025–26, roughly −63% to −68%.
items.quote: 委外檢測開口契約: 次世代基因體核酸定序實驗
items.why_new: Quantifies the combined fall in in-house plus outsourced spend at NHRI; F718 only noted that NHRI moved to outsourcing.
items.verify_note: Duplicates F846 (same NHRI award and budget series) and leans on F800/D078 for the service contract. The 'no successor service contract' rests on PCC title searches failing to find one, which is weak. The derived −63% to −68% mixes service and outsourcing spend from different time windows.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Taiwan's flagship hospital (NTUH) signed new three-year reagent contracts for retired or legacy Illumina platforms that run to 2028–2029.
items.detail: NTUH awarded MiniSeq mid-output 300-cycle kits (7 items) for Jun 2025–May 2028 at NT$2,148,230, sole-source under Art. 22(1)(4), with one bidder (Genetech). That runs well past MiniSeq end of sale (30 Sep 2025). It also awarded NextSeq 500/550-class mid-output v2.5 300-cycle kits for Aug 2026–Jul 2029 at NT$4,410,000 (restricted tender, Art. 22(1)(2), single bidder, 2.2% below the NT$4,508,000 floor). Clinical labs keep legacy Illumina boxes on reagent contracts for 3+ years, which fits a slow, sticky high-price tail and is consistent with management's 'stays for years' framing.
items.quote: 中通量300鹼基循環定序試劑組v2.5開口合約
items.why_new: These are new dated legacy-platform reagent commitments to 2028–29 at an Asian clinical flagship; earlier tail items are US, Canadian, UK and EU service contracts.
items.verify_note: The new elements are the MiniSeq kits contracted to May 2028 (past the Sep 2025 end of sale) and the NextSeq v2.5 mid-output kits to Jul 2029. These are low- and mid-throughput legacy platforms, not the 6000, so they bear on the 6000 tail's stickiness only by analogy. The amounts are unit-price ceilings.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Kaohsiung VGH bought outsourced clinical WGS at NT$12,800 per genome in Dec 2025 and Jan 2026, and a bidder linked to AXELIOS (Centogene) bid higher, not lower.
items.detail: Kaohsiung VGH bought 210 oral-cancer genomes for NT$2,688,000 (Dec 2025, one bidder; the original bid of NT$13,500 per genome was cut to the floor). It bought 250 women's-medicine genomes including blood extraction for NT$3,200,000 (Jan 2026). Both prices derive to NT$12,800 per genome (~US$400), awarded to Genomics BioSci. In the Jan 2026 lot, Centogene APAC (權拓基因) bid NT$3,498,750 (NT$13,995 per genome, +9%) and was ruled non-compliant on documents. This extends the flat NT$12,800 rate to a fourth hospital and into 2026.
items.quote: 權拓基因股份有限公司
items.why_new: D073 and F744 cover three earlier awards. Kaohsiung VGH's 2026 awards and the Centogene APAC bid are new.
items.verify_note: The NT$12,800 Kaohsiung VGH awards (Dec 2025 and Jan 2026) are already in F744. This is not a fourth hospital. The only new detail is a non-compliant bid of NT$13,995 by 權拓基因. Its identity as Centogene, and whether it would use AXELIOS for this work, are unverified. A single bid rejected on documents says little about rival pricing.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: On NTUH's NT$297M flagship WGS reagent-with-instrument contract, the hospital pushed the sole bidder down 10.8%, from NT$332.9M to the floor.
items.detail: K114031 runs 1 Mar 2026–28 Feb 2029 and bundles WGS reagents with instruments (a reagent-rental structure). Genetech (均泰, Illumina's distributor) was the only bidder. Its original bid of NT$332,927,500 was awarded at NT$296,999,880, NT$120 under the NT$297,000,000 floor. The first round failed with no bidders. Even without competition, the large clinical buyer used its budget-floor mechanism to extract ~11% off the vendor's ask, about US$1.1M a year.
items.quote: 次世代全基因體定序試劑3項(附儀器)開口合約
items.why_new: F715 gave only the contract value; the bid-to-award concession and the reagent-with-instrument bundling are new.
items.verify_note: Numbers check out against the PCC record: one bidder (Genetech), bid NT$332,927,500, award NT$296,999,880 against a NT$297,000,000 base price, term 1 Mar 2026 to 28 Feb 2029. The first call drew no bids. Two corrections. First, the NT$297M is the base price (底價), not a 'floor' the vendor was pushed to. When a bid comes in above the base price, Taiwanese procurement law requires the vendor to cut down to it, so this is a routine step and not evidence of a large buyer using leverage. The award is

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Two Taiwanese veterans' hospitals pay very different prices for the same Illumina NextSeq 2000 P3 kit: Taipei VGH about 49% more than Taichung VGH.
items.detail: Taipei VGH (1150157V, May 2026, single bidder Genetech) paid NT$235,000 per P3 set (15 sets, NT$3,525,000) and NT$201,000 per P4 XLEAP set (18 sets). Taichung VGH (115A018, Sep 2026, single bidder Genomics BioSci) paid NT$9,480,000 for 60 P3 kits ≈ NT$158,000 each and NT$2,640,000 for 12 P4 kits ≈ NT$220,000 each (derived from the tender quantities). The P3 gap is +49% at Taipei, while P4 is 9% cheaper there. Prices depend on the channel and the deal, not a list. That fits individualized, negotiable pricing rather than a uniform price floor.
items.quote: P3 大通量定序試劑組
items.why_new: F713, F717 and D071 cover each hospital separately. The cross-hospital comparison of the same kit and the two competing Illumina channels are new.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Taipei VGH's mid-throughput Illumina reagent commitments rose roughly 60–70% between its 2023–25 and 2025–28 contracts.
items.detail: Dec 2023 (1120652Y) bought a 2-year 'high-throughput reagent set' of 29 sets for NT$6.67M (~NT$230K per set). The new cycle stacks three awards: 1140732E (Nov 2025, 2-year lot NT$3.942M, ≈17 sets at ~NT$230K) plus 1150157V (May 2026: 15 P3 + 18 P4 sets, NT$7.143M). That is ~NT$11.1M and ~50 sets vs NT$6.67M and 29 sets (derived; the Apr 2025 P4 contract 1140134V may overlap). Clinical mid-throughput usage at this hospital is growing, not stalling.
items.quote: 高通量定序試劑組等7項2年單價開口契約
items.why_new: Known items give only per-set prices at Taipei VGH; the contract-cycle volume comparison is new.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Taiwan's public procurement shows no NovaSeq 6000 kit buying since Dec 2023 and no NovaSeq X kit line by name, because high-throughput work moved into bundled or outsourced contracts.
items.detail: Title searches on PCC for 'NovaSeq' return 19 records, all at NHRI, ending with 16 S4 v1.5 kits and 6000 service in Dec 2023. Searches for 'S4' found only those NHRI rows, and '25B' found no sequencing rows. In 2024–26, hospital high-throughput sequencing appears only as reagents-with-instrument lots (NTUH NT$32.5M and NT$297M) or as per-genome outsourcing to Genomics BioSci and Taiwan Genome Alliance. So the share of 6000 kit value is 100% through 2023 and there are no observable kit lines in 2024–26. The requested 6000-vs-X kit-line count cannot be built from Taiwan's public data.
items.why_new: This is a method finding: it records that the Taiwan kit-line vein is dry, so later agents need not repeat it.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: A Taiwanese clinical center and NHRI are adding long-read capacity next to Illumina in 2026.
items.detail: Taipei VGH awarded a 3-year 'third-generation sequencing whole-genome reagents (6 items, with equipment)' contract (M11476V, Mar 2026) at NT$11.3M to Genomics BioSci, origin USA (likely PacBio); one bidder after two failed rounds. NHRI opened a vendor-quote solicitation on 12 Oct 2026 for a long-read sequencing system for its new F building. Meanwhile, NHRI's own outsourced PacBio budget for 2026 fell to NT$1.19M from NT$3.99M. The net effect for Illumina is mixed; this is a weak signal.
items.quote: 三代定序全基因體基因檢測試劑6項(含設備)
items.why_new: Taiwan long-read adoption was not in the ledger (Taiwan CDC nanopore items F749 and F750 cover ONT only).

items.label: 2B
items.claim: NHRI's shrinking Illumina outsourcing spend is mostly explained by falling unit prices, not lower volume: Illumina-lot awards fell ~26% over 2023–25 while Taiwanese outsourced genome prices fell ~47–59%, which would leave room for flat-to-higher volume.
items.detail: The NHRI Illumina lot was awarded at NT$13.99M (Aug 2023), NT$11.21M (2024) and NT$10.34M (Sep 2025), down 26% (F845). Over the same period, outsourced 30x WGS prices in Taiwan fell from NT$24,000 (Taipei VGH, Jul 2023) to NT$9,800 (NHRI's own Oct 2024 award) and NT$12,800 (2025–26) (D073, F759). If unit prices fell ~47–59%, the implied volume change is 0.74/0.53 = 1.4x to 0.74/0.41 = 1.8x, i.e. volume up, not down. This depends on mix and on how much of each ceiling was drawn down. On a budget-to-budget basis, the 2023 lot budget was ~NT$20.6M (13.99/0.68) against NT$8.80M in 2026 (−57%). That decline is similar in size to the unit-price fall, which again points to price rather than volume. This fits the thesis's 'volume flat, price worse' research pattern.
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (PCC) via g0v pcc-api
items.quote: A組 Illumina平台 8,804,000元
items.why_new: F845 and F846 read the NHRI decline as shrinking research spend; netting it against the verified Taiwanese unit-price fall shows that price, not volume, drives it.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Natera's capacity build in H1'26 is running ahead of its test growth: machinery and equipment rose ~52% annualized and Q2 depreciation +47% y/y, against total tests +22%. That points to more sequencing per test (genome-based MRD) or capacity ahead of demand.
items.detail: Natera's machinery and equipment went from $170.6M to $214.8M in six months (+25.9%, ~+52% annualized), and construction in process rose to $131.1M. Q2'26 depreciation was $13.1M vs $8.9M (+47% y/y), and H1 capex was $85.6M vs $47.7M (+79%) (10-Q, 30 Jun 2026). Known Q2'26 total tests grew +22% (1.04M), so depreciation per test rose from ~$10.4 to ~$12.6 (+21%). Accrued lab materials owed to suppliers rose 2.5x ($12.4M → $30.9M), which is consistent with a reagent ramp, although the filing does not break out sequencers or Illumina. One reading is that Gb per test is rising, which cuts against slowing Illumina volume at its largest clinical customer. The other is that capacity is being bought ahead of volume, which is the known caveat.
items.why_new: Capex and depreciation growth compared with test growth is a ratio no prior item computed; the known items cover only Natera's test counts and the Austin facility announcement.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Caris is publicly weighing sequencing suppliers other than its incumbent while it ramps lab capacity and spends heavily on capex.
items.detail: On the Q2'26 call (5 Aug 2026), CFO Luke Power said Caris is looking at additional sequencing capabilities beyond its current supplier. Q2 capex was $22.1M, which absorbed free cash flow, and inventory rose $47M q/q as Caris invested ahead of the Caris Detect ramp. GAAP gross margin was 68% vs 63% a year earlier, with H2 guided to about 60%. The vendor is not named in the excerpt, and this is the call's wording, not a contract change.
items.quote: additional sequencing capabilities, not just what our current existing supplier is
items.why_new: The 'two competitors' quote is known. This adds the $22.1M Q2 capex, the +$47M inventory build and the Power remark on assessing other sequencing technologies, which were not in the exclusion list.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: In June 2026 NTUH sole-sourced a 3-year NextSeq 500/550 v2.5 kit contract that runs to Jul 2029, so a legacy mid-throughput tail is contracted out three years.
items.detail: TD150300, awarded 9 Jun 2026: a NextSeq 500/550 v2.5 300-cycle kit open contract worth NT$4.41M (~US$138K) for 1 Aug 2026–31 Jul 2029, about NT$1.47M a year. The budget was NT$4.9M and the award came in 10% below it. It was a restricted tender under Procurement Act Art. 22(1)(2), which covers exclusive or proprietary supply, with one bidder (Genetech). For scale, NTUH bought a one-off NextSeq 500/550 lot for only NT$452K in Nov 2020. A clinical hospital renewing legacy-platform reagents to 2029 shows tails being locked in under multi-year contracts, not converted.
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (pcc via openfun API)
items.quote: 中通量300鹼基循環定序試劑組v2.5開口合約
items.why_new: A new 2026 award. Prior items covered NextSeq 2000 (P1–P4) kits, not legacy NextSeq 550 v2.5 contracts running to 2029.
items.verify_note: This repeats F861, which already covers NTUH signing new three-year legacy-platform contracts running to 2028–29. The NextSeq 500/550 is a mid-throughput instrument, not the NovaSeq 6000, so it says little about the 6000 tail in 1A. The award is NT$1.47M a year (about US$47K), which is immaterial.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: The Academia Sinica institute that bought an Illumina NextSeq 500 in 2016 bought its next mid-throughput sequencer from Element (AVITI) in May 2026, for 22% less.
items.detail: Academia Sinica's Institute of Molecular Biology bought a NextSeq 500 for NT$11.80M in Jun 2016 (105-IMBE020, Illumina distributor Genetech, single bid). On 28 May 2026 the same institute awarded an 'AVITI mid-throughput sequencing platform' for NT$9.20M (~US$290K) to Element's Taiwan channel, Asia Pathogenomics (亞洲準誠) (115-IMBE016, budget NT$9.768M, −5.8%). That award was a restricted tender under Art. 22(1)(2), meaning the institute specified AVITI as a proprietary product. We could not confirm that the AVITI replaces the NextSeq 500, so the replacement reading is an inference. Either way, a top national research institute chose a rival platform when refreshing its mid-throughput capacity.
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (pcc via openfun API)
items.quote: AVITI中通量定序平台01套
items.why_new: F747 counted Element awards at Academia Sinica. This adds the same-institute NextSeq 500 (2016) to AVITI (2026) pairing and the price gap.
items.verify_note: The IMB AVITI award (115-IMBE016, NT$9.20M) is already in F747 and F885. The only new piece is the lineage: the same institute bought a NextSeq 500 in 2016. The '22% less' compares two different instruments bought ten years apart, so it says nothing about pricing and should be dropped. We could not confirm that the AVITI replaced the NextSeq. Keep this only as a weak refresh anecdote.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: A large private Taipei hospital spent its MOHW 'Healthy Taiwan' sequencing grant mostly on non-Illumina platforms. UK-origin long-read gear (likely ONT) took about 2.5x the US-origin reagent dollars.
items.detail: Cathay General Hospital's 2026 Healthy Taiwan Deep Cultivation buys, all subsidized by MOHW and all single-bid, were: a 'low-throughput long-fragment' sequencer of UK origin (likely Oxford Nanopore) for NT$1.78M (CGH115001, Feb 2026); its UK-origin chips and consumables for NT$3.15M (CGH115002); 10 Taiwan-origin 'NGS chips with reagents' at NT$196K each, NT$1.96M in total (CGH115003); and US-origin 'sequencing reagents and consumables' for NT$1.635M (CGH115005, brand not stated). The long-read consumables (NT$3.15M) are about 1.9x the US-origin reagent lot. Including the sequencer (NT$4.93M in total), the long-read spend is about 3.0x. The national precision-health program, which runs over ROC years 114–118 (2025–2029), is funding rival platforms at hospitals.
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (pcc via openfun API)
items.quote: 低通量長片段核酸定序儀系統檢驗分析晶片及耗材採購案
items.why_new: F750 covered ONT at NTUH and unnamed centers. Cathay General and the Healthy Taiwan grant channel are new.
items.verify_note: The ratios contradict each other. The claim says '2.5x', but the detail works out to 1.9x on consumables (3.15/1.635) and 3.0x including the sequencer (4.93/1.635). The claim should say 1.9x for consumables only. The US-origin reagent lot (NT$1.635M) has no brand and could be Illumina or Thermo. The Taiwan-origin chips are not Illumina. 'Likely ONT' is an inference. This is a long-read grant purchase of about US$0.3M in total, so it is tangential to the short-read discounting argument and adds l

items.label: 2A
items.claim: A Taiwanese government research institute raised its Illumina library-prep and consumables spend 28% y/y and added a new Illumina-made sequencer in 2026.
items.detail: The Animal Health Research Institute (MOA) awarded 'NGS library-prep reagents and chips' of Singapore origin (Illumina's manufacturing site) to Illumina distributor Genetech. The award was NT$1.246M in Oct 2025 (B-114-0880, budget NT$1.467M) and NT$1.595M in Oct 2026 (115-2013, budget NT$1.9125M), +28% in award and +30% in budget. The institute also bought one Singapore-origin NGS sequencer for NT$2.295M (~US$72K, likely a benchtop Illumina system) in May 2026 (115-2003). The 2026 single bidder bid at budget and was negotiated down 16.6%, to below the NT$1.62M floor. Government research sequencing at this buyer is growing on Illumina rather than moving to rivals.
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (pcc via openfun API)
items.quote: 次世代定序儀專用建庫試劑及晶片
items.why_new: This buyer's y/y consumables series and its new 2026 sequencer were not in the corpus.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: The biggest single-bidder Illumina award in this pull still moved 16.6% off the opening bid, while other single-bid Illumina lots closed within 1% of budget, so concessions vary by deal rather than following a list.
items.detail: On 115-2013 (Oct 2026) Genetech bid the full NT$1.9125M budget and accepted NT$1.595M (−16.6%), below the NT$1.62M floor. Other single-bid Illumina-distributor awards closed much nearer budget: Chang Gung Linkou's Illumina sequencer at −0.8% (NT$2.245M vs NT$2.264M, Aug 2025), the MOA sequencer at −2.3%, NTUH NextSeq 550 kits at −10% and NTUH MiSeq at −5%. This fits the expert view that Illumina prices deal by deal. It adds dispersion data to F714/F763/F835, though it does not show discounts deepening over time.
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (pcc via openfun API)
items.why_new: Adds the award-versus-bid gap on five new 2025–26 single-bidder Illumina awards. Prior items covered other buyers.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: NTUH bought the same NT$694K block of Illumina DRAGEN analysis volume in both FY2025/26 and FY2026/27, which implies no growth in genomic data analyzed on DRAGEN at the flagship hospital.
items.detail: PH2500116 (award 4 Jun 2025, covering 1 Jul 2025–30 Jun 2026) and PH2600137 (Jun 2026, covering 11 Jul 2026–10 Jul 2027) both bought 'illumina DRAGEN analysis throughput' for exactly NT$694,000 against an identical NT$842,250 budget. Both were sole-source (Art. 22(1)(2)) from Genetech. DRAGEN usage is metered by data volume, so a flat purchased block suggests flat analyzed Gb, although the hospital may also be under-using its prior block. It also shows no price change on Illumina's software usage.
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (pcc via openfun API)
items.quote: illumina DRAGEN高速基因體資料分析運算系統分析流量
items.why_new: First DRAGEN usage-purchase series found. No DRAGEN volume proxy was in the corpus.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Taichung VGH tried to lease a NextSeq 2000 system for three years with a NT$27.9M budget, and the first round drew no bids, a sign that reagent-rental and lease structures are spreading at Asian clinical sites.
items.detail: Taichung VGH ran 114P-11 (an RFI, Mar 2025) and then tender 114X-R4 for a 'NextSeq 2000 sequencing system lease'. The budget was NT$27.9M (~US$870K, ~US$290K a year) over 3 years from acceptance, with installation within 150 days. The first round failed with no bids on 8 May 2025 and was re-tendered on 13 May 2025. No award appears in the title index. A lease worth almost 3x the price of a NextSeq 2000 must bundle reagents, which matches Illumina's push toward subscription and consumption pricing (F559/F560). Those structures blur list-versus-net price.
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (pcc via openfun API)
items.quote: NextSeq 2000測序系統租賃
items.why_new: The Taichung lease tender has not been reported before. F751 covered only its Sep 2026 NextSeq 2000 kit contract.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Taiwan hospital awards signed in 2024–26 show a legacy-chemistry tail (MiSeq v3, NextSeq 500/550 v2.5) of about NT$16.5M a year, locked in to 2027–2029.
items.detail: NTUH MiSeq v3 (TD130370): NT$45.0M, 1 Sep 2024–31 Aug 2027, which is NT$15.0M a year. NTUH NextSeq 500/550-type v2.5 300-cycle medium-throughput set (TD150300): NT$4.41M, 1 Aug 2026–31 Jul 2029, which is NT$1.47M a year. Together that is about NT$16.5M a year. Against the Illumina kit contracts I could identify as in force, legacy is about 12.7%. The rest: NTUH K114031 WGS bundle NT$297M/3y = NT$99.0M a year (brand unnamed, so X is inferred); Taichung P1–P4 NT$19.9M/2y = 9.96M a year; Taipei VGH 1150157V NT$7.14M/2y = 3.57M a year; Taipei P4 1140134V NT$1.81M/2y = 0.9M a year. The sum is 99.0+15.0+1.47+9.96+3.57+0.9 = NT$129.9M, and 16.5/129.9 = 12.7%. Treat the share as indicative: it mixes award years, and Taipei VGH 1140732E item 1 (NT$3.94M/2y) is omitted because the notice names no brand.
items.source_name: Taiwan e-Procurement (PCC) via openfun API, NTUH awards TD130370 and TD150300
items.why_new: F848/F849 gave the contracts; this adds annualised values and a rough legacy share of identified Illumina award value.
items.verify_note: The components repeat F848 (MiSeq v3) and F861/F869 (NextSeq). Neither platform is the 6000, and a locked-in legacy tail supports management's 'permanent tail' claim, so the 'supports' label is the wrong direction. The 12.7% share is fragile. The denominator is dominated by K114031, which names no brand, and it mixes award years and leaves out unbranded lots. It is not a usable metric.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Taipei VGH's P4 XLEAP kit volume doubled at an unchanged NT$201,000 per set, which is volume growth without price concession.
items.detail: The Apr 2025 award (1140134V, one bidder, Genetech) was 9 sets at NT$201,000 = NT$1.809M for 11 Apr 2025–10 Apr 2027. The Apr 2026 award (1150157V item 1) was 18 sets at NT$201,000 = NT$3.618M for 1 Jul 2026–30 Jun 2027 (per the notice's contract-period field). Quantity rose 100% at an identical unit price, so Illumina's revenue at this account is +100% on this item, with no price step. This is a mid-throughput kit in Taiwan, a tiny account. It cuts against both 'volume slows' and 'discounting accelerates' at this buyer.
items.why_new: F713 noted the flat price; the doubling of contracted sets from 9 to 18 is new.
items.verify_note: This repeats F713 (the same NT$201,000 per set, 9 sets then 18 sets). The periods overlap: the first contract runs Apr 2025 to Apr 2027 and the second Jul 2026 to Jun 2027. So '+100%' is not a clean y/y comparison. Annualized it is 4.5 sets a year versus 18, or the first contract was used up early. The account is immaterial.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Taichung VGH's Sep 2026 award shows a deeper award discount versus budget on larger flow cells (P3 about −21%, P4 about −15%) than on small ones (P1 and P2 about −6%).
items.detail: Award 115A018 (15 Sep 2026, Genomics BioSci, single bidder, 1 Oct 2026–30 Sep 2028) implies per-set prices of P1 NT$46,000 (30 sets), P2 NT$93,000 (69), P3 NT$158,000 (60) and P4 NT$220,000 (12). Budget per set was 49,000, 98,500, 200,000 and 260,000, so the award is −6.1%, −5.6%, −21.0% and −15.4% versus budget. The P3 bid was NT$180,000 and fell to NT$158,000, which is −12% from bid, so the largest-volume item was negotiated down hardest. Total award was NT$19.917M against a NT$23.39M budget (−14.8%). The 'single bidder' label still shows concession under a leverage-style buyer. This is one hospital, and the P-series are mid-throughput XLEAP kits.
items.why_new: F751/F814 gave aggregate budget gaps; this adds the per-item unit-price ladder, quantities and bid-to-award gaps.
items.verify_note: This repeats F751 and D071, which already give the award-versus-budget cuts of −6%, −6%, −21% and −15%. The buyer sets the budget, so award versus budget measures how padded the budget was, not discounting. D071 shows the P3 price about 18% above US list, which cuts against 1B. The bid-to-award −12% on P3 is the only new detail and is too thin to stand on its own.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Even sole-bidder legacy tails take price concessions: NTUH's NextSeq v2.5 set was cut about 10% from the bid, and the MiSeq tail about 5% from the bid.
items.detail: TD150300 (budget and sole bid NT$4.9M, reserve 4.508M, award NT$4.41M, −10.0%). TD130370 MiSeq v3 (bid NT$47.4M, awarded NT$45.0M, −5.1%) came after three tender rounds, two of which failed. Illumina's distributor Genetech conceded price on the retiring-platform lots without competition. This is consistent with a tail that is still price-managed. The values are small.
items.source_name: Taiwan e-Procurement (PCC), NTUH TD130370 and TD150300
items.why_new: Bid-to-award concession on legacy-platform lots was not in the known list.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Subsidised Cathay General Hospital sequencing buys landed at 98–99% of budget, showing no deep discounting at new clinical buyers.
items.detail: CGH115005 (sequencing reagents, NT$1.635M against NT$1.65M budget, 99.1%) and CGH115003 (NGS chips with reagents, 10 units at NT$196,000 = NT$1.96M against NT$2.0M, 98.0%) were both awarded 23 Mar 2026 to single bidders after a failed first tender in Feb 2026. They were funded by the Ministry of Health's Healthy Taiwan programme. The sums are tiny, and the chip origin is listed as Taiwan, so the brand is unclear.
items.why_new: A new buyer with award-to-budget ratios; Cathay was not among the Taiwan buyers already covered.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Federal outsourcing to Psomagen peaked in FY2024 at about $3.1M of NIH/HHS awards and fell about 66% in FY2025, so it is not a rising channel.
items.detail: Govconinabox lists Psomagen HHS awards of 19 totalling about $3.13M in FY2024 and 18 totalling about $1.07M in FY2025, versus 1 award of $180K in FY2023 (first 50 of 129 awards only). A Fed360 search snippet puts all-agency obligations at about $5.0M in FY2023, $3.7M in FY2024 and $0.5M in FY2025. FY2026 is net negative. Award count held near 18-19 while dollars fell, so average order size shrank. That points to a shrinking federal research budget, not to a shift of share to cheap providers. It is therefore mostly evidence against the idea that federal outsourcing is growing.
items.why_new: No federal award data on low-cost sequencing providers is in the known corpus.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Novogene federal awards are small and falling: about $229K net across 33 awards in FY2025 versus about $301K across 17 awards in FY2024.
items.detail: The first 50 of 204 awards show the average order shrank from about $18K to about $7K net, and USDA and HHS are the main buyers. FY2025 VA awards net to -$181K because of one $156.5K de-obligation. Award counts doubled while dollars fell, so the average order is much smaller. That is consistent with research buyers sending many small orders, but it is far too small to move Illumina's numbers.
items.why_new: First federal award counts and dollars for Novogene, with no equivalent in the known corpus.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: UCLA's NovaSeq 6000 S4-300 lane price in Aug 2023 can be set against its 2024 X Plus 25B-300 lane price. This is a one-core price series.
items.detail: The search summary of the 1 Aug 2023 sheet says S4-300 was $4,817 internal, $5,057 JCCC and $5,313 external for-profit per lane. It says the 1 Mar 2024 sheet had X Plus 25B-300 at $3,168 internal, $3,538 JCCC and $3,933 external for-profit. That is a lane-to-lane cut of about 34% internal and 26% external for-profit. A 25B lane holds much more output than an S4 lane, so $/Gb fell far more. Unverified: this comes from a search summary, and I did not confirm that the lanes are comparable.
items.source_name: UCLA Technology Center for Genomics & Bioinformatics rate sheets (search-result summary)
items.why_new: Gives dated 2023 and 2024 internal and external lane prices at one core, with the S4 to 25B step. The known list has only the 1 Jul 2026 UCLA $3.51/lane.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: UCLA's external for-profit 25B-300 lane price may have fallen from $3,933 (Mar 2024) to about $3,512 (2026), but the tier of the 2026 figure is unconfirmed.
items.detail: The Mar 2024 and Jun 2024 sheets list external for-profit at $3,933 and internal at $3,168. The current page lists 25B-300 at $3,512.47, which matches F856 (the 1 Jul 2026 external figure). If the tiers match, that is about −10.7% over roughly 28 months, or about −4.6% a year. If the 2026 price is a lower tier, the cut is smaller or the series is not comparable. This is a modest decline, not the 'insane discounts' the thesis expects. It cuts both ways on thesis 2B.
items.why_new: Quantifies a 2024-to-2026 same-lane change at one core. Prior notes had only the 2026 point.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: In Taiwan public procurement, Element's channel won about NT$51.5M (about US$1.6M) of AVITI/AVITI24 instrument awards in 2024–26, plus a NT$13.3M AVITI24 reagent contract that locks in NTU through 2028.
items.detail: There were four single-bid awards. Academia Sinica bought an AVITI24 for NT$15.31M (BRCAS11347, Nov 2024; the corrected notice names Element Biosciences Inc. as the winner). NTU College of Medicine bought an AVITI24 for NT$17.0M (1143A010, Jul 2025). Chi Mei Medical Center bought a 'high-throughput NGS sequencer' for NT$9.96M (114B01342H1, Feb 2026). Academia Sinica IMB bought an 'AVITI mid-throughput platform' for NT$9.2M (115-IMBE016, May 2026). The sum is 15.31+17.0+9.96+9.2 = NT$51.47M. NTU then signed an open AVITI24 reagent contract for NT$13.318M (1143A024, 9 Dec 2025 to 31 Dec 2028) under Procurement Act Art. 22(1)(4), the clause for follow-on compatible supplies, so a rival platform now has a captive multi-year consumables stream at a flagship research university.
items.quote: AVITI24定序平台專用試劑一批(至117.12.31止)(開口合約)
items.why_new: F747/F748 named Element's Taiwan awards but not their NT$ values, the total, or the 3-year reagent lock-in at NTU.
items.verify_note: This largely aggregates the known F747 and F748. The new element is the NTU AVITI24 open reagent contract (NT$13.318M, 9 Dec 2025 to 31 Dec 2028, Art. 22(1)(4)). The Chi Mei unit has no brand, so the confirmed Element total is NT$41.5M and NT$51.5M is an upper bound. Note that F870 and F885 use different Chinese names for the vendor (亞洲準誠 vs 亞洲準譯). The NOWnews article confirms 亞洲準譯.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: One NTU AVITI24 reagent contract (~NT$4.4M a year) is about twice Taipei VGH's whole Illumina high-throughput reagent lot (~NT$2.0M a year).
items.detail: NTU's AVITI24 reagent award is NT$13.318M over about 3.06 years (Dec 2025–Dec 2028), or about NT$4.35M a year. Taipei VGH's two-year 'high-throughput sequencing reagent set' lot from Illumina's distributor 均泰 is NT$3.942M (1140732E item 1, Nov 2025), or about NT$1.97M a year. That lot itself was down from NT$6.67M for 29 sets in Dec 2023 (1120652Y). A single research-lab reagent budget on a rival platform now exceeds a medical center's Illumina HT reagent spend. The comparison covers one research site and one clinical site, not the market.
items.why_new: This is the first rival-platform reagent spend set against an Illumina reagent lot in the same procurement system.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Element is not buying Taiwan research share on instrument price: AVITI24 awards landed at ~US$475–540K, close to budget, by single-bid restricted tender.
items.detail: Academia Sinica paid NT$15.31M against a NT$15.827M budget (−3.3%, about US$474K). NTU paid NT$17.0M against NT$17.1M (−0.6%), and Element's channel had originally bid NT$19.6M. Neither shows the deep instrument discounting that would signal an aggressive price war in research. The pressure shows up as share diversification, not as falling rival prices.
items.why_new: These are the first AVITI24 transaction prices and budget-to-award gaps from public records.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Illumina's 2023 Taiwan clinical-mNGS partner, Asia Pathogenomics, is now Element's Taiwan channel and holds several public-hospital infectious-disease NGS contracts.
items.detail: In Aug 2023 Asia Pathogenomics (亞洲準譯), Taiwan's first LDT-certified NGS lab, signed an MOU with Illumina Taiwan for infectious-disease mNGS (metagenomic sequencing, which identifies pathogens directly from a patient sample). By 2024–26 it sold all four Element instruments above, and its CTO presented infection testing on Element AVITI (LinkedIn post seen as a search snippet). Its public clinical mNGS awards include NTUH Cancer Center NT$8.72M (AH150140, Dec 2026–Nov 2027), Taipei VGH NT$3.73M over 2 years (X11414E, Nov 2025), NCKU Hospital and Taoyuan Hospital. Which sequencer runs these clinical tests is not verified.
items.quote: 簽訂合作備忘錄（MOU）
items.why_new: It was not previously known that Illumina's clinical mNGS partner is now Element's distributor and runs a clinical outsourcing book.
items.verify_note: Verified: the NOWnews article (2 Aug 2023) says 亞洲準譯 signed an mNGS MOU with Illumina's Taiwan branch at the Asia Biotech Expo. It is new that a former Illumina clinical partner is now Element's channel. The sequencer behind its hospital mNGS contracts is not verified, and the CTO's Element presentation is only a search snippet. So clinical displacement is not shown. It is a channel-defection anecdote.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Clinical infectious-disease mNGS outsourcing shrank sharply at two Taiwanese public hospitals, though one new cancer-center contract offsets part of it.
items.detail: At NCKU Hospital the award was NT$9.52M for Nov 2024–Nov 2025 (Y11349). The next award was NT$0.573M for Mar–Dec 2026 (Y11510), about NT$0.72M annualized, or −92%. At Taoyuan Hospital the award was NT$2.71M over 2 years for 80 tests (AA1130015, ~NT$1.36M a year), then NT$1.391M over 3 years (KA115051304, ~NT$0.46M a year), or −66%. Against that, NTUH Cancer Center signed a new NT$8.72M one-year contract (AH150140). Other NCKU lots may exist, so this is suggestive only.
items.why_new: This is the first mNGS (infectious NGS) clinical volume series; earlier items covered WGS, NIPT and exome only.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Clinical mNGS is priced per read depth at Taoyuan Hospital, and extra depth is cheap: 60M more reads add only ~NT$9,500 (~US$300).
items.detail: The Taoyuan Hospital APGseq contract (AA1130015, Sep 2024) priced a 40M-read test at NT$28,500 (40 tests), a 100M-read test at NT$38,000 (20 tests) and a 40M+40M test at NT$40,500 (20 tests). The step from 40M to 100M reads is NT$9,500 for 60M reads, about NT$158 (≈US$5) per million reads at the margin. Most of the test price is fixed workflow cost, not sequencing, which fits the view that sequencing price is not the binding constraint.
items.why_new: This is the first public tiered depth-priced clinical NGS schedule found.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Kaohsiung VGH started two outsourced WGS programs (~460 genomes in 2026), both at the NT$12,800 floor, and they are trivial in Gb terms.
items.detail: The oral-cancer WGS award was 210 units for NT$2.688M (ST1411027, Dec 2025; single bidder Genomics BioSci after one failed tender), or NT$12,800 a genome. The women's-medicine WGS award was 250 units for NT$3.2M (ST1412017, Jan 2026), also NT$12,800. At ~100–125 Gb per 30x genome, 460 genomes is ~46–58K Gb, about 0.006–0.007% of the ~800M Gb HT base. That makes five Taiwanese awards at exactly NT$12,800.
items.why_new: Kaohsiung VGH's oral-cancer WGS program and its genome count were not in the corpus. Earlier items covered Taipei/Taichung VGH, NTUH and TMU.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: NHRI, Taiwan's main public research institute, raised its whole-exome library-kit buying from Illumina's distributor by 72% y/y in 2026.
items.detail: The 全外顯子建庫試劑組 award was NT$1.999M in Jul 2025 (114A0C0138) and NT$3.43M in Aug 2026 (115A0C0221). Both were single-bid restricted tenders won by 均泰 (Genetech), with Singapore-origin content (Illumina manufacturing). The rise comes while NHRI's outsourced sequencing budget fell ~71% (F846), so this may be insourcing rather than new demand. Either way, Illumina-channel research spend at this buyer grew in 2026.
items.why_new: NHRI's exome-prep spend trend was not in the corpus, which only had its S4 kits, service and outsourced WGS.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: NHRI's NovaSeq 6000 S4 kit price fell ~66% from Jul 2020 to Dec 2023, and its annual kit count fell ~72%.
items.detail: In Jul 2020 NHRI bought 32 S4 (300-cycle) kits directly from Illumina Inc. for NT$17,337,600 (09GD-0001; USD award at 30.1), or ~NT$541,800 (~US$18.0K) per kit. In Dec 2023 it bought 16 S4 v1.5 kits from Illumina Taiwan for NT$2,929,920 (112A0C0676), or ~NT$183,120 (~US$5.8K) per kit, down 66%. 2020 volume was 32 + 25 kits (Jul and Dec awards) = 57, against 16 in 2023. The 2020 per-kit figure is unusually high against US list and may bundle other items, so treat it with caution.
items.why_new: It adds the Jul 2020 direct-from-Illumina datapoint to F712/D067, which started at Dec 2020.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Illumina's distributor keeps winning Taiwan public sequencer systems uncontested in 2025: three single-bid awards totalling NT$28.55M.
items.detail: The CDC pathogen-WGS automated library and sequencing system went for NT$17.9M (KA114028, Jun 2025; budget 19.84M), TFDA's high-throughput NGS system for NT$5.6M (114TFDA-A-512, May 2025; budget 5.8M), and NTUH Yunlin's high-throughput sequencer for NT$5.05M (YL-A24008, May 2025; budget 5.35M). Each had one bidder (均泰), with awards 3.4–9.8% under budget. Taiwan's public-health and regulatory labs show no rival tendering for core systems. Models are not stated.
items.why_new: It quantifies the specific CDC, TFDA and NTUH Yunlin system awards. F763 was general.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Taiwanese clinical exome outsourcing shows bid gaps of ~29% between labs once there is competition.
items.detail: Taipei City Hospital's 2024 WES contract (F113032, Oct 2024–Jul 2027) had three bidders. 台基盟 won at NT$1.782M against two rivals at NT$2.52M each (−29%) and against a NT$2.7M budget (−34%). The next WES award (R115092, Aug 2026) was single-bid at NT$0.6M to Genomics BioSci. Outsourcer margins compress sharply when bids are contested, and that pressure flows back to reagent pricing.
items.why_new: This is a new buyer (Taipei City Hospital) and the first contested WES bid gap; F785 covered NIPT only.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Illumina's own end-of-life policy bars service contracts on resold end-of-sale or end-of-life instruments. A third-party aftermarket cannot prop up a retired 6000 tail.
items.detail: Policy CN 1107421 (effective 18 Jul 2024) says pre-owned End-of-Sale/End-of-Life instruments 'are not eligible for service contracts' except for a title transfer without relocation, or an M&A transfer. Approval for service on resold units needs the Regional GM and is granted 'only in extraordinary circumstances'. This fits the search finding of no independent service vendor for the 6000. It means that once a 6000 end-of-sale notice is issued, the clock on the tail becomes hard.
items.quote: not eligible for service contracts
items.why_new: Known list covers the retirement page and MiSeq dates, not the policy's resale-service bar or the pricing mechanics.
items.verify_note: Verified in policy CN 1107421 (effective 18 Jul 2024), §4. The policy applies only to resold, pre-owned instruments after end of sale or end of life. It does not cover existing owners. It also says Illumina 'will not refuse to support an instrument solely because it was the subject of a third-party resale', and it can still supply billable services and consumables with approval. The finding therefore limits a secondhand 6000 market after an end-of-sale notice. It does not make the tail clock har

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Illumina's end-of-life policy mechanics give a firm timetable once a 6000 notice is issued: 5 years of service after the notice, with service prices rising from the notice date.
items.detail: The policy says the End-of-Service-Life date 'typically will be five (5) years after the End-of-Life notice date' for RUO and Dx instruments, and it can be shorter. The Last Ship date comes 2–6 months after the end-of-sale notice for RUO instruments and at least 6 months for Dx. Service contract offers 'are subject to price increases from the End-of-Life notice date'. Contracts are renewable only up to 12 months before EOSL, and Illumina may discontinue individual consumable kits earlier if demand is low. A mid-2027 notice would imply EOSL around mid-2032. This is a more formal basis than the earlier extrapolation of service to ~2031–32, and it adds the consumable-kit discontinuation risk.
items.quote: five (5) years after the End-of-Life notice date
items.why_new: The earlier 2031–32 date was labeled our extrapolation. This is the policy text behind it, plus the kit-discontinuation and service-price-increase terms.
items.verify_note: Verified in §2: the end-of-service-life date is 'typically… five (5) years after the End-of-Life notice date', and it 'may be shorter' or can be extended case by case. Last Ship is 2–6 months after notice for RUO and at least 6 months for Dx. Service contract offers are subject to price increases from the notice date, renewals are allowed up to 12 months before end of service life, and individual consumable kits may be discontinued early if demand is low. Caveat on direction: the five-year windo

items.label: 1A
items.claim: A 2018-built 6000 is listed in the UK at £8,000 for spares or repair, with the control software failing at 94% initialisation.
items.detail: UniGreenScheme (Universal Resource Trading) lists the unit at £8,000 ex-VAT (£9,600 inc.). It powers on, is cosmetically good, and has a PAT test dated 24 Nov 2025. A second listing at £7,950 was seen in search results only. At £8K the unit is about 1% of the $985K launch price. Software faults on an 8-year-old unit that no third party services point to Illumina-only repair, which supports the view that the 6000 base shrinks through scrapping.
items.why_new: Adds a dated, named, fault-described unit to the generic used-price range already known.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Government buyers explicitly justify Illumina-only 6000 service by saying third-party providers do not exist or are too slow, so there is no independent aftermarket.
items.detail: The CDC sole-source notice (posted 10 Oct 2024, covering 7 Dec 2024–6 Dec 2025, est. $144,910.12 for NovaSeq 6000 plus MiSeq) calls third-party service insufficient because of 'longer timelines and procedural delays'. The Navy NMRC notice (22 Dec 2025) cites market research 'confirming the absence of alternative service providers'. Per a search snippet, it prices the Silver plan at $141,313. The NCI notice (14 Aug 2026) is sole-source under FAR 6.302-1. Illumina keeps 100% of 6000 service revenue at these accounts, at roughly $140–145K per box per year.
items.quote: third-party services insufficient
items.why_new: Known list has the Navy, NCI and NIEHS notices. The CDC dollar estimate, the third-party wording and the NMRC $141K figure are new.
items.verify_note: This is new as procurement evidence that third-party 6000 service is absent, and it fits F896 and the known F619. Correction: the CDC figure of $144,910 covers a NovaSeq 6000 plus a MiSeq, so it is not a per-6000 price. The Navy $141,313 comes from a snippet. A fair range is about $110–141K per 6000 per year (NHRI F800 ~US$110K). Service retention says little about the consumables mix shift, so the link to 1A is indirect: owners cannot extend boxes cheaply outside Illumina.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: A federal 6000 service solicitation (NIA, Mar 2025) was posted as full and open, but it still required certified Illumina technicians, so the market is effectively sole-source.
items.detail: Solicitation 75N95025Q00163 (posted 5 Mar 2025, closed 19 Mar, performance 13 Apr–12 Oct 2025, a six-month term) requires 'certified Illumina technicians', parts, labor, travel, a 4-hour remote response and a 3-day on-site target. The six-month period is unusual against the annual cycles elsewhere. It suggests a bridge contract, possibly for a 6000 on its way out at the NIA, though that is an inference.
items.why_new: Not in the known list. It is an NIA six-month 6000 service contract in 2025.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Illumina's end-of-life policy says it may discontinue individual consumable kits on a retiring instrument when demand is low, a lever that could force 6000 users to the X.
items.detail: The policy says that during the EOL period Illumina should continue to supply consumables, but 'if demand is low and/or availability of materials is limited, Illumina may discontinue any individual Instrument Consumable kit(s) at any time'. It also says Illumina may 'allocate at its discretion' in cases of limited supply. This gives Illumina a lever to pull the 6000 tail onto X, but it may also trigger rivals' pitches (Novogene already ended 6000 support on 1 Jun 2025).
items.quote: may discontinue any individual Instrument Consumable kit(s)
items.why_new: The policy text on kit discontinuation is not in the known list.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Third-party resale does not produce a serviced 6000 secondary market, because Illumina reserves service priority and may refuse to restore operability on pre-owned boxes.
items.detail: The policy lets Illumina weigh buyer purchase volume, existing install base and the business need for the instrument when deciding whether to serve a pre-owned instrument. It says it 'does not guarantee that a pre-owned … instrument can be restored to operability'. Combined with $8K–$60K asking prices and no ISO found, a buyer of a used 6000 relies on Illumina's goodwill for service and kits, which Illumina can deny. Illumina therefore controls whether the used-6000 market becomes a source of new low-volume consumables demand.
items.quote: does not guarantee that a pre-owned
items.why_new: Not in the known list. It addresses whether the used market can extend the tail.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Taiwan's births fell 20% in 2025 and another ~15% in Jan–Aug 2026, a hard cap on NIPT volume that matches the ~17% drop in contracted tests at Taipei VGH.
items.detail: MOI household-registration data, as reported by the press: 2025 births were 107,812, down 27,044 (−20%) from 134,856 in 2024, the 10th straight annual decline. Jan–Aug 2026 births were 61,742, about 11K fewer than the same period of 2025 (~−15%, our estimate from the reported figures). Feb 2026 was the first month ever below 7,000 (6,523, −37% y/y). Hospital NIPT contracts that are being renewed with fewer tests per year (above) are consistent with a shrinking pregnancy pool, not with saturation alone.
items.source_name: Ministry of the Interior birth statistics via PeopleNews / CNA / UDN
items.quote: 2025年新生兒不到11萬人續創新低
items.why_new: The corpus has no birth-denominator data for any NIPT market. This one is falling 15–20% a year.
items.verify_note: Verified: PeopleNews gives 2025 births of 107,812 vs 134,856 in 2024 (-20%). Its latest monthly figure is Dec 2025 (9,027), so the Jan–Aug 2026 ~-15% and the Feb 2026 6,523 figure are unverified at this URL. Taiwan is a tiny share of Illumina's NIPT Gb (see D077), so this only explains the local contract declines (F782/F801). It does not show market-wide NIPT maturation. The cited '~17% drop at Taipei VGH' does not match a verified item.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: NYCU Hospital's annualized NIPT outsourcing fell about 27% between its 2024–26 and 2026–28 contracts, and the work was consolidated onto one vendor.
items.detail: 2024–26: 112114L99 '38-item' NIPT NT$12.72M (Bionet, 2 yrs) + 112112L99 2nd-gen NIPT NT$3.708M (Taiwan Advance Bio-Pharm, 2 yrs) = NT$8.21M/yr. 2026–28: 115306L54 38-item NT$1.496M for 1 yr (Bionet, limited tender, Feb 2026) + 115108L54 blood NIPT NT$8.984M over 2 yrs (Bionet, Apr 2026) = ~NT$5.99M in the first year (1.496 + 4.492), which is −27%. No 2026 successor to the 2nd-gen lot was found. All awards had a single bidder. The lots' scopes may not map 1:1, so the comparison is directional.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC e-procurement via pcc-api.openfun.app (NYCU Hospital 112112L99, 112114L99, 115306L54, 115108L54)
items.why_new: The NYCU Hospital NIPT series is not in the known list. The strategist named 115306L54 but did not mine it.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Bauer's FY27 10B NovaSeq X lane prices are flat to up at every read length, so the cheapest X flow cells show no further price cuts.
items.detail: FY27 10B lane prices are $1,030 / $1,193 / $1,314 at 100 / 200 / 300 cycles, effective 1 Jul 2026 to 30 Jun 2027. The FY26 100-cycle price was $1,011, so the FY27 price is +1.9%. The 300-cycle price is +0.8%, which matches the earlier T665 reading. The 1.5B 100-cycle lane went from $1,288 to $1,679, +30.4% (1679/1288). A core's internal rate is a pass-through of Illumina's net kit price, so this is consistent with Illumina not cutting small X flow-cell prices in 2026.
items.source_name: Harvard Bauer Core FY27 NGS Sequencing (search-result snippet; the page returned 403 to fetch)
items.why_new: T665 had 10B 300-cycle +0.8%; the 100-cycle 10B and 1.5B 100-cycle moves are new.
items.verify_note: Restates F768/F775, which already give 10B 100c $1,011→$1,030, 10B 300c +0.8% and 1.5B up. Nothing new.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: The 25B's per-read advantage over the 10B differs a lot by read length, and it is largest at 100 cycles, so price steps within the X are deepest where a 35B-style cut would land.
items.detail: FY27 per million reads, using the page's stated reads per lane (25B 2.5B, 10B 1.0B): 100-cycle 25B $0.561 vs 10B $1.030, so the 25B is 45.5% cheaper. 200-cycle is $0.857 vs $1.193, 28.2% cheaper. 300-cycle is $0.970 vs $1.314, 26.2% cheaper. The ~26% narrowing the strategist noted at 300 cycles is confirmed. The 100-cycle 25B lane is flagged 'infrequently run', so that price is less meaningful.
items.source_name: Harvard Bauer Core FY27 NGS Sequencing (snippet)
items.why_new: T665 and F777 cover the 300-cycle 10B/25B premium only. The 100- and 200-cycle discounts are new.
items.verify_note: Arithmetic checks: 1403/2.5=$0.561 vs $1.030; 2143/2.5=$0.857 vs $1.193; 2426/2.5=$0.970 vs $1.314. The 'supports' framing does not hold. The 25B's per-read discount to the 10B shrank y/y at both 200c and 300c (see derived item), and the only deep gap is at 100c, which the page flags as 'infrequently run'. Re-labelled 'against'. Partly overlaps F777.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Taipei City Hospital used up a 33-month NIPT contract in about 15 months after Taipei began subsidizing NIPT in 2025, needed a one-month bridge, then added a follow-on expansion. Subsidies can pull NIPT volume up even as births fall.
items.detail: R113118 awarded NT$2.6M (Sep 2024; two bidders) plus NT$1.666M (Sep 2024) = NT$4.266M, with a term 'to 30 Jun 2027 or until the ceiling is used up.' A restricted bridge award R114133E of NT$159.5K covered 10 Dec 2025–8 Jan 2026, which implies the ceiling ran out around Dec 2025. The follow-on expansion R113118-1 (Feb 2026) is NT$2.295M for Apr 2026–Jun 2029, so at the ~NT$3.4M/yr run-rate it would run out in about 8 months. Taipei City announced NIPT as a subsidized Down-syndrome screening option for resident pregnancies starting in 2025 (Taiwan News, 17 Dec 2024).
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC (Taipei City Hospital R113118, R114133E, R113118-1); Taiwan News
items.why_new: F783 had the run-rate only. The early exhaustion, the bridge, the expansion size and the subsidy driver are new.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: The 1.5B flow cell is priced at about 3.5x the 25B per read, so small X flow cells carry a very high $/Gb. That is the price tier most exposed to low-cost rivals and to reconsolidation onto larger flow cells.
items.detail: FY27 1.5B 300-cycle is $2,028 for 0.6B reads per lane, or $3.38 per million reads. The 25B 300-cycle is $2,426 for 2.5B reads per lane, or $0.97 per million, a ratio of 3.5x. The 10B is $1.31 and the 5B is $1.42 per million. The 1.5B costs more per lane than the 10B ($2,028 vs $1,314) at 300 cycles, the same pattern as at 100 and 200 cycles.
items.source_name: Harvard Bauer Core FY27 NGS Sequencing (snippet)
items.why_new: F770 gave the 5B/10B/25B per-read costs; the 1.5B per-read ratio to the 25B and the 1.5B-above-10B inversion are new.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Bauer offers no AVITI, Ultima or Roche SBX service in FY26 or FY27, so a Harvard core shows no rival-platform price pressure on research Illumina volume.
items.detail: The FY27 and FY26 NGS pages list only NovaSeq X Plus (25B, 10B, 5B, 1.5B), NextSeq 1000 and MiSeq. Searches of the core's pages found no AVITI, Ultima or SBX pricing. The long-read page lists only PacBio Revio. No NovaSeq 6000 row appears. Absence is inferred from snippets only, because the direct fetch was blocked.
items.why_new: F773 said the 6000 row was unseparated. This extends it to a no-AVITI/Ultima/SBX check on FY27.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Taipei VGH's largest NIPT lot (2025–28) went to Taiwan Genecare's NIFTY, the BGI-branded test, and it also absorbed twin testing previously held by a different vendor, so over half of this flagship hospital's NIPT dollars sit on a BGI-branded test.
items.detail: X11407E (Aug 2025): 'NIFTY (twins)' 180 tests and 'NIFTY PLUS (singleton, 39 items)' 360 tests, NT$9.612M over 3 yrs (NT$3.204M/yr), or ~54% of Taipei VGH's ~NT$5.98M/yr NIPT spend. In 2023–25, twins sat with Taiwan Advance Bio-Pharm (X11211H, NT$19,000/test). NIFTY is BGI's brand. That it runs on BGI/MGI (DNBSEQ) sequencers in Taiwan is our inference and was not verified in the notice.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC e-procurement (Taipei VGH X11407E, X11211H)
items.quote: 非侵入性胎兒基因染色體檢測-NIFTY PLUS（單胞胎）（39項）
items.why_new: No known item ties Taiwanese clinical NIPT volume to a BGI-branded test or quantifies its share.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Bauer's PacBio Revio cell price barely moved (−1.1%) in FY27, so long-read pricing shows no discounting pressure either, and long-read is about 7x Illumina's per-Gb cost.
items.detail: A FY27 Revio SMRT cell (25M) costs $1,564 internal and $2,190 PO, vs $1,581 / $2,213 in FY26 (−1.1%). The page describes the cell as about 90 Gb, so $17.4/Gb. The new Nx option (3 acquisitions) costs $2,578 internal. The FY26 25B 300-cycle was about $2.06 per Gb on 1,000 Gb, and the FY27 one is about $2.43, so long-read is roughly 7x. Kinnex prep fell from $1,605 to $1,543 (−3.9%).
items.source_name: Harvard Bauer Core FY27 Long Read page (snippet)
items.why_new: The FY27 long-read rows were the stated gap from T665.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Bauer's NextSeq 1000 P2 lane prices on an undated sheet are above the FY26 ones, so mid-throughput prices are not falling at this core.
items.detail: An undated Bauer NGS fee page lists P2 300-cycle at $3,759 internal vs $3,344 on the FY26 page (+12.4%), and P1 300-cycle at $1,451 vs $1,382 (+5.0%). The page may be the FY27 schedule but is not labelled. Combined with the flat or rising 10B, this suggests mid- and high-throughput consumables pricing is firm at this core.
items.source_name: Harvard Bauer Core NGS Sequencing page (snippet)
items.why_new: T665 did not cover NextSeq 1000 or MiSeq rows.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Even single-bidder NIPT awards are bargained 8–20% below budget at some Taiwanese hospitals, which qualifies F786's '95–100% of budget' finding.
items.detail: Taipei VGH X11415E (Nov 2025): budget NT$2.70M, Bionet bid NT$2.43M, award NT$2.16M (−20% vs budget, −11% vs bid). X11212H (Dec 2023): budget NT$2.16M → award NT$1.728M (−20%). NYCU 112114L99 (Jan 2024): budget NT$13.776M → NT$12.72M (−7.7%). Kinmen KM113B018 (Feb 2025): bid NT$2.626M → NT$2.428M (−7.5%). Against these, MOHW Taoyuan, Taichung VGH 114Y-R11 and NYCU 115108L54 landed at 100% of budget. Discounting therefore depends on the buyer, not on competition.
items.why_new: Adds buyer-level bargaining data that partly contradicts F786.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Taipei VGH's singleton basic-NIPT lot appears to have shrunk from 72 to about 60 tests a year, with the price per test held at NT$12,000.
items.detail: X11212H (2023–25): 144 tests at NT$12,000 on a budget of NT$2.16M (= 144 × NT$15,000). The successor X11415E (2025–28) was budgeted NT$2.70M 'based on recent years' usage' and awarded NT$2.16M. The same 15,000/12,000 budget-to-award pattern implies 180 tests over 3 yrs (60/yr, −17%) at NT$12,000. The notice gives no unit price, so this is our inference.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC e-procurement (Taipei VGH X11212H, X11415E)
items.quote: 依機關近年使用量，預估本案需求數量
items.why_new: This lot pair is not in the known list.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: MSK, which still deposits mostly 6000 series on GEO, now releases series that use the NovaSeq X and AVITI together, so it runs three platforms at once.
items.detail: GSE333562 (a genotyping SuperSeries with GIFT-seq, released 25 Sep 2026) lists GPL34281 (NovaSeq X) and GPL34295 (AVITI), with Memorial Sloan Kettering as contact institute. F604 found MSK's 6000 series still rising (52 in Jan–Sep 2026, 71% of 6000+X). MSK therefore spans the 6000, X and AVITI. That fits a large clinical-adjacent account that keeps the 6000 running while it tests other sequencers.
items.why_new: Adds an AVITI leg to MSK's known 6000/X split.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Roche's own research group (F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd) released a 40-sample bulk RNA-seq series on AVITI in Sep 2026.
items.detail: GSE308912 (engineered intestinal tissue fibrosis model, released 30 Sep 2026, 40 samples GSM9256164–9256203) lists GPL34295 and Roche as contact institute. The record does not name the instrument, and I could not tell whether the data came from Roche's internal labs or a service provider. It shows that a large buyer with its own SBX platform accepts Element data in routine RNA-seq, and that it is not exclusive to Illumina.
items.why_new: Names a pharma depositor on a rival record; none of the known items does.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: AVITI adopters in 2026 releases include several large US and European research institutes, which broadens the rival's research base beyond core facilities.
items.detail: Contact institutes on 2026 AVITI-only or AVITI-plus-Illumina series: Salk (Oct 2026), University of Iowa (Oct 2026), Columbia (Sep 2026), WEHI (Oct 2026), Cold Spring Harbor (Oct 2026), Boston Children's (Sep 2026), UC Davis Genome Center (Oct 2026), Stanford (Sep 2026), Sanford Burnham Prebys (Sep 2026), University of Geneva (Sep 2026) and Cornell's Pugh Lab (Jul 2026). Iowa is consistent with F795, where its microbiome core moved to AVITI. These are named depositors on the AVITI record, not price evidence.
items.why_new: Gives named institutional depositors; known items give only counts.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: A NSF MRI award funded an Element AVITI24 rather than an Illumina system at a university, one example of rival capital placement in research.
items.detail: NSF MRI Track 1 award 2511003 gave the University of Idaho $584,845 starting 15 Sep 2025 to acquire an Element AVITI system for multi-omics research and training. It is the only AVITI or Element award returned for 2023-2026. The same search returned no NovaSeq X, NovaSeq or Ultima awards, so NSF shows no platform-count trend. This is one data point, so the evidence is anecdotal.
items.quote: Acquisition of Element AVITI System to Enable Multi-Omics Research and Research Training
items.why_new: This is the first named NSF MRI award for an AVITI, and it is a rival-platform capital purchase in academia.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Under Illumina's own end-of-life policy and the MiSeq precedent, an end-of-sale notice cannot force the regulated NovaSeq 6000 tail off before about 2031, even if the notice came in early 2027. A 2027 conversion step would therefore have to come from economics or Illumina's price levers, not from the platform being retired.
items.detail: Policy CN 1107421 (Jul 2024) sets end of service life at 'typically five years' after the notice and Last Ship at least 6 months after notice for Dx instruments. The MiSeq was announced Mar 2025, with end of sale 30 Sep 2025 and service to 31 Dec 2029, which is about 4.75 years from notice and matches the rule. As of Oct 2026 the 6000 product page shows no notice. So a Q1'27 notice implies service and consumables to about Q4'31. The policy does give Illumina two levers that could pull conversion forward. Service prices can rise from the notice date, and individual 6000 kits can be discontinued early 'if demand is low'.
items.source_name: Illumina Product End-of-Life Policy 1000000117071 v01; Illumina retirement page (MiSeq)
items.quote: may discontinue any individual Instrument Consumable kit(s) at any time
items.why_new: The known ~2031–32 date was our own extrapolation. This ties it to the written policy, checks it against the MiSeq's 4.75-year actual, and adds two levers: post-notice service price increases and early kit discontinuation.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: The NTU AVITI24 reagent contract implies a ceiling of about US$140K a year in consumables for a single Element box. That is above Illumina's own FY26 pull-through guide for its competing NextSeq 1000/2000 ($80–100K), so research consumables dollars that leave Illumina are not trivial per site.
items.detail: NTU College of Medicine signed an AVITI24 open reagent contract (1143A024) for NT$13.318M covering 9 Dec 2025 to 31 Dec 2028, about 3.06 years. That works out to about NT$4.35M a year, or about US$140K at 31 NT$/US$, for the AVITI24 it bought in Jul 2025 (NT$17.0M). Illumina guided FY26 NextSeq 1000/2000 pull-through at $80–100K and NextSeq 500/550 at $90–110K. Open contracts are estimated ceilings, not committed spend, so actual draw may be lower.
items.quote: AVITI24定序平台專用試劑一批(至117.12.31止)(開口合約)
items.why_new: Earlier items counted Element's Taiwan instrument wins. None turned the reagent contract into a per-box consumables run-rate or compared it with Illumina's mid-throughput pull-through guide.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Cancer/tumor-tagged GEO series are leaving the NovaSeq 6000 faster than non-cancer series, which contradicts a 'sticky clinical-adjacent tail' in public data.
items.detail: Human GEO series released in Q3'24 → Q3'25 → Q3'26 (cancer OR tumor OR tumour): 6000 series 764 → 791 → 794; X series (GPL34281) 10 → 51 → 131. The 6000 share of 6000+X fell 98.7% → 93.9% → 85.8% (−12.9 pts). The non-cancer remainder (all minus cancer) fell 616/641 = 96.1% → 650/722 = 90.0% → 853/973 = 87.7% (−8.4 pts). Intermediate cancer points: Q1'26 859/947 = 90.7%, Q2'26 795/889 = 89.4%. Caveats: X count is the plain 'NovaSeq X' GPL only and excludes X Plus GPLs. The 'cancer' keyword matches mostly research series, and tagged series are ~49% of all 6000 series in every quarter.
items.source_name: NCBI GEO via E-utilities (db=gds), GPL24676 vs GPL34281
items.why_new: Known items give only all-series 6000 share; this splits by oncology keyword and by quarter, and shows no slower decay.
items.verify_note: Direction corrected. The thesis is that the tail keeps converting and management's 'permanent tail' claim is wrong, so faster 6000 decay in cancer-tagged series supports 1A. It is weak evidence: (1) the X count uses only GPL34281 and omits X Plus GPLs (D065), which understates X share; (2) GEO is research deposits and says little about regulated clinical 6000 labs; (3) the absolute 6000 count is flat (764→794), so the share move is X addition, not 6000 retirement. Not checked by fetch.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Series that mention 'patient' or 'clinical' also show the 6000 share falling about 8 points in a year (93.5% → 85.5%), so there is no slower-decay clinical pocket.
items.detail: Keyword (patient OR patients OR clinical): Q3'25 6000 = 608, X = 42, so the 6000 share is 608/650 = 93.5%. Q3'26 6000 = 597, X = 101, so the share is 597/698 = 85.5%. The all-series share over the same period went 92.1% → 86.8% (−5.3 pts), so the clinical-keyword group fell somewhat faster. The 6000's absolute count in this group was flat (−1.8%), while X series rose 2.4x.
items.why_new: Adds a clinical-keyword cut and quantifies it against the all-series share.
items.verify_note: Direction corrected for the same reason as F919. The 'patient/clinical' keyword catches research papers, not clinical production labs. 6000 counts are flat (608→597), so this says more conversion is possible but no clinical-lab decay. Same X-Plus omission as F919. Largely overlaps F919.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Even in oncology-tagged public data, the 6000 still holds about 86% of series and its absolute count has not fallen, so the 6000 tail is not yet gone.
items.detail: Cancer-tagged 6000 series were 764 (Q3'24), 791 (Q3'25) and 794 (Q3'26), roughly flat. Conversion is coming from X additions (10 → 131), not from the 6000 shrinking. Quarterly 6000 cancer series: Q1'26 859, Q2'26 795, Q3'26 794, a slight drift down from Q1. The 6000 therefore stays the majority platform in oncology-adjacent public work, though the mix share is falling about 4–5 pts per quarter-year-end.
items.why_new: The oncology-tagged absolute 6000 series path (Q3'24–Q3'26) is new.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Public cfDNA/ctDNA sequencing on the 6000 and X is tiny and shows no growing liquid-biopsy research base in GEO.
items.detail: Series matching (cfDNA OR ctDNA OR 'cell-free' OR 'circulating tumor DNA'): Q3'24 6000 = 3, X = 1; Q3'25 6000 = 8, X = 2; Q3'26 6000 = 9, X = 0. That is 4, 10 and 9 series out of roughly 1,400–1,900 human 6000+X series per quarter, about 0.5%. The 6000 share (75%, 80%, 100%) is statistically meaningless at this n. Public GEO lags clinical lab work, and clinical labs rarely deposit, so it is a weak proxy for MRD Gb.
items.why_new: No known item counts cfDNA/ctDNA series on these platforms.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Whole-genome-tagged series on the 6000 and X are few and not growing, so WGS is not visible as a rising public Gb source.
items.detail: Series matching ('whole genome' OR WGS OR 'whole-genome'): Q3'24 6000 = 11, X = 0; Q3'25 6000 = 24, X = 3; Q3'26 6000 = 16, X = 5. The total fell from 27 (Q3'25) to 21 (Q3'26), −22%. The 6000 share was 100%, 88.9% and 76.2%. These are about 1% of human series, so they are tiny, but they show no WGS acceleration in public data.
items.why_new: Gives WGS-keyword series counts by platform, consistent with the known decline in WGS trial starts.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Rival sequencer vendors' share of direct US federal sequencer-vendor obligations rose to ~17% in FY2026 from ~10% in FY24–25, as rival obligations grew ~21% while Illumina's fell 29%.
items.detail: Sweetspot FY net obligations for Illumina / Element / PacBio / ONT: FY24 $35.64M / $0.51M / $2.48M / $0.75M, so rivals had 9.5% of $39.4M. FY25: $33.93M / $0.78M / $2.02M / $1.18M, so 10.5% of $37.9M. FY26: $23.97M / $0.75M / $1.87M / $2.21M, so 16.8% of $28.8M. Rivals together went $3.98M → $4.83M (+21%). The trend is not monotone: FY23 was 15.7%, driven by a $6.0M PacBio year. Ultima adds ~$0.17M in FY25 and nothing in FY26. Distributor purchases are excluded for all vendors.
items.source_name: Sweetspot GovCon directory (Illumina, Element, PacBio, ONT profiles)
items.why_new: This is the first cross-vendor share series for US federal buyers; known evidence covers only Canadian federal and Taiwanese tenders.
items.verify_note: New dataset. The base is tiny: ~$29M of direct federal obligations, under 1% of Illumina revenue. Distributor purchases (e.g. Government Scientific Source on GSA) are excluded, and Illumina is more likely than rivals to sell through distributors, so the 29% Illumina drop may be channel shift. FY26 (ended 30 Sep) may still be missing late-reported actions. The trend is non-monotone (FY23 15.7%). Treat as directional only.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Element's direct federal obligations keep rising, reaching ~3% of Illumina+Element in FY26, including an AVITI24 for NCI's Center for Cancer Research and bulk USDA AVITI kit buys.
items.detail: Element net obligations were $0.40M (FY22), $0.61M (FY23), $0.51M (FY24), $0.78M (FY25) and $0.75M (FY26), with award actions rising to 7 in FY26 from 4. Element/(Illumina+Element) went 1.4% (FY24) → 2.2% (FY25) → 3.0% (FY26). Recent awards: $315K AVITI24 'to enhance shared research capabilities' of NCI CCR (23 Sep 2026; PIID 140D0426P0333, which the page attributes to Interior); USDA 120 AVITI 2x150 kits for $148K (2 Sep 2026); a $135K AVITI→AVITI24 upgrade (9 Jul 2026); and a USDA device-upgrade IDIQ (1232SA26D0020). The base is very small in absolute terms.
items.why_new: Element's US federal award trajectory and the NCI CCR AVITI24 buy are not in the known list.
items.verify_note: Correction: Element's obligations did not 'keep rising'. They were flat to down ($0.78M FY25 → $0.75M FY26). Its share rose only because Illumina's fell. The award count rose 4→7. The NCI CCR AVITI24 sits under an Interior (IBC-assisted) PIID, so attribution to NCI rests on the description. Named-site wins (NCI CCR, USDA) are the new part. Overlaps F924.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: NHLBI's TOPMed CORE 2.0 sequencing contracts ($500M ceiling each, 10-year ordering) are only 2–8% used after three years.
items.detail: HigherGov IDV pages show the following. Broad 75N92023D00013: $38.15M obligated, 7–8% of $500M (last modified 30 Jul 2026). Baylor 75N92023D00012: $42.21M, 8% used, potential task-order value $74.8M. NYGC 75N92023D00016: $9.19M, 2% used, funded backlog $0. Ordering runs from Sep 2023 to Sep 2033. Sweetspot puts total CORE 2.0 obligations at $93.3M across 15 task orders and 9 holders; Cedars-Sinai, UCSD and Vanderbilt have $0, and Psomagen has $72.6K. That is roughly $31M a year, about level with the predecessor CORE vehicle ($158.8M over its life).
items.source_name: HigherGov IDV records; Sweetspot vehicle page
items.why_new: TOPMed CORE ceiling use and annual run-rate are not among the known funding evidence (NIH, All of Us, GREGoR).
items.verify_note: New. IDIQ ceilings are routinely set far above expected use, so 2–8% use after 3 of 10 years mainly reflects ceiling inflation, not a funding cut. The useful fact is the run-rate: ~$31M/yr across CORE 2.0, flat vs the predecessor. That supports flat research volume more than tight funding. The predecessor-period comparison is not normalized for length.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: TOPMed CORE task orders to Broad and NYGC fell ~78% from FY24 to FY25 and stayed low in FY26, so the flagship NHLBI omics program is lumpy and not growing.
items.detail: Broad TOPMed CORE task orders: $3.63M (Sep 2023), $24.48M (Sep 2024), $4.81M (Sep 2025), and FY26 about $5.2M (HigherGov $38.15M less the $32.92M through FY25). NYGC: $0.74M (FY23), $5.69M (FY24), $1.89M (FY25). The two combined went $4.4M → $30.2M → $6.7M. Baylor's FY26 order was $3.83M (28 Sep 2026). The FY24 spike may be multi-year funding, so this reads as no growth rather than a collapse.
items.source_name: GovCon in a Box (USAspending-derived) Broad/NYGC profiles; Sweetspot Baylor profile
items.why_new: There is no prior time series of TOPMed sequencing task orders at the big genome centers.
items.verify_note: New. As the item says, the FY24 spike is likely multi-year funding, so read it as 'no growth', not a decline. The FY26 Broad figure (~$5.2M) is derived by subtraction from HigherGov totals and is not itemized. Pairs with F926.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: NIH BICAN (brain-atlas) large-scale sequencing-core awards to Broad and NYGC were flat in nominal dollars from FY23 to FY25, so falling $/Gb turns into more data rather than more vendor revenue.
items.detail: Task order 75N95023F00002 shows NYGC at $8.96M (May 2023), $8.99M (May 2024) and $8.70M (May 2025, −3%), and Broad at $7.40M in each of May 2023, 2024 and 2025. These are fixed annual budgets for large-scale single-cell sequencing, the counting work Roche targets with AXELIOS. Flat dollars combined with falling price per read imply flat Illumina revenue at best.
items.why_new: BICAN sequencing-core funding levels are not in the known evidence.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Psomagen's federal obligations fell another ~82% in FY26 to $0.19M, and its NHLBI work moved from sequencing to Olink proteomics.
items.detail: Sweetspot: $1.30M (FY22), $5.03M (FY23), $3.20M (FY24), $1.06M (FY25), $0.19M (FY26, 21 actions). In the listed awards, eight NHLBI orders from Feb to Jul 2025 were Olink Explore HT proteomics (sickle cell, sepsis, including $229K), as were two more in May 2026 ($200K and $49K). Earlier awards were WGS and RNA-seq ($1.85M WGS, Sep 2024). USDA terminated a NovaSeq X sequencing order (−$21.3K, Feb 2025).
items.why_new: F881 covered FY24–FY25 only; the FY26 figure and the shift to proteomics are new.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Federal labs are not shifting research sequencing to the cheapest outsourcer: Novogene's net federal obligations were negative in FY26, though small sole-source awards continue.
items.detail: Sweetspot Novogene (UEI KM6KF2YEWNN6): $798K (FY22), $623K (FY23), $807K (FY24), $229K (FY25), −$309K (FY26, 26 actions, net of deobligations such as a −$157K VA cancer-research mRNA-seq order). New 2026 awards are still small: a VA Palo Alto sole-source RNA-seq ($18K, Aug 2026), an NIH pharmacogenomics order ($25K, Sep 2026) and an Interior wildlife-genomics order ($10K, Aug 2026). For federal buyers, the low-cost Chinese channel is shrinking, not taking share.
items.why_new: F882 had FY24–FY25 only; FY26 net deobligation and the 2026 award detail are new.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Oxford Nanopore's direct federal obligations nearly doubled in FY26 to $2.21M, now ~9% of Illumina's, so some federal research spend is moving to long-read.
items.detail: ONT net obligations: $2.77M (FY22), $1.95M (FY23), $0.75M (FY24), $1.18M (FY25), $2.21M (FY26, +88% y/y). ONT/Illumina went 2.1% (FY24) → 3.5% (FY25) → 9.2% (FY26). FY26 awards include a PromethION 2 Integrated platform at Interior (Sep 2026), an NCI methylation-profiling instrument with reagents ($100K, Sep 2026) and USDA flow cells ($203K). PacBio was flat to down: $2.48M → $2.02M → $1.87M.
items.why_new: There is no prior US federal ONT/PacBio obligation trend; the known evidence has Taiwan CDC nanopore spend only.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Ultima has almost no US federal footprint: $166K across two FY25 NIH orders, nothing in FY26, and one $1.03M UG100 purchase in 2021.
items.detail: Sweetspot (UEI DXEVRGJ7MW28) lists $1.19M lifetime across 3 awards, all HHS: a UG100-V sequencer for $1.025M (Sep 2021), NHGRI library reagent for $19.9K (May 2025) and 'Purchase of Ultima Genomics reagents' for $146.5K (Aug 2025). That compares with Illumina's $24M in FY26 direct obligations. Ultima's low-price threat is not visible in federal procurement.
items.quote: PURCHASE OF ULTIMA GENOMICS REAGENTS, NEW PO
items.why_new: Ultima's federal award history is not in the known list.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: 10x Genomics' direct federal obligations dropped to $3.9M in FY26 from $10.7M in FY25, a sign of weaker federal single-cell spend, which drives Illumina counting volume.
items.detail: Sweetspot 10x: $8.46M (FY22), $8.39M (FY23), $8.03M (FY24), $10.74M (FY25), $3.92M (FY26 YTD, 57 actions vs 172). Award actions fell 67%. The page metadata says it was last updated Jul 2026 but lists Sep 2026 awards, so FY26 may be incomplete; treat as directional.
items.why_new: The known list has the 10x academic commentary but no federal procurement series.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Among Illumina's 50 most recent federal awards (Sep 2025–Dec 2025), NovaSeq X kit orders outnumber 6000 kit orders 6 to 1, so the federal research 6000 consumables tail is nearly gone.
items.detail: GovCon in a Box lists one NovaSeq 6000 SP reagent kit order ($52K, 24 Sep 2025). NovaSeq X orders: $211K, $234K (IVD X kits), $149K, $75K (25B/10B plus P3 XLEAP), $35K, and a MiSeq/X Plus line. The remaining tail spend in this sample is MiSeq and NextSeq service plans, which fits the research conversion of ~92% already known. The sample covers 50 of 2,848 awards.
items.why_new: The known federal evidence is 6000 service plans (F613–F622); the kit-order mix in US federal awards is new.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: The US birth denominator for NIPT is shrinking, and the shrinkage accelerated through mid-2026.
items.detail: The CDC 12-month-ending general fertility rate fell from 54.6 per 1,000 women aged 15-44 (2024 Q4) to 53.7 (2025 Q2), 53.3 (2025 Q4), 53.0 (2026 Q1) and 52.7 (2026 Q2). The y/y decline was -1.5% at 2026 Q1 and -1.9% at 2026 Q2, versus the -1% headline for full-year 2025 (3,606,400 births). A falling denominator caps NIPT test growth for the whole market, since the ACMG first-line recommendation and 70-80% penetration leave little room to add tests.
items.url: https://data.cdc.gov/resource/76vv-a7x8.json?$where=indicator='15-44 years' AND race_ethnicity='All races and origins'&$order=year_and_quarter DESC
items.source_name: CDC NCHS VSRR Quarterly provisional estimates for selected birth indicators (data.cdc.gov)
items.why_new: Gives the 2026 Q1 and Q2 quarterly fertility-rate trend (-1.5% and -1.9% y/y); known notes cite only the 2025 -1% figure.
items.verify_note: Same dataset as F940, with an arithmetic error. The data show Q1'25 GFR at 54.5 and Q1'26 at 53.0, so y/y is -2.8%, not -1.5%. F940 has it right. Duplicate.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Births to older mothers, the highest-intensity NIPT cohort, are still rising, which partly cushions test volume.
items.detail: The CDC birth rate for women aged 35-39 rose from 54.0 (2024 Q2) to 54.6 (2025 Q2) and 55.4 (2026 Q2), about +1.5% y/y. The rate for women aged 40-44 rose from 12.6 to 12.7 to 12.9. Older mothers are more likely to get NIPT and to get follow-on tests, so the mix partly offsets the falling overall GFR.
items.url: https://data.cdc.gov/resource/76vv-a7x8.json?$where=(indicator='35-39 years' OR indicator='40-44 years') AND race_ethnicity='All races and origins'
items.source_name: CDC NCHS VSRR quarterly provisional estimates (data.cdc.gov)
items.why_new: Offers an official-data watch-out on age mix for the NIPT-maturing argument; not in the known notes.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Illumina still has no NovaSeq X Dx or X-based IVD support page, and 6000Dx IVD documentation was still being revised in 2026, so regulated Illumina-kit labs have no IVD path off the 6000.
items.detail: The 6000Dx support documentation page shows the DNA Prep with Enrichment Dx insert revised on 9 Apr 2026 (US/Canada, 200014829_02) and 5 Mar 2026 (EEA, 200038118_01), with translations through 19 May 2026. RUO DRAGEN DNA Prep with Enrichment documentation on the 6000Dx is dated 12 Aug 2026. The page names no NovaSeq X Dx, and the IVD instrument list is MiSeqDx, NextSeq 550Dx and 6000Dx only.
items.why_new: The known list covers PMA sequencer names and the 6000Dx (2022) but not the 2026 6000Dx IVD document revisions or the absence of an X Dx page.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: 6000Dx software has had no release for about 26 months (Software Suite v2.4.0, Aug 2024), which is neither new development nor end-of-life.
