items.detail: Downloads page: DRAGEN Germline v1.0.8 and BCL Convert v1.0.4 (both on Suite v2.4.0) are dated 13 Aug 2024. The prior generation (v2.3.1) is dated 6 Nov 2023, and DNA Prep with Enrichment DRAGEN 1.2.37 is dated 23 Jan 2024. The cadence is about one release per 9-10 months through 2024, then nothing. There is no end-of-support notice on the page. The stall is ambiguous. It could mean a mature platform, or investment shifting away from the 6000Dx.
items.why_new: The 6000Dx software release cadence and the 26-month gap are not in the known list.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: GEO HTS series count accelerated to +34.7% y/y in Q3'26 (+17% a year earlier), while samples per series fell, so growth is broad-based rather than driven by mega-series.
items.detail: HTS GSE (series) counts: Q3'23 6,229; Q3'24 5,667; Q3'25 6,631 (+17.0%); Q3'26 8,929 (+34.7%). Samples per series: Q3'24 22.9, Q3'25 22.1, Q3'26 18.3 (162,994/8,929). That is −17% y/y, so more, smaller studies. The unit choice matters: Q3'23 had 756,087 HTS samples from 6,229 series (121 per series), a mega-series distortion that makes Q3'23 unusable as a base.
items.why_new: This adds a series-vs-sample cross-check, the Q3'23 mega-series outlier, and a samples-per-series trend.
items.verify_note: Partly overlaps D058 (GEO HT samples +25%) and F721 (expression series +42%). The series-count angle and falling samples per series are new. GEO deposits lag sequencing by roughly 6–18 months and count studies, not Gb. D060 shows Gb-weighted public NovaSeq output only +12% y/y, so this overstates volume acceleration. Mainly research, so 2A/2B are also relevant.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: The US birth denominator for NIPT is shrinking faster in 2026 than the 2025 headline shows: the 12-month-ending general fertility rate fell from 54.5 (Q1'25) to 53.0 (Q1'26) and from 53.7 (Q2'25) to 52.7 (Q2'26).
items.detail: These are NCHS VSRR 12-month-ending GFR figures per 1,000 females aged 15-44. The y/y drop is -2.8% in Q1'26 and -1.9% in Q2'26. Sequential steps were 54.5→54.6 (Q4'24)→53.3 (Q4'25)→53.0 (Q1'26)→52.7 (Q2'26), so the decline is ongoing, not a one-off. Scaling the confirmed 3,606,400 births in 2025 by 52.7/53.1 gives roughly 3.58M, or about 3.50-3.55M if the female 15-44 population is flat to slightly down. That is my estimate: the dataset holds rates only, not counts, and it assumes a constant population.
items.source_name: CDC NCHS VSRR quarterly provisional estimates (dataset 76vv-a7x8)
items.why_new: Known items cover the 2025 births total and Taiwan births. This adds the US 12-month-ending rate through Q2'26 with y/y math.
items.verify_note: Verified on data.cdc.gov: 54.5 (25Q1), 53.7 (25Q2), 53.6 (25Q3), 53.3 (25Q4), 53.0 (26Q1), 52.7 (26Q2, flagged significant). The API output has no time_period field, and 24Q2 (53.9) is out of line with 24Q1/Q3 (54.6), so the 12-month-ending basis is unconfirmed. Downgraded from strong. The GFR overstates the fall in birth counts: 2025 GFR fell ~2.4% while births fell ~0.6–1%, because the 15–44 female population grew. The 3.58M estimate that assumes constant population is therefore too low (see d

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Birth-rate declines are concentrated in the age 20-29 groups, which are the largest share of births and the lowest-depth, lowest-risk NIPT users.
items.detail: Q2 12-month-ending age-specific rates, 2025 vs 2026: age 20-24 fell 54.8→51.5 (-6.0%), age 25-29 fell 89.4→83.7 (-6.4%), age 18-19 fell 22.8→21.1 (-7.5%), and age 15-17 fell 5.0→4.3. From Q2'24 to Q2'26 the 25-29 rate fell 89.7→83.7 (-6.7%) and the 20-24 rate fell 56.3→51.5 (-8.5%). The pool of pregnancies to be tested is shrinking from the young end.
items.source_name: CDC NCHS VSRR quarterly provisional estimates
items.why_new: The age-specific series was not in the known items, which have only an aggregate birth denominator.
items.verify_note: I checked the CDC 76vv-a7x8 dataset. The figures for ages 20-24 (56.3/54.8/51.5) and 25-29 (89.7/89.4/83.7) are correct. The dataset has no 18-19 row; 15-19 went 12.8→12.2→11.2. Two framing problems. First, ACMG recommends NIPT for every pregnancy (known), so the 'lowest-risk users' link to volume is weak. Second, D086 shows the count of births falls only about 0–1% a year. This is a composition point, not a volume shock.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Births to older mothers, the cohort with the highest NIPT intensity and uptake, are still rising, which partly cushions test volume.
items.detail: Q2 12-month-ending rates, 2025→2026: age 30-34 rose 94.4→96.3 (+2.0%), age 35-39 rose 54.6→55.4 (+1.5%), and age 40-44 rose 12.7→12.9 (+1.6%). The 2024→2026 gain is 93.5→96.3 at 30-34 and 54.0→55.4 at 35-39. Older-mother births carry higher screening rates and often more follow-on testing, so the mix shift supports revenue per test more than test count. The 30-34 group is the only one without a significance flag in 2026 Q2.
items.source_name: CDC NCHS VSRR quarterly provisional estimates
items.why_new: This quantifies the offset to the shrinking NIPT denominator with the age mix.
items.verify_note: Verified: 30-34 went 93.5→94.4→96.3, 35-39 went 54.0→54.6→55.4, and 40-44 went 12.6→12.7→12.9. The 2024 Q2 figure for 40-44 is 12.6 in the data, not 12.7. The claim that the mix shift supports revenue per test is inference.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: A rough US NIPT ceiling, using the denominator and the expert penetration range, sits well below the 2.9-3.4M the lead suggested once births fall to about 3.5M.
items.detail: Births of ~3.50-3.58M (12 months to Q2'26, my estimate) times the 70-80% penetration experts cite gives about 2.45-2.86M deliveries already tested. Adding ~1M non-delivery pregnancies is the strategist's figure, not a measured one. Only a small share of those get screened, and the lead did not give that rate. With 100% of deliveries tested the ceiling is ~3.5M plus any non-delivery tests. The 70-80% is already largely reached, so growth has to come from penetration of the last 20-30%, repeat or reflex testing and added tiers, not from a growing denominator. I could not verify the penetration figure in this source.
items.source_name: CDC NCHS press release and VSRR
items.quote: decreased by 1% from 2024
items.why_new: This turns the known 70-80% penetration claim into a numeric volume cap using current births.
items.verify_note: This restates known facts: 70–80% penetration (known), the birth denominator (D086/F940), and NIPT maturing (known). The ~1M non-delivery pregnancies is unsourced, and the 2.9–3.4M 'lead' figure has no source. No new measured fact.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: US 2025 births were 3,606,400 (-1%), with a record-low teen birth rate and a general fertility rate of 53.1. NCHS gives no sign of a rebound.
items.detail: The NCHS release dated 9 Apr 2026 reports births down 1% from 2024, GFR 53.1 ('fell slightly') and a teen birth rate of 11.7 per 1,000, down 7%. Ages 15-17 fell 11% and ages 18-19 fell 7%. The release gives no 2024 absolute count or 40+ rates. The 2026 quarterly GFR (53.0, 52.7) is below the 53.1 for 2025, so the slide has continued into 2026.
items.quote: decreased by 1% from 2024
items.why_new: This ties the 2025 count to the 2026 quarterly trend and adds the teen and age declines. It is not a new headline number.
items.verify_note: The 3,606,400 births (-1%) and the 2026 quarterly GFR path are already used in D086 and F940. The teen-rate detail does not matter for NIPT volume.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Hispanic fertility, a large share of US births, is falling fastest in the 12-month-ending series, which pressures the NIPT pool in high-growth states.
items.detail: Hispanic GFR in the dataset fell from 66.1 (Q4'24) to 62.3 (Q4'25) to 61.4 (Q1'26) to 59.0 (Q2'26), a 10.8% decline from Q4'24 to Q2'26. In Q2 alone it fell 63.9→59.0 (-7.7% y/y). Non-Hispanic White was 51.7→53.5 (rising, +3.5% since Q4'24), and non-Hispanic Black fell 51.4→49.3. The race composition of births is shifting, and Medicaid-insured pregnancies are a main driver of NIPT payer mix. I did not test the link to payer mix.
items.source_name: CDC NCHS VSRR quarterly provisional estimates
items.why_new: The race-split fertility trend is not in the known items.
items.verify_note: I could not reproduce the Hispanic GFR rows; the general-fertility query returned nothing. The values may be age-specific rates by Hispanic origin rather than a GFR. Neither the Medicaid/payer-mix link nor the 'high-growth states' link was tested. Use as context only.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The 6000Dx instrument and consumables package inserts are unchanged since Sep 2022 and the library-tube insert since Nov 2024, so the regulated kit set has had no redesign for about four years.
items.detail: Instrument inserts (CE-IVD 200025276, US-IVD 200025284) and the consumables insert (200025483) are all dated 29 Sep 2022. The library-tube insert (200025484) is dated 21 Nov 2024. The English product documentation is dated 29 Sep 2022. A regulated lab on these kits has had no label change to adapt to, and the next change is not signalled.
items.why_new: Package-insert document IDs and dates are new. The known list only has the 6000Dx kit price cut.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: In 2026 UConn's Center for Genome Innovation dropped all of its own NovaSeq 6000 flow-cell prices and now sends high-throughput work out as NovaSeq X 25B lanes to The Jackson Laboratory's genomics core (JAX-GM), so another research core's 6000 tail has ended through consolidation onto a partner.
items.detail: UConn's billing catalogue shows 'No active price groups' for its NovaSeq 6000 S1, SP and S2 100-cycle products. A search snippet shows that in Jul–Dec 2025 these were priced at $4,681.75 (S1), $2,554.24 (SP) and $8,817.78 (S2). The only live high-throughput item is '300 cycle, 25B NovaX (JAX-GM)' at $2,936.57 per lane for 1 Jan–31 Dec 2026. A lane is 6.5B paired-end reads, about 975 Gb, so roughly $3.01/Gb. A Feb 2026 UConn bioinformatics page still lists a NovaSeq 6000 in-house, so the instrument may be idle rather than retired.
items.source_name: UConn Center for Genome Innovation billing catalogue (honeycrisp)
items.quote: No active price groups found for this product.
items.why_new: UConn was known only as a $2.94/Gb 25B price point; the 6000 delisting and the JAX outsourcing route are new.
items.verify_note: Verified that the S1 100-cycle product (392) shows 'No active price groups.' The UConn 25B lane price of ~$2.94/Gb is already known (1B core list). The new parts are the deactivated 6000 products and the routing of high-throughput work to JAX. One more core's 6000 tail is ending, but by consolidation the instrument may be idle rather than retired.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: UCSF CAT's older rate sheet (from about mid/late 2024, with 25B 100/200-cycle 'Coming Nov. 2024') shows the size of later cuts: 25B-300 UC −10.5%, 10B-300 −16.5%, and for-profit external 25B down about 16%.
items.detail: Old sheet (node/706): 25B-300 $2,850 UC / $3,591 non-profit / $4,448 for-profit; 10B-300 $1,724; 10B-100 $1,252. Current sheet: 25B-300 $2,551, 10B-300 $1,439, 10B-100 $1,105 (−11.7%). The for-profit surcharge is now +46.3%, so for-profit 25B ≈ $2,551 × 1.463 = $3,732, against $4,448 before (−16.1%). Non-profit (+33%) ≈ $3,393, against $3,591 (−5.5%). The cuts fall between roughly late 2024 and 2026, which overlaps Berkeley's summer 2026 volume consolidation.
items.source_name: UCSF Center for Advanced Technology rate pages
items.quote: Coming Nov. 2024
items.why_new: F817 noted the fall but not its dating or the for-profit external cut; this update quantifies both.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Illinois's Carver core (prices effective 1 Aug 2026) has a volume tier of 6–16% off NovaSeq X lanes for 8+ lanes, and its 10B PE150 lane appears to have fallen from $2,110 to $2,000.
items.detail: Rates effective 1 Aug 2026: 25B PE150 $3,380 / $3,180 for 8+ lanes (−5.9%); 25B SR100 $2,190 / $1,930 (−11.9%); 10B PE150 $2,000 / $1,710 (−14.5%); 10B SR100 $1,520 / $1,270 (−16.4%). A search snippet of an earlier version showed the 10B PE150 at $2,110 (−5.2%). External users pay a 30.8% overhead, capped at 20% for Illinois state institutions. The same sheet also lists 'Full Wafer Pricing' at $3,310, which is probably an Ultima wafer (unconfirmed).
items.source_name: Roy J. Carver Biotechnology Center, UIUC
items.quote: All pricing is updated, effective Aug. 1, 2026.
items.why_new: D045 used Carver only for the 10B/25B ratio; the volume-tier discounts and the 10B cut are new.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: UConn still charges researchers a 'temporary 5% tariff surcharge' on Illumina sequencing for the whole of 2026, and its 25B lane price rose slightly. Research users are absorbing cost increases, not getting cuts.
items.detail: The 2026 25B-300 lane is $2,936.57 (1 Jan–31 Dec 2026). A search snippet shows Jul–Dec 2025 at $2,924.04 (+0.4%) and an earlier 1 Jul 2025 figure of $2,534.74 (+16%; snippet only, unverified). The 6000 rows carried the same 5% surcharge in 2025. This fits Illumina's own tariff pass-through and suggests research cores pass it on to end users.
items.source_name: UConn Center for Genome Innovation billing catalogue
items.quote: Cost includes library pool QC, Illumina shipping and temporary 5% tariff surcharge.
items.why_new: This is a core-level tariff surcharge on Illumina lanes; the known list has tariff pass-through only at the Illumina level.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Berkeley's QB3 core has cut services for lack of staff: it no longer offers amplicon sequencing and does no Oxford Nanopore library prep. Labour, not sequencing price, limits research throughput.
items.detail: The QB3 rate page (effective 1 Jun 2026) sends amplicon users to Rush University and says it lacks 'bandwidth for library preparations' for nanopore. It also has no NovaSeq X of its own and outsources all lanes to UCSF CAT. This matches the known library-prep constraint, seen here at a single core.
items.quote: At this time we do not have the bandwidth for library preparations
items.why_new: The source's earlier mining covered lane prices only; the capacity-constraint text was not captured.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: At Harvard's Bauer Core, the 25B's per-read discount to the 10B narrowed by about 10–13 points in FY27 at both 200 and 300 cycles, so this core passes on less of the higher-density flow cell's economics than a year ago.
items.detail: FY26 per million reads (25B 2.5B reads, 10B 1.0B per lane): 200c $1,830/2.5=$0.732 vs $1,234 → 25B 40.7% cheaper; 300c $2,059/2.5=$0.824 vs $1,304 → 36.8% cheaper. FY27: 200c $0.857 vs $1,193 → 28.2% cheaper; 300c $0.970 vs $1,314 → 26.2% cheaper. The narrowing comes from 25B lane prices rising +17% while 10B prices were flat. If the 35B follows this pattern at cores, its step-down to researchers may be shallower than the ~20% cut assumed. Internal rates also include core overhead and utilization, so this is a core-policy read, not an Illumina net-price read.
items.source_name: Harvard Bauer Core FY26/FY27 rate pages (snippets)
items.why_new: F777 showed narrowing only at 300c per Gb. This shows it at 200c too, on a per-read basis, and rebuts F906's 'supports' framing.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: The US NIPT birth denominator is shrinking, but only by about 0–1% a year in counts, because the general fertility rate's ~2–3% decline is partly offset by a growing population of women aged 15–44.
items.detail: The CDC GFR fell 54.6→53.3 (-2.4%) from 2024 Q4 to 2025 Q4, while 2025 births were 3,606,400 against ~3.63M in 2024 (about -0.6% to -1%). That implies the 15–44 female population grew ~1.5–1.8%. With GFR down 1.9% y/y at 2026 Q2 and population growth likely slower (lower immigration), 2026 births are probably about -0.5% to -1.5%. That is a small but negative base for a test already at ~70–80% US penetration. It confirms NIPT volume growth must come from depth or expanded panels, not more pregnancies.
items.source_name: CDC NCHS VSRR quarterly provisional birth indicators
items.why_new: Turns F940's rate data into a count-based NIPT denominator and corrects the overstatement in F935/F940's constant-population assumption.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Illumina's direct US federal obligations (~$24M in FY26) are less than the run-rate of a single NHLBI sequencing vehicle (~$31M/yr), so federal research sequencing dollars flow mainly through genome centers, which have the most leverage on Illumina price.
items.detail: Sweetspot shows Illumina's direct federal net obligations falling $33.9M (FY25) → $24.0M (FY26). TOPMed CORE 2.0 task orders to Broad, Baylor, NYGC and others total ~$93M over three years (~$31M/yr), flat vs the predecessor vehicle. Federal sequencing money therefore reaches Illumina mostly indirectly, through large centers such as Broad (known 'insane' discounts and an AXELIOS buyer). That supports the view that research pricing is set by large-lab negotiation. Both series are small and lumpy, and distributor sales are excluded.
items.why_new: Combines two new federal datasets to show where research sequencing dollars are routed. No known item covers this.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: NCBI GTR has about 11x more clinical test records naming the NovaSeq 6000 than the NovaSeq X, as of 12 Oct 2026.
items.detail: esearch db=gtr returned Count=130 for 'NovaSeq 6000' and Count=12 for 'NovaSeq X' (queried 12 Oct 2026). The 12 X hits look like loosely matched records, mainly University of Michigan single-gene tests, Integrated Genetics MaterniT21, and Mass General Brigham. Instrument fields are not yet verified, and GTR is lab-reported and goes stale, so this is only a rough indicator of the regulated and LDT tail. Many 6000 records sit in consecutive ID blocks, which suggests a few labs registered dozens of tests each.
items.why_new: The known list has no registry-level count of tests by sequencer; it only has anecdotes about specific FDA tests.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Mayo Clinic Laboratories' Ehlers-Danlos gene panel record names the NovaSeq 6000 as its instrument and was updated on 10 Apr 2026.
items.detail: The GTR record 603740 (version GTR000603740.6) lists Methodology > Instrument as Illumina NovaSeq 6000, for both sequence analysis and deletion/duplication analysis. It was updated 2026-04-10, which means a major reference lab was still declaring the 6000 six months ago. Mayo has many sequential record IDs, so there may be a large Mayo block on the 6000.
items.quote: Illumina NovaSeq 6000
items.why_new: This is a named, dated lab-reported 6000 use in a clinical test; the known list names only Tempus, Natera and Caris postings.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Rival short-read platforms (AVITI, DNBSEQ/MGISEQ, Ultima) grew from 3.8% to 5.5% of US-tagged GEO sequencing series in a year, with rival series up 97% against 34% for NovaSeq.
items.detail: US-tagged GEO series released in Q3'25 vs Q3'26. Rival terms: 69 → 136 series. NovaSeq: 1,753 → 2,351. Rival share = 69/(1,753+69) = 3.79% → 136/(2,351+136) = 5.47%, +1.7 pts. NovaSeq series grew +34% and rival series +97%. Rivals took about 11% of the US year-on-year series increase: (136−69)/((136−69)+(2,351−1,753)) = 67/665 = 10%. This is the first US-specific rival-share datapoint. It is small and below the 3-point flag, but the direction fits rival capture of academic work.
items.date: 2026-10-12 (data for Q3'25 and Q3'26 release quarters)
items.source_name: NCBI GEO DataSets via E-utilities (esearch db=gds)
items.why_new: Prior GEO items were by platform record or a contact-country proxy and did not give a text-based rival share of series by country.
items.verify_note: Verified Q3'26 US rival count = 136. Correction: the share of the increment is 67/665 = 10.1%, not 'about 11%.' 'USA[All Fields]' is a noisy country tag. Per D065, if the NovaSeq term misses X Plus GPLs, the rival share is overstated. This is well below the SRA increment capture of ~23% (D056).

items.label: 2B
items.claim: In no country tested did the rival-platform share of GEO series rise by more than 3 points, so the strategist's flag threshold was not hit anywhere.
items.detail: Share change, Q3'25 → Q3'26. US 3.8% → 5.5% (+1.7). China 12.1% → 13.6% (+1.5). Germany 6.7% → 9.1% (+2.4). Japan 16.4% → 18.3% (+1.9). France 10.5% → 12.0% (+1.5). UK was not usable (1 and 1 rival series; NovaSeq 21 and 25). The text match on 'UK' is unreliable because GEO usually writes 'United Kingdom'. Germany had the largest rise, but on small numbers: 13 → 18 rival series, and NovaSeq series were flat at 182 → 180. Rival capture is real but gradual in public research data.
items.why_new: This is the requested country screen. It shows no country with a rival-share jump above 3 points, a watch-out for the 2B pricing-pressure story.
items.verify_note: Plausible and consistent with D057 (GEO shows slower rival capture than SRA). The country text-matching caveats apply, and the German base is small (13→18).

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Germany shows NovaSeq series flat (182 → 180) while rival-platform series rose 13 → 18, the only country where Illumina volume stalled in public research data.
items.detail: Germany-tagged GEO series, Q3'25 vs Q3'26. NovaSeq −1%, rivals +38%. The rival share rose 6.7% → 9.1% (+2.4 pts), the largest move of the five usable countries. US NovaSeq series grew +34%, China +28.6% and Japan −1%. Japan's NovaSeq series are also flat (163 → 161) with rivals 32 → 36. Counts are tiny, so this is directional only.
items.why_new: No earlier item split public Illumina series growth by country, and Germany and Japan flat NovaSeq counts were not in the corpus.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Public NovaSeq series from Japan and Germany were flat y/y in Q3'26 (−1% each), so the 'volume keeps accelerating' read does not hold outside the US and China.
items.detail: Japan 163 → 161 NovaSeq series, Germany 182 → 180, France 68 → 95 (+40%), China 1,098 → 1,412 (+29%), US 1,753 → 2,351 (+34%). Combined, the five countries rose from 3,264 to 4,199 (+29%), and the US and China account for most of it. This is a series count, not Gb, and prior items show Gb growth in public data is much weaker (~12%). Growth is therefore concentrated in two markets.
items.why_new: This gives country-level y/y series counts, where the corpus had only global GEO growth.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: In China-tagged GEO series, rival platforms (mostly DNBSEQ) are 13.6% of sequencing series, up from 12.1%, and rival series grew +48% vs +29% for NovaSeq.
items.detail: China-tagged series, Q3'25 → Q3'26. Rivals 151 → 223. NovaSeq 1,098 → 1,412. Share = 151/1,249 = 12.1% → 223/1,635 = 13.6% (+1.5 pts). Rivals took about 19% of the y/y series increase (72/386). China is already outside Illumina's reach for consumables (import ban), so this is a read on research behaviour, not Illumina revenue.
items.why_new: The earlier China proxy covered 6000/X conversion only, not rival share of series.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Japan's 18% and China's 14% rival shares are the highest, but both sit in markets where Illumina's exposure is limited or already stable, and none rose faster than 2 points.
items.detail: Japan rival share 16.4% (32/195) → 18.3% (36/197), +1.9 pts, flat NovaSeq. France 10.5% → 12.0% (+1.5 pts). The US is the market that matters most for Illumina research consumables, and its rival share is only 5.5%. This lowers the weight of rival-driven research price pressure in the US over the last year.
items.why_new: This is a watch-out that quantifies where rival share is low and where it is not rising fast.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Mayo Clinic Laboratories alone holds 104 of the 130 GTR NovaSeq 6000 records (80%), so the registry's 6000 tail is mostly one large reference lab.
items.detail: esearch for "NovaSeq 6000" AND "Mayo Clinic Laboratories" returned 104; 104/130 = 80%. Records I opened were current: hereditary renal cancer panel (updated 2026-05-18), Ehlers-Danlos panel (2026-04-10), SEPTIN9 and muscular dystrophy panels (2025-09-16). None of the Mayo records I opened names the X. Mayo is one of the largest US clinical reference labs, and it is still declaring the 6000 on tests refreshed in 2025-26.
items.quote: Illumina NovaSeq 6000
items.why_new: F953 covered one Mayo record; this quantifies Mayo's share (104 of 130) and shows several current versions.
items.verify_note: Verified: 104/130 GTR 'NovaSeq 6000' records are Mayo. That share mostly shows Mayo files many GTR records, not that the tail is concentrated in Mayo. GTR's instrument field is self-declared and can lag the lab's actual instruments. See the derived item: excluding Mayo, the X is ~32% of declared records.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Mayo Clinic Laboratories reviewed and re-versioned its 6000-labelled tests repeatedly through 2022-2026 without switching to the X.
items.detail: The Ehlers-Danlos record has 6 versions: registered 2022-12-15, then updates on 2023-04-06, 2024-04-08, 2025-04-04, 2025-09-16 and 2026-04-10. The muscular dystrophy panel was updated 2025-04-01 and 2025-09-16, and the renal cancer panel 2024-04-15 and 2026-05-18. The instrument field stayed 'Illumina NovaSeq 6000' through every revision I could see, so the lab had many chances to change it and did not. This fits the regulated or validated clinical tail, but the field may lag the lab's actual instruments.
items.why_new: Adds a dated version history showing repeated re-attestation of the 6000 by a major clinical lab.
items.verify_note: Verified the version history for 603740 (6 versions, 2022-12-15 to 2026-04-10, 6000 throughout). It overlaps with F960, and updates to the declared field may be administrative.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Tempus (xT) declares the NovaSeq 6000 for its flagship tissue test in GTR, reviewed Nov 2025.
items.detail: Tempus xT, record GTR000613444.1 (Tempus AI - RTP), lists 'Novaseq 6000' for both the MSI and coding-sequence methods. It was registered 2024-11-06 and the lab's last annual review was 2025-11-12. This is consistent with Tempus job postings listing both 6000 and X, but it is a declared field.
items.quote: Novaseq 6000
items.why_new: Not in the known list; it is a filing-like lab declaration that a large oncology customer's test runs on the 6000.
items.verify_note: Verified: Tempus xT on the NovaSeq 6000, registered 2024-11-06. The 2025-11-12 date is the lab's annual review, not a test-specific review. It adds a declared 6000 to the known Tempus job postings that list both the 6000 and the X.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The 12 'NovaSeq X' hits are few and mostly small labs, but they include Labcorp-owned Integrated Genetics/Sequenom (MaterniT NIPT) and Mass General Brigham, so some clinical conversion is declared.
items.detail: X-family records: Integrated Genetics–Sequenom (CLIA 05D2015356) MaterniT21, MaterniT GENOME and the two Genome Add-On tests, all 'Novaseq X Plus', last updated 2024-11-01. University of Michigan Molecular Genetics (CLIA 23D1088637) has BRCA1/2 (updated 2026-06-24, versions 2022-2026), TP53, CFTR, ATP7B and GDI1. MGB Laboratory for Molecular Medicine's polygenic cardiovascular risk test (registered 2025-12-04) runs on the X Plus at the Broad Clinical Laboratory. A male infertility panel (registered 2026-07-18) also names the X Plus. So a large NIPT lab has declared an X move, which matches the known NIPT-converts-first view.
items.quote: Novaseq X Plus
items.why_new: Names the labs behind the X records and gives dates; shows NIPT already on the X and a US academic lab (Michigan) converting.
items.verify_note: Not opened. That the NIPT lab (Sequenom/Labcorp) converted first matches known cohort 4 (price-motivated movers, mostly moved), so it adds little against the thesis. Its last update was Nov 2024.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Rival short-read platforms are almost absent from clinical test registrations: AVITI appears in 11 GTR records, all from a small Polish-linked lab, and Ultima is not detectable.
items.detail: esearch for AVITI returned 11 IDs (613429, 558563, 558561, 332665 and others). The two I opened are from the Laboratory of Human Genetics (testing at Genomed S.A., Warsaw): retinal dystrophy panel (registered 2024-10-25) and childhood absence epilepsy panel (updated 2025-01-31). Against 130 for the 6000, that is 11 AVITI records per 130 6000 records (~8%) and all from one lab family. An 'Ultima Genomics' query returned 31,252 results, so it was a loose match and gave no usable count. Clinical labs are not yet declaring rival platforms, which weakens near-term large-account leverage in the clinical book.
items.why_new: Quantifies the rival footprint in clinical test registrations. It cuts against 1B/2B in the clinical channel.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Newly registered tests are still being filed on the NovaSeq 6000 in 2026, with one registered 7 Oct 2026.
items.detail: A Dystonia Gene Panel (record 619920, Clinical Biochemical Genetics Diagnostic Laboratory) names 'Illumina Novaseq 6000' and was registered 2026-10-07. Another 6000 record (CMS mutation detection, 613591) was registered 2025-01-14 and reviewed 2026-04-20. Labs setting up new test listings in late 2026 still choose the 6000, which fits a tail that does not convert on a fixed schedule.
items.quote: Illumina Novaseq 6000
items.why_new: Shows a brand-new 2026 registration naming the 6000. It is one small lab, so low weight.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Excluding Mayo, the NovaSeq X family accounts for about a third of the sequencer declarations in NCBI's Genetic Testing Registry (GTR), so the registry's apparent 6000 dominance mostly reflects one heavy filer.
items.detail: GTR has 130 'NovaSeq 6000' records, 104 of them from Mayo Clinic Laboratories (verified via esearch, Oct 2026), against 12 X-family records (F963). Counting all records, the X share is 12/142 = 8.5%, far below management's ~78% clinical X share of high-throughput Gb (Q2'26). Excluding Mayo, it is 12/(26+12) = 32%. Declared registry fields lag real instrument use, so GTR cannot measure how big the clinical tail is; it can only name specific holdouts such as Mayo and Tempus.
items.why_new: Combines the GTR 6000 and X counts into a share, with and without Mayo; not in the known list.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Rival platforms' capture of year-on-year growth in US public sequencing deposits (~10% in GEO series) is less than half their capture in global SRA runs (~23%), so US academic share loss is real but slower than the global run data suggest.
items.detail: US GEO series in Q3'26 vs Q3'25: rival series grew by 67 against 598 more NovaSeq series, so rivals took 67/665 = 10.1% of the increment (F954, count of 136 verified). Global SRA runs in Q3'26: rivals (AVITI+T7) took ~23% of new-platform run growth (D056), largely DNBSEQ (D061). The gap suggests much of the global rival gain is MGI outside the US, while US research share loss to rivals runs at about 1.7 points a year.
items.why_new: First US versus global comparison of rivals' capture of growth.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Half the value of Taichung VGH's 2025–27 'whole-exome' reagent tender went to a UK-origin nucleic-acid chip (likely nanopore flow cells) next to the US-origin exome reagent, so a clinical buyer is splitting sequencing spend across platforms.
items.detail: Tender 114A08 (May 2025) made two awards, both to the sole bidder ANTEC Bioscience. Item 1, 'B98014028016 nucleic acid analysis chip' (UK origin), went for NT$4.0M against a NT$5.0M budget, running May 2025–Apr 2027. Item 2, the 'whole-exome sequencing reagent' (US origin), went for NT$4.1M against NT$5.0M, running May 2025–Apr 2027. Both awards were 18–20% below budget, even with one bidder. ANTEC also delivered both of the CDC's 2026 nanopore instruments, which supports reading item 1 as ONT consumables. The brand is not stated.
items.quote: 核酸分析晶片
items.why_new: The item-level split, the origins and ANTEC's role in Taichung 114A08 were not mined before. The strategist had flagged this tender.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Taiwan CDC's budget for its Illumina-certified sequencer service contract rose 17% from 2023 to 2026, showing no service-price erosion at a public-health account.
items.detail: Annual 'next-generation sequencer maintenance contract' budgets were NT$638,700 (2023), NT$733,000 (2024, +14.8%), NT$744,000 (2025, +1.5%) and NT$747,500 (2026, +0.5%). Every tender requires 'Illumina, Inc.-certified service technicians'. These are budgets, not awards; no award notices were returned. The growth flattened after 2024.
items.quote: 須提出原廠(Illumina, Inc.)認證之維修人員證明
items.why_new: This four-year Taiwan CDC Illumina service-budget series has not been reported. Earlier service items covered Taipei VGH, NHRI and US federal buyers.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: NTU Cancer Center locked oncology mutation testing into 4-year, non-US-origin reagent-plus-instrument contracts in 2026, so part of its tumor genotyping volume sits outside Illumina until 2030.
items.detail: AD14E140, 'human oncogene mutation analysis reagents (with instrument)': NT$14.94M against a NT$16.2M budget, one bidder (Ji Cheng), Germany origin, May 2026–May 2030. AD15E020, 'gene mutation kits (with instrument), 3 items': NT$6.0M at budget, one bidder, Belgium origin, Aug 2026–Aug 2030. The brands are not stated. Germany suggests Qiagen and Belgium suggests Biocartis Idylla (PCR-based), but both are inferences. Together that is ~US$660K over four years at one cancer center.
items.quote: 人類致癌基因突變分析試劑(附儀器)開口合約
items.why_new: The NTU Cancer Center's 2026 oncology mutation-testing contracts have not appeared before. Earlier items covered only its failed benchtop sequencer tender (F852).

items.label: 1B
items.claim: The UC system-wide Illumina agreement locks in a long, multi-year discount framework (Feb 2024 to Jun 2029), including a 25% service discount.
items.detail: The UC-wide Illumina agreement (CalUsource 2023003585) runs 2/15/2024 to 6/14/2029 and covers instruments, reagents, service agreements and research services. The only quantified term is 25% off service agreements. Consumable discounts are unspecified and no tiers are published. This shows large academic buyers pool purchasing, but it does not show deepening discounts.
items.source_name: UC Office of the President Procurement
items.why_new: The UC system-wide contract, its dates and the 25% service discount were not in the known evidence.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Labcorp's new Plasma Detect MRD tests, registered Dec 2025, list the NovaSeq 6000Dx as the platform, so a new MRD product is being filed on the 6000 line.
items.detail: Plasma Detect Genome MRD-Baseline (619625) and Plasma Detect MRD-Monitoring (619713), Molecular Oncology Laboratory, LabCorp (CLIA 34D1008914), were registered 8 Dec 2025. The Test Platform field reads 'illumina NovaSeq 6000 Dx'. The Instrument column shows only the sonicator. This is a regulated-grade 6000Dx platform on a brand-new whole-genome MRD product. It supports the idea that new volume at a large lab starts on the 6000Dx, not the X. Whether that reflects a validation lag or a real plan to stay is unknown.
items.quote: illumina NovaSeq 6000 Dx
items.why_new: Not in known list: Labcorp WGS-MRD filed on the 6000Dx in Dec 2025.
items.verify_note: Checked on GTR. 619625 'Plasma Detect Genome MRD-Baseline' at LabCorp's Molecular Oncology Laboratory, registered 2025-12-08, has Test Platform 'illumina NovaSeq 6000 Dx'. Its instrument field lists only the Covaris S2 sonicator. This is new: no Labcorp MRD platform is in the known list. GTR entries are self-reported, though, and the 6000Dx may only be the validation platform. A single listing does not show a plan to stay on it.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: UCSF500 and JAX Genome, two academic clinical tests, remain on the 6000 in current records.
items.detail: UCSF500 Cancer Gene Panel (591895) reads 'Illumina NovaSeq 6000 system' and was last updated 31 Jan 2026 (v.2, first registered 6 Oct 2020), so it was re-filed on the 6000 in 2026. JAX Genome (613393, CLIA 07D2061461) reads 'Illumina NovaSeq 6000', was registered 7 Oct 2024, with a lab annual review on 28 Aug 2026. A genome-scale clinical test registered in late 2024 on the 6000 is notable.
items.quote: Illumina NovaSeq 6000 system
items.why_new: Names specific academic labs and dated 2026 re-filing absent from known evidence.
items.verify_note: New lab names (UCSF, JAX). UCSF500 is a v.2 update of a 2020 panel, so the 2026 date may only be routine upkeep, not a decision to stay. JAX Genome is a low-volume academic clinical test. Both are self-reported and add little to F960–F962.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: A leading NIPT lab (Labcorp's Integrated Genetics-Sequenom, MaterniT) lists the NovaSeq X Plus on all four of its records, so the NIPT cohort moved to the X.
items.detail: MaterniT21 (501985), MaterniT GENOME (569955), MaterniT21 Genome Add On (593063) and its Redraw (593064), CLIA 05D2015356, all read 'Novaseq X Plus'. They were last updated 1 Nov 2024. 501985 had v.1-2 in Nov 2013, v.3 in Jan 2020 and v.4 in Nov 2024. No MaterniT record is in the 6000 set. This supports the known Thaysen cohort 4 claim that NIPT mostly moved, and it means the 6000 tail is not in NIPT. It also means the NIPT price cut has already been absorbed.
items.quote: Novaseq X Plus
items.why_new: Known note says only that 'Labcorp-owned Integrated Genetics (MaterniT)' appears among the X hits. This gives all four record IDs, dates and the version history.
items.verify_note: Duplicate of F963, which already lists all four MaterniT records as 'Novaseq X Plus', last updated 2024-11-01. Per F995, MaterniT moved from HiSeq 2000 to the X Plus, not from the 6000, so it says nothing about the 6000 tail beyond what is known.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Michigan's Molecular Genetics Laboratory re-versioned six hereditary-gene records to the NovaSeq X Plus on 24-25 Jun 2026, so a US academic clinical lab did switch in 2026.
items.detail: Michigan (CLIA 23D1088637) has 6 of the 12 X hits: BRCA1/2, ATP7B, CHD7, TP53, CFTR sequencing and GDI1, plus CF carrier screening 507010 ('Illumina NovaSeqX'; v.4 on 25 Jun 2026 after v.3 in Jul 2024). ATP7B 508735 is v.5, last updated 24 Jun 2026, and BRCA1/2 509980 is v.5, also 24 Jun 2026. The prior version of 508735 (v.4, 27 Jun 2025) read 'Illumina NextSeq 550', so this switch was from the mid-throughput NextSeq, not the 6000. A 'NovaSeq 6000 AND Michigan' search returns 0.
items.quote: Illumina NovaSeq X Plus
items.why_new: Known list has only the aggregate '12 X hits'. This identifies half as one lab, the dates, and shows the previous platform was a NextSeq 550.
items.verify_note: Michigan's X records are already in F963. The item itself says the switch was from the NextSeq 550, not the 6000, so it does not cut against 1A. F995 covers this properly.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Most of the 12 X hits are not independent evidence of clinical X conversion, because they come from a few labs and one is a false positive.
items.detail: The 12 'NovaSeq X' hits are 6 Michigan records (50%), 4 Integrated Genetics MaterniT records (33%), plus one Indian male-infertility panel (619856) and one Mass General Brigham polygenic risk test (619622), whose Instrument field says 'Not provided' (the text mentions Broad Clinical Labs sequencing). So only 10 of 12 names the X in a verified field, from 2 US labs. Broadening to 'NovaSeq X Plus OR NovaSeqX OR NovaSeq X' gives 14 hits: it adds 507010 (Michigan) and 618996 (UW SUDY exome, Instrument 'Not provided', registered 29 Sep 2025). GTR is self-reported and lightly maintained, so the 130 vs 12 ratio overstates the 6000's share.
items.why_new: Corrects the 11:1 ratio: de-duplicates the X hits and shows they cluster in two labs.
items.verify_note: Mostly restates F963 and D088. The only additions are the 14-hit broadened search and two records with 'Not provided' instrument fields, which are minor methodological caveats. The direction is also muddled: it weakens the X count and also says the 6000 share is overstated.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The 6000 set outside Mayo is only about 26 records and spans oncology (Tempus, UCSF, JAX, Labcorp), rare disease and small foreign labs.
items.detail: 130 6000 hits minus 104 Mayo = 26. I identified: Tempus xT/xR/xF (7 records, 3 sites incl. 558436 CHI and 613445 RTP), Labcorp Plasma Detect (2), UCSF500 (1), JAX Genome (1), a Bangladesh whole-exome test from NeuroGen (595969), 2 Burdwan University (India) rare-disease tests (613590, 613591), UW SUDY exome (618996, dual hit), and Providence 'ProvSeq 523' (556857). About 6 IDs (e.g. 576389 'NeXT Dx', 619621, 613192, 613130, 611987) could not be resolved because the summaries were truncated. By test category the non-Mayo tail is mostly tissue/liquid oncology and exome, not NIPT.
items.why_new: Gives the category breakdown that the known list calls out as the next step (Mayo split out).

items.label: 1A
items.claim: NeXT Dx (Natera-competitor Personalis/Tempus-bound WGS-style test) and ProvSeq 523 are listed on the 6000, so WGS-adjacent and 500-gene oncology products are being built on it.
items.detail: 576389 'NeXT Dx' and 556857 'ProvSeq 523' (Providence) are in the 6000 set. I could not read their Instrument fields or dates, because the batch summary truncated. Providence is the same group that validated 30x clinical genomes on the 6000 in 2025 (known). Needs a manual open of both records to confirm.
items.why_new: Adds two named products to the 6000 tail; both unverified.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Mayo's 6000 records are mostly hereditary gene panels and single-gene full-gene tests, so the registry's 6000 tail is low-volume rare-disease testing.
items.detail: Opened IDs included CFTR, MECP2, GATA2, BTK, NOTCH3, VHL, STK11, BAP1, FH, NF1, and neuromuscular, arrhythmia, SCID, nephrology and epilepsy panels (Mayo CLIA 24D0404292/24D1040592). Counted from batches: 16 in IDs 603733-603748, 14 in 597342-597355, plus 593005/593088/593144 and others. This matches the F830 view that low-volume owners have little reason to convert. These are per-test records and carry no volume.
items.why_new: Categorizes Mayo's 80% share by test type.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Taiwan's NHRI cut the budget for its outsourced Illumina sequencing lot for 2027 to NT$8.80M, about 15% below the NT$10.34M it awarded for 2026, and its total outsourced sequencing budget fell about 60%.
items.detail: NHRI's 2026 open contract (114B0E0213, awarded 26 Aug 2025) had a NT$24,867,926 budget. It awarded NT$10,341,095 for Lot A (Illumina, to Genomics BioSci) and NT$3,989,000 for Lot B (PacBio). The 2027 tender (115B0D0286, published 1 Oct 2026, bids open 14 Oct) has a total budget of NT$9,997,500, split into Lot A Illumina at NT$8,804,000 and Lot B PacBio at NT$1,193,500. The Illumina ceiling is therefore 14.9% below last year's Illumina award (8.804/10.341−1), and the total budget is 59.8% below last year's (9.9975/24.868−1). Awards usually land below budget, so actual 2027 Illumina outsourced spend is likely to fall more than 15%.
items.quote: Lot 1 (A組) Illumina … 8,804,000元
items.why_new: Known items cover NHRI lots only through 2026; this is the first look at the 2027 tender (Oct 2026).
items.verify_note: Duplicate. F845 and F846 already give the Oct 2026 NHRI tender split (Illumina NT$8.80M plus PacBio NT$1.19M, total NT$9.9975M) and the earlier Illumina-lot awards. The −14.9% vs the 2025 award is simple arithmetic on known figures.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: NHRI's 2026 outsourced sequencing contract was effectively uncontested: each lot drew exactly one bidder, and long-read capacity was bought separately alongside it.
items.detail: The 114B0E0213 award lists 2 bidders in total, one per lot. Genomics BioSci took the Illumina lot (items 1–21) at NT$10.34M and 台基盟 took the PacBio lot (items 22–28) at NT$3.99M. Nobody bid on both lots, so the Illumina lot was a single-bid award. The 2027 tender keeps the same two-lot structure. In budget terms the PacBio lot is cut more (−70% vs its 2026 award) than the Illumina lot (−15%).
items.why_new: Adds the bidder count per lot for the 2026 lot and the 2027 lot split by platform; earlier items gave only totals and the trend.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: In Sep 2026, Tri-Service General Hospital (Taiwan's military teaching hospital) bought 16 iSeq 100 reagent sets and 10 NextSeq 500/550 kits, a year after the iSeq 100 reached end of sale. Legacy Illumina reagent tails keep running.
items.detail: HJ15568P448 (decided 2 Sep 2026): item 1, iSeq 100 reagent kit, 16 sets at NT$175,500 each (NT$2.808M); item 2, NextSeq 500/550 reagents, 10 sets at NT$82,000 (NT$0.82M). Both are US-origin and were supplied by 瑞林生物科技. Illumina's retirement page puts the iSeq 100 end of sale at 30 Sep 2025, so a hospital was still committing to retired-platform consumables 12 months later. This fits a slow-decaying tail on legacy boxes.
items.quote: 次世代定序系統(iSeq 100)專用試劑套組(或同等品) 16 套
items.why_new: New buyer (Tri-Service/NDMC). Known legacy-tail items cover NTUH's MiSeq and NextSeq contracts, not iSeq buying after end of sale.
items.verify_note: Checked: HJ15568P448 has 16 iSeq 100 kits at NT$175,500 each and 10 NextSeq 500/550 kits at NT$82,000, both US origin, vendor 瑞林. It is the same point already made by F848 and F861 (NTUH MiSeq/MiniSeq contracts), on a small, non-6000 platform. iSeq service runs to 2029, so buying its consumables is expected. Illustrative only.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: At the same military hospital, the Illumina-origin reagents were awarded at exactly the base price, with no discount, while Taiwanese-made library reagents in the same tender went 20% below base.
items.detail: The tender had a budget and base price of NT$4,880,500 and awarded NT$4,630,000 across 2 bidders. Items 1–2 (Illumina iSeq and NextSeq kits, US origin): base NT$2,808,000 and NT$820,000, awarded at the same amounts (0% off). Items 3–5 (Camelot NGS dual-index, purification and polymerase kits, Taiwan origin): base NT$1,252,500, awarded NT$1,002,000 (−20.0%). Even though the 'or equivalent' wording opened the tender to rivals, Illumina's legacy consumables showed no price give.
items.why_new: New per-item price-to-base comparison in Sep 2026 for low- and mid-throughput Illumina kits against local reagents.
items.verify_note: Checked: items 1–2 were awarded exactly at base (NT$2.808M and NT$0.82M), while the Taiwanese-made items 3–5 came in 20% below base (NT$1.2525M vs NT$1.002M). The base price is set by the buyer and usually already reflects a negotiated price, so 'no discount vs base' does not mean no discount vs list. It is consistent with D074 (single-source Illumina lots award at base). Kit-specific consumables have no real 'or equivalent' rival.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Library-prep consumables at Tri-Service went to a local Taiwanese brand rather than Illumina, so Illumina captured only the sequencing-reagent part of this hospital's NGS spend.
items.detail: Of the NT$4.63M awarded, NT$1.002M (21.6%) went to Taiwan-made Camelot library-prep components (indexes, purification, polymerase), bid by 沛斯生物醫學. These were 60–100 units at NT$2,880–6,000 each. This is a single small tender, but it shows workflow dollars outside the flow cell flowing to non-Illumina vendors.
items.quote: 卡美洛NGS雙重索引套組(或同等品)
items.why_new: New datapoint: local library-prep substitution inside a hospital NGS tender.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Taiwan CDC's 2026 Illumina library-reagent and chip lot was awarded about 1% above the agency's own base price, so the buyer accepted a price above its floor rather than extracting a deeper discount.
items.detail: KA115051 (decided 21 Aug 2026): budget NT$12,056,125; base price NT$10,100,000; award NT$10,199,000, i.e. +0.98% vs base and −15.4% vs the single bidder's opening bid, which equaled the budget. The single bidder was Illumina's distributor 均泰, US origin. The concession runs from list toward the floor; there is no sub-floor price competition.
items.why_new: F749 cited the size of CDC's Illumina spend only; the base-price vs award mechanics (award above floor) are new.
items.verify_note: The award level (NT$10,199,000, flat y/y) is already in F749. The only new detail is that the award is +0.98% vs base and −15.4% vs the opening bid. That is the standard negotiation down from list, not evidence about the pace of discounting.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Taiwan's Institute of Forensic Medicine (Ministry of Justice) took two failed rounds before getting its 2026 Illumina NGS reagent lot, and then got 11.5% off the single bidder's opening bid.
items.detail: 621150506 / 621150506-1: budget NT$2,000,000. Round 1 failed for lack of bids (16 Jul 2026), round 2 was voided (4 Aug), and the lot was awarded 12 Aug 2026 to 均泰 (US origin) at NT$1,770,000 against a base price of NT$1,779,000 and an opening bid of NT$2,000,000 (−11.5%). The concession came without any visible rival bid. The same pattern showed in the vet institute's chips lot (−16.6% vs budget).
items.why_new: New buyer and a 2026 award; it extends the single-bidder concession pattern to a forensic agency.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: A new Illumina benchtop placement in 2026 at Taiwan's Veterinary Research Institute was followed within five months by a NT$1.6M (~US$50K) library-reagent and chip order, so new small placements bring real pull-through.
items.detail: 115-2003: NGS instrument, Singapore origin (consistent with Illumina benchtop manufacturing), single bidder 均泰 after one failed round; budget NT$2.35M, award NT$2.295M (−2.3%), decided 14 May 2026. 115-2013: library reagents and chips for the instrument, Singapore origin, decided 6 Oct 2026; budget NT$1,912,500, base NT$1,620,000, award NT$1,595,000. The chips spend is about 70% of the instrument price within the first ~5 months (1.595/2.295).
items.why_new: New 2026 placement plus pull-through pair at a government research institute; not in prior Taiwan items.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Illumina sequencer sales to Taiwanese public and private hospitals in 2025–26 kept closing at a single bidder and 1–6% below budget, including a sole-source 'high-throughput sequencer' at NTUH Yunlin.
items.detail: NTUH Yunlin YL-A24008 (5 May 2025): restricted tender under Procurement Act Art. 22(1)(2), a sole-source exclusivity clause; budget NT$5.35M, base NT$5.10M, award NT$5.05M (−5.6%), 均泰, Singapore origin. Chang Gung Linkou 0C-1L0324 (19 Aug 2025): 'ILLUMINA' named in the title; budget NT$2.264M, award NT$2.245M (−0.8%), single bidder after a failed round. The vet institute (May 2026) came in at −2.3%. These may partly overlap F894's three 2025 awards; the 2026 vet award and the Art. 22 sole-source basis are new.
items.quote: 採購法第22條第1項第2款
items.why_new: Adds the sole-source legal basis and a 2026 instrument datapoint; possible partial overlap with F894 is flagged.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: A Brazilian public research funder (FIOTEC/Fiocruz) moved from 6000 S4 kits to X kits only, which points to research conversion finishing.
items.detail: PNCP direct-award notices show FIOTEC buying NovaSeq 6000 S4 v1.5 kits in Sep 2023 (seq 62) and May 2024 (seq 328). From Feb 2025 to Jul 2026 it bought only NovaSeq X kits (10B, 25B, 1.5B), in six notices from R$58.6K up to R$1.05M. The series is consistent with research being about 90% on the X, so it argues against a permanent research 6000 tail. It is a single buyer with no unit prices.
items.why_new: Adds a dated buyer-level 6000-to-X conversion series from public procurement (lower value than the exclusion list's research conversion data).

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Brazil's Instituto Nacional de Cardiologia (Ministério da Saúde) bought a Silver Support service plan on a NovaSeq 6000 in July 2025, so 6000 service continues.
items.detail: Contratação Direta 312/2025 (published 15 Jul 2025) is for hospital equipment maintenance for a NovaSeq 6000 under a Silver Support Plan, at R$772,568.50. A health-system 6000 stayed under paid service in mid-2025 with no sign of retirement, which fits a clinical or hospital tail. It is one site.
items.why_new: Not in the exclusion list. It is a named hospital 6000 still under service in 2025.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: NYCU Hospital moved its prenatal cfDNA spend away from the expanded 38-condition NIPT, which needs deeper sequencing, toward basic blood NIPT. That is a down-tiering in Gb per test, the opposite of the up-tiering seen at other medical centers.
items.detail: In 2024–26 the hospital had a 38-item NIPT contract at NT$12.72M over 2 years (NT$6.36M a year; award 30 Jan 2024, Bionet, single bid) and a basic second-generation NIPT contract at NT$3.708M over 2 years (NT$1.85M a year; 6 Feb 2024, 台灣尖端先進生技, single bid). In 2026 the 38-item contract was re-awarded at NT$1.496M for one year, down 76% annualized (12 Feb 2026, Bionet). Basic blood NIPT went to NT$8.984M over 2 years (NT$4.49M a year, up 142%; 14 Apr 2026, Bionet). On our calc, the expanded tier fell from 77% to 25% of NIPT spend while the total fell about 27% (NT$8.21M → NT$5.99M a year). The total decline is already known (F904); the switch between tiers is new.
items.source_name: Taiwan Government e-Procurement (PCC) via pcc-api.openfun.app; NYCU Hospital 112114L99, 112112L99, 115306L54, 115108L54
items.why_new: F904 gave only NYCU's net −27%. The collapse of the expanded tier and the shift to basic NIPT, with vendor and contract amounts, are new.
items.verify_note: The arithmetic checks out. Expanded NIPT was 6.36 of 8.21M/yr (77%), then 1.496 of 5.99M/yr (25%). Total spend fell 27%. It is one hospital at about US$0.2M/yr and runs opposite to F779/F781, and D077 already shows Taiwanese NIPT is too small to matter for Illumina's Gb. The direction holds but the size is negligible.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Taiwanese public NIPT procurement specifies no sequencer. A Feb 2026 military-hospital RFI asks vendors to state their own 'testing platform or principle', so this regulated-screening channel is not locked to the NovaSeq 6000.
items.detail: The 國防醫學大學 / Tri-Service General Hospital Penghu RFI NI15034P (11 Feb–4 Mar 2026) covers NGS Down-syndrome screening plus singleton and multiple-pregnancy NIPT. Vendors fill in an A–H spec form that includes '檢測平台或原理', with only '次世代定序等' as an example. None of the 10+ NIPT award notices checked for 2024–26 (NYCU, Kinmen, MOHW Taipei and Taoyuan, NTUH Yunlin, Pingtung VGH) names NovaSeq, NextSeq, VeriSeq, Illumina or BGI. The outsourced lab can therefore switch sequencers without a new tender, unlike FDA-locked US assays.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC, 國防醫學大學 RFI NI15034P
items.quote: 檢測平台或原理
items.why_new: No prior item tested whether Taiwanese NIPT tenders tie the test to a specific Illumina instrument. They do not.
items.verify_note: Accurate for Taiwan, where NIPT is outsourced as a service and the tenders specify no sequencer. But Taiwan's NIPT channel is LDT-like and tiny, so it says almost nothing about the US FDA-locked clinical 6000 tail that drives 1A.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: New NIPT contracts at small Taiwanese public hospitals are tiny and flat-priced. MOHW Taoyuan Hospital's July 2026 award covers only 135 basic NIPT tests over three years, at NT$11,000 each.
items.detail: KA1150601 was awarded 30 Jun 2026 at NT$1,485,000, equal to the budget, with one bidder (華聯生物科技). The notice states '11000*135=1485000' for 1 Jul 2026–30 Jun 2029, which is about 45 tests a year. NT$11,000 is about 8% below Taipei VGH's NT$12,000 basic singleton price (F914). MOHW Taipei Hospital's 3-year NIPT contract is similarly small: NT$1.488M from 28 Aug 2024 to 27 Aug 2027, Bionet, single bid, about NT$0.5M a year.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC, 衛生福利部桃園醫院 KA1150601; 衛生福利部臺北醫院 2878-113010
items.why_new: The Taoyuan and Taipei MOHW hospital NIPT awards and the NT$11,000 per-test price were not in the ledger.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Small-hospital NGS prenatal screening is struggling to attract vendors. NTUH Hsinchu's NT$195K NGS Down-syndrome screening tender failed twice in July 2026 and had to be re-specified, and MOHW Chiayi's NT$1.49M NIPT tender also drew no bids at first.
items.detail: GH151020 (NTUH Hsinchu branch) had a budget of NT$195,000 for one year, about 32 tests at NYCU's NT$6,000 rate. Tenders failed for no bidders on 17 Jul and 29 Jul 2026, and the 21 Jul re-tender notes '修正規格後第一次重行招標'. MOHW Chiayi's CHYI1142722 (budget NT$1,492,800, 2 years) failed on 10 Jul 2025 for no bidders and was re-tendered on 11 Jul. Low vendor interest at the low-volume end suggests this market is saturated or not worth serving.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC, NTUH Hsinchu GH151020; MOHW Chiayi CHYI1142722
items.quote: 流標(無廠商投標或未達法定開標家數)
items.why_new: These failed tenders at the NTUH Hsinchu and Chiayi branches were not recorded. F852 covered a different, sequencer tender.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Illumina's 6000Dx IVD instrument and consumable DIs are all still in commercial distribution, and the NovaSeq 6000Dx records I saw have no discontinuation date or later version.
items.detail: The NovaSeq 6000Dx instrument (DI 00816270020637, model 20068232) was published 18 Oct 2022, with public version 1 dated 26 Oct 2022. It is 'In Commercial Distribution' with no end date. In the first 10 of 53 'NovaSeq Illumina' results, the 6000Dx Library Tube, the 24-pack, the S4 Buffer Cartridge and the DRAGEN Dx for 6000Dx record were all in commercial distribution. None of the 10 results was an X Dx entry. This is a watch-out: regulated clinical users have a supported IVD path only on the 6000Dx, which is consistent with a durable regulated tail. It is not proof, because only 10 of the 53 results were seen.
items.why_new: The known list has the 6000Dx (2022) only as an FDA-clearance fact. It has no GUDID commercial-distribution status or record history, and no sign of an X Dx DI.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Guardant's FY25 cost of revenue rose 20% to $349.0M, driven by sample volume and partly offset by lower cost per sample.
items.detail: Cost of revenue was $349.0M in 2025 vs $289.8M in 2024 (+20%). The 10-K credits higher oncology, biopharma and screening sample volume, partly offset by reduced cost per sample, mainly for Reveal, Guardant360 Liquid and Shield. Gross margin computed from revenue less cost is about 64% vs about 61% in 2024. This is a calculation, not a company disclosure. It points to customer-side per-test cost deflation, so Illumina's revenue per test falls even as tests grow.
items.quote: reduced cost per sample of our tests
items.why_new: FY25 10-K cost-of-revenue attribution with dollar figures. Known items mention only Guardant's flat GAAP gross margin and the Liquid move to the X.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The 2024-26 GTR switches to the X Plus came from labs on older platforms (NextSeq 550, HiSeq 2000), not from the 6000, so GTR cannot show a 6000-to-X conversion rate.
items.detail: Michigan Molecular Genetics Lab BRCA1/2 (509980) read NextSeq 550 at v3 (2024-07-08) and v4 (2025-06-27), then NovaSeq X Plus at v5 (2026-06-24). The prior version of every Michigan record I checked was NextSeq 550 (508371 TP53: v6, 2026-06-24, X Plus; v5, 2025-06-27, earlier instrument). Labcorp/Integrated Genetics MaterniT21 (501985) went from HiSeq 2000 (v3, 2020-01-09) to NovaSeq X Plus (v4, 2024-11-01), with no 6000 step. So the earlier 'Michigan switched to the X' item is a NextSeq-to-X move, not a 6000 conversion. The 12 X hits therefore overstate 6000 conversion.
items.why_new: Corrects how the known Michigan and Labcorp X records should be read: the prior instrument was not the 6000.
items.verify_note: The 509980 version page confirms v5 (2026-06-24) reads 'Illumina NovaSeq X Plus'. The version list does not display earlier instruments, so the NextSeq 550 reading for v3/v4 is the agent's and is unconfirmed here. The direction should be changed. If none of the X records came from the 6000, the GTR X hits are not 6000 conversions, and this undercuts the 'against' reading of F963/D088 rather than cutting against 1A. Relabelled as weak support for 1A.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Labs that stay on the 6000 mostly do not touch their records, so GTR shows a frozen tail of stale 6000 listings.
items.detail: ProvSeq 523 (Providence, 556857) was last updated 2020-01-09 (v5) and still names the 6000. Tempus xF CHI (569040) was last updated 2024-11-07 (v6), after v5 on 2022-09-01. Tempus xF RTP (613443) is v1, registered 2024-11-06, with a lab annual review on 2025-11-12 and no new version. Labcorp Plasma Detect (619713, 619625) are v1 from 2026-01-15 and name the 6000Dx. Of the 8 non-Mayo 6000 records I read, 1 was re-versioned in 2025-26 and 3 are v1 records registered in 2024-26.
items.why_new: Adds dated version histories (staleness) for Tempus, Providence and Labcorp records.
items.verify_note: Partly new: it shows how old the GTR records are, which the known GTR items (F960–F971, D088–D091) do not cover. The 'labs mostly don't touch records' claim rests on only 8 non-Mayo records, and Mayo re-versions often (F961). Staleness also weakens GTR as evidence in either direction, including the 'no 6000→X switch' inference in D090. Date correction: F970 has Labcorp Plasma Detect registered 8 Dec 2025, not 15 Jan 2026 (the 2026 date may be a last-update date).

items.label: 1A
items.claim: New tests from reference labs and academic labs continue to be registered on the 6000 in late 2025 and 2026, up to 7 Oct 2026.
items.detail: University of Miami Dystonia Gene Panel (619920) registered 2026-10-07, Instrument 'Illumina Novaseq 6000'. Labcorp Plasma Detect Genome MRD baseline and monitoring were registered 2026-01-15 on the 6000Dx. Wisconsin State Lab SUDY exome (618996) was registered 2025-09-29, but its Instrument field reads 'Not provided'. Across the three, at least two are dated 2026 and name the 6000 family.
items.why_new: The Miami record is not in the known list and is five days old.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: A second tail pattern: a lab can move its legacy tests to the X while its newer products start on the 6000.
items.detail: Labcorp's MaterniT lines (Integrated Genetics) sit on the X Plus (v4, Nov 2024), while Labcorp's Molecular Oncology Lab registered its new MRD products on the 6000Dx in Jan 2026. Michigan moved six legacy panels to the X Plus on 2026-06-24 (BRCA, TP53, CFTR, ATP7B, CHD7, GDI1 in the esearch set). The same parent therefore runs both generations by product line.
items.why_new: Links the Labcorp NIPT-on-X and MRD-on-6000Dx records as a lab-level split.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: A federal public-health lab is still paying for a combined NovaSeq 6000 and MiSeq maintenance contract, at a disclosed estimate of about $145K a year.
items.detail: CDC's Genomic Sequencing Laboratory in Atlanta posted a sole-source, firm-fixed-price maintenance and repair notice on 10 Oct 2024. It covers the NovaSeq 6000 and MiSeq, with performance 7 Dec 2024 to 6 Dec 2025 and an estimated value of $144,910.12. The 6000 is still the platform of record for outbreak sequencing. This is the only dollar figure in the federal 6000 service notices. It is not split between the two instruments. The Navy, NCI and NIEHS notices give no price.
items.source_name: SweetSpotGov mirror of a SAM.gov CDC notice (75D30125Q78540)
items.why_new: The known list names Navy, NCI and NIEHS 6000 service notices. It has no CDC notice and no service-contract dollar value.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: NIEHS bought small NovaSeq 6000 v1.5 flow-cell kits sole-source in Aug 2023 and then kept the 6000 on service through Jun 2026, which fits a low-volume tail with no urgency to convert.
items.detail: NIEHS Synopsis 75N96023Q00128 (posted 16 Aug 2023) was a sole-source intent to buy 4 S1 100-cycle kits (cat. 20028319) and 3 SP 100-cycle kits (cat. 20028401). The same institute then bought a Bronze service plan for 29 Jun 2025 to 28 Jun 2026. A Silver plan notice appeared in 2021. A buyer needing only 7 small flow cells a year is the low-volume tail that the thesis calls less volume-elastic.
items.source_name: NIEHS Office of Acquisitions synopsis PDF
items.why_new: The known list covers the NIEHS Bronze plan downgrade (F620). It does not cover the 2023 S1/SP kit purchase quantities.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: NICHD's 6000 and MiSeq Silver plan ended 14 Feb 2026, and I found no renewal notice. That is ambiguous: it could mean a retired instrument or just an unposted renewal.
items.detail: A search snippet shows NICHD intended a sole-source Silver Support Plan for a NovaSeq 6000 and a MiSeq, covering 15 Feb 2025 to 14 Feb 2026. Two searches found no 2026 successor notice, but SAM.gov was not checked directly. Of five federal 6000 service buyers, NICHD is the only one with no visible follow-on. Federal notices are a small sample of all 6000 owners.
items.why_new: The known list names NICHD only in the probe notes. It has no coverage dates and no renewal check.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Dutch national NIPT uptake is already 73.5% of pregnancies, near the 79.8% scan ceiling, which limits future NIPT volume growth.
items.detail: Under the Dutch screening programme (Peridos registry), NIPT uptake was 51.2% in 2020, 67.8% in 2023 and 73.5% in 2024, from 171,349 pregnancies. Abnormal results stayed at 0.5%. Uptake of the 13-week scan was 79.8% and the 20-week scan 86.9%. NIPT uptake is therefore about 6 points below the 13-week scan. Annual uptake gains slowed from about +5.6 points a year (2020-23) to +5.7 points in 2024, so there is no flattening yet. The 2025 monitor is the test of whether it has plateaued. This is a summary from search results; I did not read the PDF pages.
items.source_name: RIVM / PNS NIPT Monitor 2024 (IQ Health, Radboudumc; Peridos registry)
items.quote: Deelname NIPT is 73,5% en verder toegenomen
items.why_new: This is a national NIPT uptake series, with uptake already high in a universal-access country. Nothing like it is in the exclusion list.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Dutch NIPT uptake was still rising in 2024, up 5.7 points from 2023, so NIPT volume had not yet plateaued.
items.detail: Uptake rose from 67.8% in 2023 to 73.5% in 2024, a relative gain of about 8%, and from 51.2% in 2020. Counselling was registered in 94.9% of pregnancies, against 93.6% in 2023. A plateau is not proven until the 2025 data, which is expected around Jan 2027. This is the watch-out for the NIPT-maturing argument.
items.why_new: This is a quantified counterpoint from a national registry, which the known list lacks.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Illumina does flag discontinued Dx products in GUDID, so the 6000Dx's 'in distribution' status is a real signal, not a stale record.
items.detail: Several legacy Dx DIs are marked 'Not in Commercial Distribution': MiSeqDx Reagent Kit v3 (…071), MiSeqDx Universal Kit, MiSeqDx CF assays (…019/026/033), NextSeq550Dx Reagent Kit v2 (…095), the NextSeq 550Dx LRM FASTQ module (…415) and the Praxis Extended RAS Panel. Because Illumina updates the registry when it retires products, the unflagged 6000Dx kits suggest no retirement is imminent. This leans against the idea that the regulated 6000 tail is about to be forced off.
items.why_new: Gives the registry-retirement pattern for older Illumina Dx lines, which was not in the known list.
items.verify_note: This mostly restates the known 'no 6000 end-of-life notice' point from a new outlet. GUDID 'not in distribution' flags track superseded SKUs (for example MiSeqDx kit versions while the MiSeqDx itself is still sold), not platform retirement, so an unflagged 6000Dx is a weak signal. The thesis's 5 points of 2027 conversion also does not depend on a forced end-of-life.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Illumina's 6000Dx DIs were published in 2022 only, with no 2025-26 additions, which fits a regulated tail that does not convert to the X.
items.detail: The search listings show sequential DIs from 00816270020538 to 00816270020743 for the 6000Dx family. A probe of 00816270020750 returned 404, so the sequence ends at …743. I only verified publish dates for three records (Oct-Nov 2022). I did not verify the dates of the other DIs in the sequence.
items.why_new: Probed the DI sequence boundary; the registry's coverage was not checked before.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: In NCBI's Genetic Testing Registry (GTR), no X-family record with a traceable history shows a NovaSeq 6000 to X switch, while the 6000's largest declarer keeps re-versioning its 6000 records through 2026.
items.detail: The X-family records with checked histories (Michigan's records and four Labcorp/Integrated Genetics MaterniT records) came from the NextSeq 550 or the HiSeq 2000, not the 6000 (F995). Meanwhile Mayo's 104 of 130 6000 records were re-versioned through 2025–26 and still name the 6000 (F960, F961). So the observed 6000→X conversion count in GTR is 0. GTR is self-reported and lightly maintained, so this is a directional read on regulated-lab inertia, not a rate.
items.why_new: D088 treated the 12 X records as evidence of conversion; their origin platforms show they are not 6000 conversions.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Within Labcorp, the price-sensitive NIPT line moved to the X Plus in Nov 2024, but a new whole-genome MRD product registered in Dec 2025 lists the NovaSeq 6000Dx. That fits Thaysen's cohort map, in which NIPT moves and new regulated assays sit on Dx-grade 6000 boxes.
items.detail: Labcorp/Integrated Genetics' MaterniT records read 'Novaseq X Plus' from 2024-11-01 (F963). Labcorp's Plasma Detect Genome MRD-Baseline (619625), registered 2025-12-08, lists 'illumina NovaSeq 6000 Dx' (verified). A whole-genome MRD baseline at ~30x+ is a high-Gb assay. Launching it on the 6000Dx 13 months after the NIPT move suggests large labs' new regulated volume can start on the 6000 tail, which is the high-price-per-Gb part of the fleet.
items.quote: illumina NovaSeq 6000 Dx
items.why_new: Pairs a new Labcorp MRD platform listing with the known MaterniT X move inside one lab group.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: The 100,000 newborn target belongs to the UK Generation Study, not GUARDIAN, and no official GUARDIAN target was found.
items.detail: The Oct 2024 Clinical Trials Arena article ties 'up to 100,000' to the UK Generation Study. The GeneDx Oct 2026 release gives no GUARDIAN target or start date. Any analyst model that assumes GUARDIAN is heading to 100,000 is not supported by these sources. GUARDIAN's 30,000 is also less than a third of the UK program's target.
items.quote: will screen up to 100,000 newborn babies
items.why_new: Corrects the mapping of the 100,000 target in the probe brief; not in the known list.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Brazil's FIOTEC paid R$58,630 for a NovaSeq X 10B kit in Feb 2025, which may be about 30% below Illumina's list price. This is unconfirmed because the kit quantity is unknown.
items.detail: PNCP record 2025/138 (published 14 Feb 2025) is described as a single 'KIT NOVASEQ X SERIES 10B ILLUMINA, CODIGO 2008559', with homologated total R$58,630.31. At an assumed BRL rate of about 5.75 per USD that is about $10.2K. That compares with the $14,493 10B-300 list price from Jan 2025, a gap of about 30%. If the order was for more than one kit, the per-kit discount is deeper. I could not open the item list (the itens endpoint timed out) and the exchange rate is my assumption, so the discount figure is soft.
items.source_name: PNCP (Brazil national procurement portal), FIOTEC direct contracting 10121113/2025
items.quote: KIT NOVASEQ X SERIES 10B ILLUMINA - CODIGO: 2008559
items.why_new: Gives a Brazilian public-buyer price for a 10B kit against the Jan 2025 list. The known list had only Taiwan, Spain and US core prices.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Brazil's HC-FMRP-USP hospital appears to have paid close to list for NovaSeq X 1.5B kits in 2024-25, so there is no sign of a deep public-buyer discount on small X kits.
items.detail: Record 2025/3 (published 2 May 2024) covers 33 MiSeq v2 kits plus 14 NovaSeq X 1.5B-300 kits (P/N 20104705), homologated at R$565,059. 14 kits at the $3,928 list is about $55K. Adding 33 MiSeq v2 kits at an assumed ~$1,100-1,300 each (about $36-43K) gives a total of about $91-98K. R$565K at a BRL rate of 5.1-5.8 is about $97-111K. That is at or slightly above list-implied value, though the MiSeq price and the rate are my assumptions. A second buy (2025/347, May 2025) was R$322,994 for 1.5B kits plus exome prep, with no quantity visible.
items.quote: 14 unidades de KIT NOVASEQ SERIE X 1.5B REAGENT, 300 CICLOS
items.why_new: This is a hospital buyer's small-flow-cell price. It is consistent with the known finding that small X flow cells carry a high $/Gb (Bauer, CAT), but from a different country.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: A Brazilian federal buyer paid R$772,568 in Jul 2025 for a NovaSeq 6000 maintenance plan, which is about the same as Silver-plan service pricing elsewhere.
items.detail: Ministry of Health (INC) record 312/2025, published 15 Jul 2025, covers a 6000 maintenance plan with parts, labor, reagents and remote support, at R$772,568.50. At about 5.5 BRL/USD that is about $140K, matching the roughly 20%-discounted Silver price of $140K implied by earlier federal US notices. Service on the 6000 is therefore still being bought at full price outside the US, with no sign of discounting to keep the tail alive. This is probably the same record as the Brazilian INC buy in F988, so treat it as a price confirmation, not a new buyer.
items.why_new: Only adds the BRL-to-USD price match to the Silver plan; the Brazilian purchase itself is likely already known (F988).

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Absolute Dutch NIPT tests grew only about 8.8% in 2024 (115,828 to 126,023), and about 4.6 of those points came from uptake rather than pregnancies.
items.detail: A search-result summary of the monitor's Figure 1 gives 126,023 NIPTs in 2024 and 115,828 in 2023. Arithmetic: 126,023/115,828 = +8.8%. The 2024 pregnancy count was 171,349 and 126,023/171,349 = 73.5%, which matches the reported uptake. The implied 2023 pregnancy count is 115,828/0.678 = about 170.8K, so pregnancies grew about +0.3% and uptake did almost all the work. Uptake gains can't continue at this pace: 100% would be only +36% in tests from the 2024 level.
items.source_name: RIVM/IQ Health Monitor 2024, Figure 1 (via search summary)
items.why_new: Gives absolute counts and a decomposition; the known list had only percentages.
items.verify_note: Duplicate of F1012's data (115,828→126,023, uptake 73.5%). F1012 keeps the fact. The ceiling arithmetic (at most +36% more tests if uptake reached 100%; about 4–5 years of headroom at +5.7 pts/yr) goes in that note and in the derived Europe-NIPT item.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: The 2024 NIPT uptake sits only 6.3 pts below the 13-week scan uptake of 79.8%, which caps the remaining headroom on any reasonable proxy.
items.detail: The 13-week scan reached 79.8% of pregnancies in 2024 (78.0% in 2023) and the 20-week scan 86.9% (86.6% in 2023). If 79.8% is a practical ceiling, NIPT could grow at most 79.8/73.5 = +8.6% in tests from uptake alone, about one more year at the 2024 pace. Even the 20-week scan at 86.9% implies at most +18%. The ceiling is a proxy, since NIPT does not strictly require the scan. Another year of increments is plausible, but double-digit growth from uptake is not.
items.why_new: The known list notes the 79.8% scan ceiling in F1002 but gives no headroom arithmetic or 20-week comparison.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Dutch NIPT volume was still growing about 9% a year in 2024, so a mature market had not yet stopped adding tests.
items.detail: Tests rose from 115,828 to 126,023 (+8.8%) and uptake rose 5.7 pts in the latest year. The abnormal rate stayed flat at 0.5%, so the case mix did not change. The headroom and the 2025 outcome are unknown, since the 2025 monitor is expected around Jan 2027. A single small country does not set global NIPT trends, and the US is at a different stage.
items.source_name: Kamerstuk 29323 nr. 189 (letter to parliament citing the RIVM monitor)
items.quote: 73,5% van de zwangeren deelnam aan de NIPT
items.why_new: This is the 'against' watch-out for NIPT maturing, a counterweight not yet in the ledger.
items.verify_note: Arithmetic checks: +8.8% tests, 126,023/171,349 = 73.5%, pregnancies about flat (+0.3%), so uptake drove all the growth. The read is against near-term maturity but bounded: at 73.5% uptake, at most ~36% more tests are left. The Netherlands is a small market and is Gb-immaterial (~10K extra tests × 1–2 Gb ≈ 10–20K Gb/yr).

items.label: 1C
items.claim: The Dutch NIPT sequencing load is tiny against Illumina's volume: roughly 126K tests is about 0.02% of high-throughput Gb.
items.detail: At about 1–2 Gb per NIPT (the known range), 126,023 tests is about 126–252 thousand Gb (0.13–0.25 Pb). Against the ~800M Gb annual high-throughput base used in the known list, that is about 0.016–0.03%. A fully saturated Netherlands adds under 0.01% of Gb, and NIPT is a minor Gb source even before maturity. The Gb-per-test and 800M figures are known-list inputs, not from the monitor.
items.why_new: Quantifies the Dutch national program in Gb terms; the known list has no national-program Gb translation.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: The abnormal NIPT rate stayed flat at 0.5%, so there is no sign of rising case-mix depth or follow-on testing intensity in the national program.
items.detail: The share of abnormal results was 0.5% in 2024 and 'comparable to previous years'. Flat positives mean no growth in diagnostic follow-up sequencing per screen. Counselling was registered for 94.9% of the 171,349 pregnancies (93.6% in 2023), so the offer is nearly universal. This leaves volume growth wholly dependent on the last few points of uptake.
items.why_new: Adds the 94.9% counselling coverage and the flat abnormal-rate read, which are not in the known list.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: The Dutch state took over funding of prenatal pre-test counselling from 1 Jan 2025 and plans NIPT roll-out only in Caribbean Netherlands in 2026, so the offer is complete and the next volume steps are marginal.
items.detail: Kamerstuk 29323 nr. 189 (11 Feb 2026) says counselling has been funded from the state budget since 1 Jan 2025, and that RIVM will introduce NIPT and the second-trimester scan in Caribbean Netherlands in 2026. The Caribbean population is tiny, so this adds negligible tests. No announced expansion of the NIPT offer (no new conditions) was found in the letter.
items.why_new: Policy facts about funding and roll-out that are not in the ledger.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Nevada Medicaid added 81420 for dates of service from 1 Jan 2026, with no prior authorization and a limit of 1 unit per 3 rolling months. This is a small state expansion.
items.detail: A search snippet of the Nevada Medicaid announcement (SB 344) gave these terms. I could not read the PDF itself, so the risk-tier criteria are unverified. Nevada has about 3 million residents, so the added volume is small. A Vermont Medicaid form (undated) still limits 81420 to high-risk indications, so some gaps remain.
items.why_new: The known list has no state Medicaid NIPT coverage changes.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: GUARDIAN enrollment pace has been roughly 700 babies a month recently, and the program is far from any 100,000 scale.
items.detail: The first 4,000 babies enrolled from Sep 2022 to Jul 2023, about 364 a month over 11 months. More than 13,000 were enrolled by Oct 2024 (about 520 a month on average since Sep 2022).
