The CGP v2 renewal (M11418E, Jun 2025, Aug 2025–Jul 2028) had a budget of NT$29.894M; the single bid was NT$29.894M and the award NT$27.648M (−7.5%; floor NT$27.8M). The first tender round failed with no bids both times. Annual value fell from about NT$10.4M to about NT$9.2M, so the hospital cut its budget 23% up front instead of extracting a bigger concession. Test quantities are not disclosed.
items.why_new: Previous Taipei VGH findings covered NIPT, WGS and P3/P4 kits, not the clinical CGP contract or its 2022 predecessor.
items.verify_note: Not re-verified (429). The direction is ambiguous. The award-vs-budget discount shrank only because the hospital cut its budget 23% up front, while annual contract value still fell ~11% (NT$10.37M → 9.22M/yr). With no test counts, the net price trend can't be read either way.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Taiwan's flagship hospital NTUH locked in a new 5-year, NT$85.5M in-house pan-cancer DNA NGS program on US-origin reagents with an instrument and room renovation, a new clinical volume source, though a small one.
items.detail: TD14E180 (awarded 17 Oct 2025): budget NT$99.4M, single bid NT$99.4M, award NT$85.5M at the floor (−14.0%). The contract runs 1 Jan 2026 to 31 Dec 2030. The first round failed with no bids. The winner was Illumina's distributor 均泰, so this is very likely an Illumina CGP kit, though the brand is not named. That is about NT$17.1M/yr (~US$0.53M/yr), trivial against Illumina's ~US$1.9B clinical consumables but a dated example of hospitals insourcing CGP.
items.why_new: No previous finding covered NTUH's 5-year CGP reagent-rental contract.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Taiwan's public-hospital outsourced CGP market goes mostly to US central labs (FoundationOne and Guardant360 distributors), concentrating Illumina-run volume in a few large accounts.
items.detail: In the 26 award notices for 'cancer gene' testing from Sep 2025 to Oct 2026 in the PCC title search, the FoundationOne CDx distributor 賈亞基因 is a winner in about 11 and the Guardant360 distributor 威健 in about 8. ACT Genomics (行動基因) wins about 5 and the local lab 慧智基因 about 4. Examples: Taipei VGH Taoyuan branch FoundationOne CDx (Feb 2026), Guardant360 INFINITY (Mar 2026), Taoyuan Hospital Guardant360 (Jul 2026). These counts come from one results page (page 1 of 6) and are approximate.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC title search via pcc-api.openfun.app
items.why_new: Earlier Taiwan findings covered WGS, NIPT and kits, not the outsourced-CGP vendor mix.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Where Taiwanese outsourced NGS lots draw two bidders, prices fall 10–16% below budget, against 0–15% in Illumina-distributor single-bid lots.
items.detail: CDC tuberculosis NGS service (KA115047, Jul 2026): budget NT$3.696M. 圖爾思生物科技 won at NT$3.1152M, 13.2% below Genomics BioSci's NT$3.5904M and 15.7% below budget. The first round failed. Taoyuan Hospital CGP outsourcing (ACTDrug/ACTOnco, KA1150333, Jul 2026): budget and floor NT$6.24M, award NT$5.616M (−10%); the second bidder (Genomics BioSci) was disqualified. Platforms are not named.
items.why_new: New 2026 contested NGS service awards that no earlier finding listed.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: NTUH's clinical exome-kit lot was cut 20% off the distributor's bid in Apr 2025, inside the same 14–20% band seen across Illumina lots, with no sign of deeper concessions.
items.detail: TD140170 'exome kits, 5 items' open contract (Apr 2025–Dec 2026), a restricted tender without public evaluation: budget and bid NT$2,210,740, floor NT$1,768,592, award NT$1,768,000 (−20.0%). Together with NTUH pan-cancer (−14.0%), NTU (−10 to −15.5%) and VRI (−15%), the realized concession band at Illumina's Taiwan distributor is 10–20%. Instrument buys run only 0.8–3.4% below bid: TFDA high-throughput system NT$5.8M→5.6M (May 2025); Chang Gung Linkou Illumina system NT$2.264M→2.245M (Aug 2025).
items.why_new: Adds the NTUH exome, TFDA and Chang Gung lots, which were not cited before, to quantify the concession band.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Taiwan's Veterinary Research Institute raised its Illumina library-reagent spend in each of 2024–26 at a constant ~15% concession, and the kit origin switched from the US to Singapore.
items.detail: Lots: Sep 2024 NT$1.125M (origin US); Oct 2025 NT$1.246M (+10.8% y/y, origin Singapore); Oct 2026 about NT$1.6M (known from F985). The concession off the opening bid was 15.0% and 15.1%. This is government research demand rising, not falling, and showing no price fight.
items.why_new: Adds the 2024 and 2025 points behind the known 2026 lot to make a 3-year series.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: UMGC's public sequencing queue lists almost no NovaSeq X Plus work, while AVITI and Ultima UG100 carry most of the rows.
items.detail: A fetched snapshot (undated, rows with est. completion Apr 2026 to Jan 2027) shows about 463 run rows. AVITI-Standard has 249 (54%), UG100 has 206 (44%), UG100-MOSS has 6 and NovaSeq X Plus has 2 (under 0.5%). This is where UMGC's in-house runs are tracked, because Illumina X Plus work is outsourced, so the NovaSeq X row count is not a share measure. It does show that a Midwest academic core's in-house research queue is almost entirely non-Illumina, and that UG100 is a large second queue (206 rows).
items.why_new: The corpus had UMGC price evaluations only; this is the first queue-level count by platform.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Ultima runs a full-size queue at UMGC, including 10B-read wafers, in an academic core whose AVITI costs have already fallen.
items.detail: UG100 rows use 1x250 kits, half wafers of 5B reads and full wafers of 10B reads. Their est. completion runs to 27 Jan 2027, and 102 of 206 rows are at Post Run QC, 53 in library prep and 8 sequencing. UG100-MOSS (a separate queue with 5B half wafers) has another 6 rows. The kit sizes are the same scale as the outsourced X Plus 25B lane (2.5B reads), so a single UG100 wafer carries 2-4x the reads of a 25B lane. That is consistent with academic buyers using Ultima for cheap bulk reads.
items.why_new: Ultima queue depth and kit mix at a named academic core was not in the corpus.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: UChicago's internal rate for a 25B 2x150 lane is $2,461, about $2.46/Gb, and AVITI 300bp costs the same as an X 10B 2x100 lane.
items.detail: The core's current page lists NovaX-25B-300 at $2,461 per lane internal ($2,599 commercial). It lists NovaX-10B-300 at $1,499 and AVITI-300bp at $1,475 per flow cell internal. At an assumed ~1,000 Gb per 25B lane, the rate is roughly $2.5/Gb, within the known $2.1-$3.5/Gb core range (CWRU $2.63, Utah $2.89). It shows no price trend because the page has no date or history. It adds one more core price point, not a new insight.
items.source_name: University of Chicago Genomics Facility rate card
items.why_new: UChicago is not in the core rate-card list already used, but its price level matches known cores.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The 6000 service notice count is small and flat, and the notices are mostly tied to single government-owned boxes, so they do not show a growing tail.
items.detail: I found about 8 dated US 6000-related service notices: 2024: NIEHS (Apr), CDC (Oct). 2025: NICHD (coverage from Feb), NIA (Mar), NIEHS Bronze (Jun), Navy (Dec), Frederick M26-159 (Dec 2025 deadline). 2026: NCI A01064 (Aug). That is about 2 in 2024, 4–5 in 2025 and 1–2 so far in 2026. Mirror sites are incomplete and SAM.gov could not be opened, so no trend can be claimed. Also, every notice is a one-year renewal, which means agencies could stop buying at any anniversary.
items.why_new: This is the first notice count by year; it shows no acceleration of federal 6000 service demand.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: A Taiwan hospital's NGS Down syndrome screening open contract was awarded at NT$6,000 per test with only about 150 tests estimated over two years, and the sibling NTUH Hsinchu contract failed twice.
items.detail: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University Hospital contract 114155L54 failed its first tender on 2025-12-26 for lack of bidders. It was awarded on 2025-12-31 (published 2026-01-02) to a single bidder, Bionet (訊聯生物), at a budget and award of NT$900,000. That is NT$6,000 per test on an estimated 150 tests over a contract term of 2026-01-01 to 2027-12-31. NTUH Hsinchu GH151020 has a NT$195,000 budget. Its tenders on 2026-06-26 and 2026-07-21 both failed (no bids or too few bidders), and a third tender was issued on 2026-07-30. Together these suggest very small, thinly bid NIPT volume at public hospitals. This is a niche procurement and only weakly informative about Illumina.
items.why_new: Not in the known list: Taiwan public-hospital NGS NIPT tender prices and failed-award history.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: UMGC's open sequencing queue (Oct 2026) holds 463 run rows, and 461 of them (99.6%) are on Element AVITI or Ultima UG100. Only 2 rows are on NovaSeq X Plus.
items.detail: The rows split into AVITI-Standard 249 (80 projects), UG100 206 (38 projects), UG100-MOSS 6 (5 projects) and NovaSeq X plus 2. The completion dates run from 4/20/2026 to 1/27/2027. This quantifies the qualitative finding (F1095) that the queue lists almost no X Plus work. The counts come from a summarizing fetch and I did not verify them row by row. Caveat: UMGC outsources most X Plus work, so the queue cannot be read as UMGC's total Illumina volume.
items.source_name: UMGC NGS Sequencing Queues (published Google Sheet)
items.why_new: Gives exact row and project counts by platform for the queue, where F1095 gave only a qualitative description.
items.verify_note: Could not verify. The UMGC page links to a published Google Sheet that did not render, so the row counts rest on the original agent's fetch alone. Because X+ work is outsourced by policy (F1068), the queue shows UMGC's in-house capacity mix, not its users' Illumina consumption. Overlaps with F1068.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: By nominal kit reads, the queue is about 2,060B reads on Ultima and about 326B on AVITI, against about 3.75B on X Plus.
items.detail: Ultima: 200 rows of '1x250 (10B reads)' plus 12 half wafers at 5B comes to 2,000 + 60 = 2,060B. AVITI: 182×1.5 + 25×1.5 + 17×0.1 + 11×0.375 + 7×0.75 + 6×0.75 + 1×0.3 = 326B. X Plus: one 10B run (1.25B) plus one 25B run (2.5B) comes to 3.75B. These are nominal kit reads, not delivered reads or Gb. Ultima's nominal reads are about 6x AVITI's and over 500x X Plus's. Ultima is 38 projects (+5 MOSS) against 80 for AVITI.
items.source_name: UMGC NGS Sequencing Queues (published Google Sheet)
items.why_new: Converts the queue into reads by platform, which no known item did. It shows rival short-read volume at a large research core is dominated by Ultima.
items.verify_note: Unverified, for the same reason as F1100. Arithmetic check: the AVITI rows sum to 249 ✓. The Ultima math (200 full + 12 half = 212 rows) only reconciles if the 6 MOSS rows are included with the 206 UG100 rows. These are nominal kit reads, and Ultima reads are single-end, so the comparison overstates Ultima versus paired-end AVITI or X. The '>500x X Plus' figure is meaningless given that X+ is outsourced.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: UMGC's 463 queued runs show a research core running its volume on non-Illumina platforms. Most queued runs are still in prep or waiting for sequencing, not finished.
items.detail: By status: 231 post-run QC, 112 in library prep, 64 in sequencing queue, 23 sequencing, 15 scheduled, 9 delayed, 9 blank. About 223 of the 463 rows (48%) were not yet sequenced, and 48 rows had no completion date. That points to steady demand for cheap rival runs through Jan 2027. It is demand at a single academic core, so it cannot be scaled to the market.
items.source_name: UMGC NGS Sequencing Queues (published Google Sheet)
items.why_new: Adds status and backlog mix to a queue that was previously only described by platform.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: UMGC's AVITI queue is about 80% 1.5B-read 2x150/2x75 High runs, so the rival's standard product is the main tier cutting into Illumina's mid-throughput business.
items.detail: 2x150 High (1.5B) has 182 rows and 2x75 High (1.5B) has 25. Together that is 207 of 249 AVITI rows, or 83%. The platform-wide price pressure is documented elsewhere (UMGC AVITI costs fell 46–51% in FY26), so this adds only which tier customers actually book. It does not give a price.
items.source_name: UMGC NGS Sequencing Queues (published Google Sheet)
items.why_new: Gives the actual kit-tier mix of booked AVITI runs; earlier items covered only the price sheet.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Universitat de Lleida's 2026 tariff reportedly prices a NovaSeq X 25B lane at €3,096 to €4,087 depending on tier, about €3.44 to €4.54 per Gb.
items.detail: A search-tool summary of the UdL sheet (file saved 14 Jul 2026, prices ex-VAT) lists a 25B 150PE lane of 900 Gb at €3,095.80, €3,591.13 and €4,087.13 across three tiers. I could not decode the PDF myself, so this is unverified. If correct, the Spanish academic spread is about 32% from the first to the third tier, and the first tier is well above the IDIBAPS tender of about €2.00/Gb and CIBER's about €12,800 per flow cell. That would show how far small-institute prices sit above large-account prices. The €/Gb figures are the search tool's arithmetic on a 900 Gb lane (the 900 Gb figure is as reported by the tool; not checked).
items.source_name: Universitat de Lleida SCTS tariff (search-result snippet only)
items.why_new: The UdL tariff is not in the list of core rate cards already used, and it is a Spanish small-institute 25B price point.

items.label: 2A
items.claim: NIH intramural sequencing buys Illumina consumables sole-source, so no competitive price pressure appears in this vehicle.
items.detail: NIH awarded IDV 75N98026D00035 to Illumina in May 2026 with 1 bid received. It has a $90M ceiling over a 5-year ordering period (to 21 May 2031) and $5.4M obligated so far (6%). The prior NISC contract was extended through 2 Mar 2026 by non-competitive modification. No discount terms or kit mix are published.
items.why_new: The 75N98026D00035 ceiling, term and sole-source status were not in the known list, though this is probably the same vehicle as F765.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: A Tempus xT record for the Research Triangle Park (RTP) lab was registered on the 6000 in Nov 2024, so a new Tempus registration was filed on the 6000 two years after the X launched.
items.detail: GTR000613444.1 was registered 2024-11-06 with the NovaSeq 6000 for both methods. Its lab-level annual review date is 2025-11-12. The Chicago xT record (558436) shows the same instrument. Tempus's main tissue test is therefore declared on the 6000 at both labs.
items.why_new: Gives the registration date and the RTP-lab record for Tempus, which was not itemised before.
items.verify_note: Duplicate of F962, which already cites GTR000613444.1 (Tempus RTP xT, registered 2024-11-06, NovaSeq 6000, reviewed 2025-11-12). The only addition is the Chicago xT record 558436, and F996 already covers stale Tempus records.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The one confirmed instrument change in GTR for an X Plus lab is Labcorp's MaterniT NIPT line, and it moved from the HiSeq 2000 straight to the X Plus.
items.detail: MaterniT21 (501985) and MaterniT GENOME (569955) both list 'Illumina HiSeq 2000' in versions dated 2020-01-09 and 'Novaseq X Plus' in versions dated 2024-11-01. Version .4 of 501985 is the switch. The 4 X Plus hits for Integrated Genetics–Sequenom are 501985, 569955, 593063 and 593064. This is a clean, dated platform change by a price-sensitive NIPT line. No 6000-to-X switch was found, because the 6000 step was skipped (see F995, F963 and D091).
items.why_new: Gives the exact before and after instruments and version dates (HiSeq 2000 in Jan 2020 to X Plus in Nov 2024). Earlier items only say 'switches came from older platforms'.
items.verify_note: Restatement. F963, F995, D090 and D091 already record that the Labcorp/Integrated Genetics MaterniT records moved to the X Plus on 2024-11-01 and that the prior platform was the HiSeq 2000. The 2020-01-09 HiSeq 2000 entry is also a stale registry field, not a dated instrument change, so the 'skipped the 6000' reading is not established.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: A Taiwan hospital's per-test price for outsourced Guardant360 liquid biopsy fell about 23% in about 10 months.
items.detail: Taoyuan Hospital (MOHW) awarded Guardant360 outsourcing at NT$107,000 per test (est. 14 tests, NT$1.498M, awarded 2 Sep 2025, Welgene). Its next award, on 30 Jun 2026, was NT$82,000 per test (est. 93 tests, NT$7.626M, one bidder, 3-year term to Jun 2029, ceiling NT$9.951M). The estimated volume rose 6.6x as the unit price fell. That is the volume-for-price pattern the thesis describes at a central CGP lab, but Taiwan is a tiny market and the price is for the whole test.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC (openfun API), Taoyuan Hospital award notices KA1140010 and KA1150413
items.why_new: No Taiwan procurement per-test CGP price series was in the known evidence.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: The FoundationOne CDx per-test price at Taoyuan Hospital did not fall between 2023 and 2025.
items.detail: Taoyuan Hospital paid NT$99,750 per test in Aug 2023 (14 tests, Taiwan SME winner; derived from NT$1,396,500 ÷ 14). In Feb 2025 it paid NT$99,750 per test (60 tests, NT$5.985M, Vita Genomics). The price was flat while the estimated volume rose 4.3x. Tissue CGP, a branded and regulated test, shows no price erosion in this data. That is consistent with the idea that branded clinical tests are insulated from price pressure.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC (openfun API), Taoyuan Hospital award notices AA1120012 and AA1140001
items.why_new: This is a new price series for FoundationOne CDx, and it shows branded CGP prices holding flat.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Mayo's aortopathy panel (CAORG) has been re-versioned four times since 2024 and still lists the 6000, so the registry's largest 6000 declarer keeps re-committing to it.
items.detail: GTR000603752 has seven versions. The dates are 2022-12-15, 2023-03-30, 2024-05-14, 2025-04-03, 2025-07-15, 2025-09-16 and 2026-04-09. The latest version (.7) lists the NovaSeq 6000 for both methods. Three of the edits fall in the last 12 months, and none changes the sequencer.
items.why_new: The known list already says Mayo re-versioned its 6000 tests (F961). This only adds the exact version dates for one test.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: The GTR instrument field is unreliable for two big NGS reporters, so GTR cannot support a count of the 6000 versus the X.
items.detail: Guardant360 (527948) was last updated 2021-08-12 and lists 'Other' as the instrument with a platform of 'None/not applicable'. Natera's Panorama (503131) was last updated 2020-07-21 and gives no instrument. The tokenised 'NovaSeq X' search returns tests that name only the 6000, as with the Tempus and Mayo hits. Search listings also show no instrument.
items.why_new: This is a data-quality caveat for the GTR counts (11x, 130 vs 12). It is not evidence for or against the thesis itself.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The 6000's Clarity LIMS integration has had only security-patch releases in 2026, while the X integration got new features.
items.detail: 6000 API v3.7.0 (Jul 2024) moved properties into the database. v3.7.1 (Apr 2026) fixed security vulnerabilities and an error-log retry. v3.7.2 (Jun 2026, document version 5) lists no features, only 'Fixed security vulnerabilities'. The X Series v1.4.0 integration (Apr 2026) added 5B flow-cell support, 1.5B with the 600-cycle kit, and a new v2.0 sequencing workflow. The 6000 integration has therefore had no feature in about 27 months (Jul 2024 to Oct 2026), and the X integration gained new flow cells in 2026.
items.source_name: Illumina Clarity LIMS help: NovaSeq6k API v3.7.x and NovaSeq X v1.4.0 release notes
items.quote: Fixed security vulnerabilities.
items.why_new: Not in the known list. The 2026 LIMS patch history shows maintenance-only mode for the 6000 against active X development.
items.verify_note: New at the LIMS-integration level, but it only extends F1053/F1054 (control-software cadence). Feature-freeze on a mature integration is expected and says nothing about the pace of conversion. Its value is as a de-prioritisation signal only.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Illumina still patches and releases software for the 6000 and 6000Dx in 2026, and no end-of-sale or end-of-support notice appears on the downloads pages.
items.detail: 6000 v1.8.2 shipped 25 Aug 2025. The 6000 and 6000Dx LIMS integrations had patches in Apr 2026 (6000Dx v1.3.1) and Jun 2026 (6000 v3.7.2 and 6000Dx v1.3.2). The 6000 and 6000Dx downloads pages contain no end-of-sale, end-of-life or last-time-buy wording. The earlier S895 pass found the same for the 6000 page.
items.source_name: Illumina Clarity LIMS help; Illumina support downloads
items.why_new: The 2026 dated patch trail and the absence of any EOS notice are not in the known list. It cuts against an imminent forced sunset.
items.verify_note: Mostly a restatement of F1053 and the known 'product page live with no end-of-life'. The only new detail is the 6000Dx LIMS security patches, which are routine maintenance and not a commitment to longevity. It also conflicts in spirit with F1112, which uses the same data.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The 6000 integration guide v3.2.1 is a legacy document: it names no X support and describes SP-flow-cell features.
items.detail: The page describes the v3.2.1 Sequencer API move, SPrime flow cell support, long reads on SP only and asymmetric read lengths. It names RTA3 and bcl2fastq2 v2.20 and mentions no NovaSeq X. The guide pairs with LIMS 4.2.x and 5.x. Later releases exist (v3.3.0 for NVCS v1.7.0, v3.4.0 for NVCS v1.8.0, and v3.7.x). The 6000 integration line is mature, with its last feature release in Jul 2024.
items.why_new: It dates the integration versions and shows no X crossover.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: California Medi-Cal broadened genome sequencing coverage and set payment at 100% of Medicare from 1 Jul 2026, easing a payer gate on WGS volume.
items.detail: GeneDx's Q2'26 release (3 Aug 2026) says it received Medi-Cal genome pricing effective 1 Jul 2026, published at 100% of the Medicare rate. Coverage had been announced for 1 Nov 2025 with no age or place-of-service limit, covering 14.7M enrollees (XiFin/Laboratory Economics, 22 Dec 2025). Medicare rates are 81425 $5,031, 81426 $2,710 and 81427 $2,338. This is a reimbursement price point that helps WGS adoption, but it is per test and not per Gb, and no volume estimate exists.
items.quote: Received California Medicaid (Medi-Cal) pricing for genome sequencing effective July 1, 2026
items.why_new: Known list covers GeneDx test growth but not the Medi-Cal WGS rate or its effective date.
items.verify_note: Verified in the GeneDx Q2'26 release: Medi-Cal genome pricing effective 1 Jul 2026 at 100% of Medicare. It is new to the corpus. Effect on Gb is small and unquantified, and payment is per test. Merge with F1116 when reporting.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Medi-Cal's Nov 2025 expansion removed age and setting limits on six genome and genomic codes, and the article expects test counts to rise substantially.
items.detail: Before 1 Nov 2025, 81425-81427 were covered only for infants in inpatient ICU (rapid WGS, since 1 Jan 2022). The expansion adds outpatient use with TAR and frequency limits. It also covers MRD code 0340U (Medicare $3,590). The article says 30 states plus Puerto Rico have only limited Medicaid WGS coverage, so California is the broadest. It gives no fiscal or volume figure.
items.quote: could increase substantially
items.why_new: Known list has Medicare MRD and CMS CLFS items but not the Medi-Cal WGS and MRD coverage expansion.
items.verify_note: Adds the scope of the Nov 2025 expansion (outpatient, prior authorisation (TAR) with frequency limits, 0340U MRD code). 'Could increase substantially' is a newsletter opinion with no numbers. Largely overlaps F1115.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Payer gates on genome volume are opening broadly: 39 state Medicaid programs now cover outpatient exome and/or genome, and Carelon covers genome for up to 56M lives from 14 Jun 2026.
items.detail: GeneDx Q2'26 release: Texas Medicaid added exome 1 May 2026, Mississippi covers both from 1 Jul 2026, 39 states in total, Carelon commercial benefit manager from 14 Jun 2026. GeneDx guides FY26 exome/genome volume growth of at least 30% and Q3'26 33,200 tests. This is a real volume lever for deep (exome and genome) Gb, though the scale is small against Illumina's base.
items.why_new: Known list has Medi-Cal alone; the 39-state count, Carelon 56M lives and Q3 volume guide are new.
items.verify_note: Verified: 39 state Medicaid programs, Carelon outpatient genome coverage effective 14 Jun 2026 covering 'up to 56 million' lives, FY26 exome/genome growth guide of at least 30%, Q3 guide of 33,200 tests. The known list had only GeneDx's +32%; the payer facts are new. The Gb scale is tiny (see derived item).

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Sequencing is a small share of the Medi-Cal genome payment, so cost is not the binding constraint on genome volume.
items.detail: Medicare/Medi-Cal 81425 is $5,031 (the DHCS page snippet shows $5,031.20 for 1 Jul 2026), and rapid trio is 81425 plus two 81426, i.e. $5,031+2x$2,710 = $10,451. A 30x genome at about 100-125 Gb and a ~$2.3/Gb 25B price is ~$230-290 of Illumina reagent, about 5% of 81425 and ~7-8% of the trio payment (3 genomes, ~$700-860). Payment is set by the payer fee schedule and the reagent share is small, so a further 20% Illumina price cut changes lab economics by only ~1%. The Gb per genome and $/Gb are assumptions from the known list.
items.why_new: Known list notes Medi-Cal coverage but not the reagent-to-reimbursement share arithmetic.
items.verify_note: Restates the known findings that sequencing is ~5–10% of clinical workflow cost and that a $100→$80 cut changes lab cost ~5%, using a new denominator. It is built entirely on assumed Gb per genome and the GSA list $/Gb, not net prices. Rapid trio WGS is usually billed under PLA/0425U-type codes, not 81425+2×81426, so the trio arithmetic is also uncertain.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Medi-Cal's genome rate is fee-schedule-fixed, so genome labs' margin gains come only from cutting their own costs, which pressures Illumina to share savings.
items.detail: The Medi-Cal 1 Jul 2026 rate is 100% of Medicare ($5,031 for 81425). A state plan snippet states a floor of 70% of Medicare and a triennial reset from 1 Jul 2026 to the average of the lowest third-party payer prices. If rates reset downward in future cycles, labs will push reagent suppliers harder. The state plan amendment (SPA 26-0019) appeared as 'Pending' in search results, so the rate-setting rules are not confirmed as approved.
items.source_name: DHCS clinical lab rate methodology (search snippet)
items.why_new: Adds the triennial lowest-price reset and 70% floor mechanics, which were not in the known list.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Medi-Cal's coverage covers a 14.7M-enrollee population with no age or place-of-service limit, a potentially large rare-disease and pediatric volume pool.
items.detail: Coverage for six codes (81425-81427, 81228, 81229, 0340U) from 1 Nov 2025 widened from inpatient neonates only. Some codes have TAR and frequency limits, so utilization is gated. Even 10,000 extra genomes at ~110 Gb is ~1.1M Gb, about 0.14% of the ~800M Gb HT base on the known list, so the effect on Illumina volume is small.
items.why_new: Quantifies the Gb scale of Medi-Cal against the known HT base.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: The same hospital's Guardant360 contracted volume rose about 4.4x per year when the per-test price fell 23%, which shows clinical demand is price-elastic.
items.detail: The Sep 2025 award covered 14 tests over 24 months, about 7 a year, at NT$107,000. The Jul 2026 award covers 93 tests over 36 months, about 31 a year, at NT$82,000 (31/7 = 4.4x). The 2020 contract was 40 tests over 24 months, about 20 a year, at NT$144,000. Volume does not move in a straight line with price, because these are hospital estimates and not actuals, and the base is tiny. Even so, falling per-test prices coincide with a much larger volume commitment. That supports the 'volume will respond to price' side and cuts against 1C and 2A, though the scale is trivial against Illumina's high-throughput Gb.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC procurement via openfun API
items.why_new: F745 and F1108 cover other series; this is a new Guardant360 volume-vs-price pair.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: The 2026 Guardant360 price cut at this hospital (about NT$25K per test) is far larger than the roughly $200 per test Guardant said it saves by moving to the NovaSeq X.
items.detail: The price fell from NT$107,000 (Sep 2025) to NT$82,000 (Jul 2026), a cut of NT$25,000. At about NT$30–32 per US$ that is roughly $780–830 per test. The known figure for Guardant's X saving is about $200 per test (Guardant360 Liquid LDT moved to the X in May 2026). The cut is about 4x the stated saving, so the customer is competing on price or passing through more than sequencing savings. That implies pressure on suppliers, including Illumina, in the central-lab chain. This is my inference. FX is assumed, and Taiwan list prices may not follow US pricing.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC procurement via openfun API
items.why_new: Compares the Taiwan price cut with the known $200 X saving, which no earlier item does.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: FoundationOne CDx and FoundationOne Liquid CDx were awarded at an identical NT$99,750 per test across 2023–2025, with no discounting.
items.detail: FoundationOne CDx at MOHW Taoyuan was NT$1,396,500 for 14 tests in Aug 2023 (AA1120012). That is NT$99,750 by division, since the notice shows no unit price. It was NT$99,750 × 60 = NT$5,985,000 in Feb 2025 (AA1140001, winner Vita Genomics, single bid). FoundationOne Liquid CDx was NT$99,750 × 15 = NT$1,496,250 in Aug 2025 (KA1140008, Vita Genomics, single bid). FoundationOne tests run on Illumina but are priced as a captive, validated central-lab product. The flat price is a counterexample to broad deflation. Guardant360 at the same hospital fell, which suggests the pressure falls on LDT-style tests and not on FDA-approved ones.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC procurement via openfun API
items.why_new: F1109 only said FoundationOne CDx was flat; this adds the Liquid CDx price and shows the flat price held across the Feb 2025 and Aug 2025 awards.
items.verify_note: Verified for AA1140001: 60 tests × NT$99,750 = NT$5,985,000, with budget, base price and award all equal, one bidder (Vita Genomics), awarded 13 Feb 2025. This is the price of a finished test from Roche/Foundation's distributor, not Illumina's reagent price, so it says little about Illumina's discounting. Foundation is also an AXELIOS adopter. The Guardant360 decline at the same hospital was not verified.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: FoundationOne CDx volume contracted at Taoyuan was 60 tests for the 2025 award versus 14 tests in 2023, at the same price, which is volume growth driven by demand and not price.
items.detail: Aug 2023 award: 14 tests over 24 months, about 7 a year. Feb 2025 award: 60 tests over about 36 months (Feb 2025–Feb 2028), about 20 a year (2.9x). Unit price stayed NT$99,750 in both. Liquid CDx adds 15 tests over 24 months, about 7.5 a year. This shows clinical NGS volume rising at a constant price, so cost is not the constraint. It also means the hospital's growth is a reimbursement and adoption story. Scale is tiny.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC procurement via openfun API
items.why_new: New pairing of unchanged price with a 2.9x volume rise on the FoundationOne CDx line.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Welgene was awarded Taipei VGH Taoyuan's 4-item bundle (Guardant360 INFINITY) at 5.1% below budget, after the 2025 tender had to be re-run.
items.detail: TY11500201 (award 11 Mar 2026): NT$3,750,000 against budget NT$3,950,000 and reserve NT$3,777,636. That is 5.1% below budget and 0.7% below the reserve. Contract period is 10 Mar 2026 to 31 Dec 2028 with one bidder. A prior notice, TY114112702 (28 Nov 2025), failed. The failed first round and the repeat at a lower reserve suggest budget reduction pressure. The bundle has no unit price, so it can't be compared with the 2025 rates.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC procurement via openfun API
items.why_new: Fills the gap listed in the probe notes for TY11500201; the award total was not previously known.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Guardant360 at Taichung Hospital was awarded at exactly budget (NT$1.47M, one bidder) in Dec 2025, which shows no discount at that buyer.
items.detail: TH114240: award, original bid, reserve and budget are all NT$1,470,000. The method was limited tender with one bidder (Welgene), for a 1 Jan–31 Dec 2026 contract. The notice gives no unit price or test count. So this buyer shows no concession in a single-bid channel, unlike Taoyuan's 23% drop seven months later.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC procurement via openfun API
items.why_new: Fills a priority gap; the notice has no unit price, so it is only an at-budget datapoint.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: National Taiwan University Hospital's cancer branch locked in a NT$14.25M two-year Guardant360 contract in Jan 2024, versus NT$5.7M at its Hsinchu branch in 2023, so large buyers lock in volume.
items.detail: AD120120 (Jan 2024, NTUH Cancer Center branch): NT$14,250,000 for Feb 2024–Feb 2026, one bidder (Kangcheng). GD12301A (Hsinchu branch, Feb 2023): NT$5,700,000, one year, one bidder, set equal to budget. Both are lump sums, so no per-test price is available. These are one-bid, at-budget awards, so no price erosion appears in this channel, and the amounts show real clinical liquid-biopsy volume. Scale is still small against Illumina volume.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC procurement via openfun API
items.why_new: Fills two priority gaps (GD12301A and AD120120) with award totals.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: Guardant360 awards in 2022 at Taoyuan were at 99–99% of budget (NT$981K of NT$990K; NT$9.81M of NT$9.9M), with a single bidder each.
items.detail: AA1110012 (Sep 2022): NT$981,000 vs NT$990,000 budget (−0.9%), one bidder (Kangcheng), one-year term. AA1110013 (Oct 2022): NT$9,810,000 vs NT$9,900,000 (−0.9%), three-year term, estimated quantity 1 and no unit price. Single-bid awards in 2022 show almost no price concession. The 2025–26 drop therefore came from a contract reset and not from an incremental annual concession.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC procurement via openfun API
items.why_new: Fills the AA1110012 and AA1110013 gaps; no unit price is available, so the 2022 per-test price is unknown.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: UMGC's Ultima WGS price list decomposes to about $3.3K per wafer plus only ~$55 per sample for prep, QC and analysis, so sequencing is ~70% of a $192 research genome and Ultima's per-Gb price gap passes almost straight through to the customer.
items.detail: Each Ultima batch fills about one wafer. 24×$192 = $4,608 (30x), 18×$238 = $4,284 (60x), 12×$329 = $3,948 (90x). Solving the 30x and 90x batches gives non-sequencing cost ≈ ($4,608−$3,948)/12 ≈ $55/sample and a wafer ≈ $3,290. That predicts the 60x batch at $4,280 vs $4,284 listed, and the wafer matches UMGC's stand-alone UG100 wafer list of $3,204 (F1066). Sequencing is therefore ~$137 of a $192 30x genome (~71%), or ~$1.1–1.3/Gb. Doing the same split on AVITI (4×$407 = $1,628 less a $1,175 High run) gives ~$113/sample prep and ~$294 sequencing per genome. For research WGS, sequencing is not a 5–10% cost, so vendor price gaps drive buying decisions directly.
items.source_name: UMGC human WGS page and UG100 rate (F1066)
items.quote: Includes sample QC, PCR-free library preparation, 30x sequencing, data QC and analysis
items.why_new: Known items give UMGC per-read Ultima prices and 'sequencing is 5–10% of workflow'; none splits an all-in research genome into wafer vs prep cost, and this split contradicts the low-share framing for research WGS.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: At NTU College of Medicine the annual ceiling of the new Element AVITI reagent contract (~NT$4.35M/yr) is about twice that of its latest Illumina reagent lot (~NT$2.2M/yr), which suggests the fall in Illumina ceilings is substitution to Element rather than price alone.
items.detail: NTU CoM's Illumina reagent lot ceilings fell from ~NT$10.5M/yr (2022–23) to ~NT$2.2M/yr (lot 1142A007, Oct 2025–Jul 2028, sample-prep reagents only; F1088). The same unit bought an AVITI24 (F885) and signed AVITI reagent contract 1143A024 for NT$13.318M over Dec 2025–Dec 2028, ~NT$4.35M/yr (~US$140K; D084). The two contracts overlap in time, so Element's ceiling is now ~2x Illumina's at this research buyer. Both are ceilings, not invoiced spend, and Illumina sequencing reagents may be bought through other vehicles.
items.why_new: Connects F1088's Illumina ceiling decline to D084's AVITI reagent contract at the same institution; neither item made the comparison.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: In Taiwan's public channel, Illumina-distributor single bids settle at a near-constant ~85% of the opening bid across buyers and years (2022–2026), and the only deviations are smaller concessions, so there is no sign of accelerating discounts there.
items.detail: Opening-bid-to-award cuts: NTU College of Medicine −15.5%, −15.1%, −15.0%, −15.2% (2022–24) and −10.0% (Oct 2025); Veterinary Research Institute −15.0% (2024) and −15.1% (2025); Taiwan CDC −15.4% (Aug 2026, award 1% above base); Tri-Service iSeq/NextSeq lines 0% vs base (Sep 2026); Taipei VGH CGP −20% (2022) → −7.5% (2025). The steady ~15% reflects buyers' floor-price setting, not vendor discretion, so it cannot show discounts accelerating, and the 2025–26 exceptions all move toward less discount. Caveat: unit volumes are undisclosed, and budgets were sometimes cut before tender (Taipei VGH CGP −23%).
items.why_new: Pools single-bid concession data across five Taiwanese buyers and explains the ~15% as a procurement artifact; earlier items read each lot on its own.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: At Taichung VGH's 2026-28 NextSeq 2000 kit award, the discount to budget grows with kit size: 5.6% on P2 but 21% on P3.
items.detail: Award BDM-1-71284672 (17 Sep 2026, one bidder, Genomics BioSci) compares each tier's floor-price award with its budget. P1: NT$1.38M vs NT$1.47M, −6.1%. P2: NT$6.417M vs NT$6.7965M, −5.6%. P3: NT$9.48M vs NT$12.0M, −21.0%. P4: NT$2.64M vs NT$3.12M, −15.4%. On the hospital's own budgeted quantities (60 P3 kits), P3 works out to about NT$158K per kit against a NT$200K budget. The deepest cuts land on the high-output tiers, and no rival was needed to produce them. The award equals the floor on every line, so the hospital was pricing against its own reserve rather than a bid war. This is a mid-throughput lot, so it is only an analogy for large accounts' extra discounts on the X.
items.why_new: Earlier items give only the P3/P4 headline or a Taipei-vs-Taichung gap. This is the item-by-item discount ladder, which shows concessions rising with volume tier.
items.verify_note: Figures verified (award date 15 Sep 2026, notice 17 Sep). Correction 1: 'floor-price award' means award at the hospital's own base price, which was set below budget. Most of the 21% on P3 is that reserve, not negotiation; the bid-to-award cuts were P1 −4.2%, P2 −4.1%, P3 −12.2%, P4 −12.0%. Correction 2: the notice names only '定序試劑組 (300循環)' (300-cycle sequencing reagent kits), not NextSeq 2000, so the platform is unconfirmed. items.label: 1B
items.claim: Taiwan public sequencer-system awards show no rival-driven price war. Element's AVITI discount to budget (5.8%) sits inside Illumina's distributor range (0.8% to 15.3%).
items.detail: Each of these had one bidder. Academia Sinica AVITI (29 May 2026) awarded NT$9.20M vs NT$9.768M budget, −5.82%, a restricted-tender award under Art. 22(1)(2) with no competing platform. Genetech (Illumina's distributor) awards: Chang Gung Linkou Illumina NGS system NT$2.245M vs NT$2.264M (−0.84%, Aug 2025); NTU Yunlin high-throughput sequencer NT$5.05M vs NT$5.35M (−5.6%, May 2025); NTU sequencer upgrade NT$3.98M vs NT$4.7M (−15.3%, Apr 2025). The Genetech mean is about −7.2%, a similar range to Element's. Buyers using sole-source clauses for AVITI also never test Illumina's price.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC, Academia Sinica 115-IMBE016; Chang Gung 0C-1L0324; NTU Yunlin YL-A24008; NTU 1140299
items.why_new: This puts the AVITI and Illumina-distributor instrument discounts side by side from the same API, with the arithmetic. Earlier items cover each channel separately.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: Ultima and MGI/DNBSEQ are absent from Taiwan's public procurement system, so the rival price pressure in Taiwan's public sector comes only from Element and nanopore.
items.detail: Title searches on the PCC API returned 0 records for 'DNBSEQ', and 'Ultima' returned only Horiba ICP spectrometer notices. 'AVITI' returned a single record (Academia Sinica, 29 May 2026). Searching '定序儀' returns 793 records, and none on page 1 (99 rows, Apr 2025 to Oct 2026) names an MGI or Ultima instrument. The rival short-read threat to Taiwanese public research buyers is therefore Element (about 5 platform or reagent awards) plus nanopore, not the cheapest per-Gb platforms. I read only page 1 of 8 of the sequencer search.
items.why_new: A zero-count check that other items did not run. It is a watch-out that rivals' lowest $/Gb platforms have no visible public-tender presence in Taiwan.

items.label: 2B
items.claim: When two bidders competed on a Taiwan CDC high-throughput sequencing service, the award fell 15.7% below budget, and the Illumina-based incumbent outsourcer lost by 13%.
items.detail: CDC tuberculosis NGS case KA115047 (award 31 Jul 2026) had a NT$3,696,000 budget and a NT$3,660,000 floor. 圖爾思生物科技 (a Taiwan-origin service) won at NT$3,115,200, which is 15.7% below budget. Genomics BioSci, the usual Illumina-platform outsourcer, bid NT$3,590,400, 15.3% higher than the winner. The first public tender in June 2026 had failed with no bidders. Where a second bidder appears, the price drops far more than in single-bidder lots at 0 to 6%. The sequencing platform used by the winner is not stated.
items.why_new: This is a named lot where an Illumina-channel vendor was undercut. Platform is unconfirmed, and the general 10-16% two-bidder range is already known.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Taiwan's Ministry of Defense is trying to buy a NT$40M 'new-generation high-precision' sequencer, so some public capital spending on sequencing is still being planned.
items.detail: Case HE15001L162 had a NT$40,000,000 budget (about US$1.3M) and was first tendered 14 Apr 2026. It failed 10 Jun 2026 and was re-tendered 17 Jun 2026. The National Defense Medical University had run a reference-price solicitation for the same item class in Oct and Nov 2025, going from 3 items to 2. The platform is not named, and 'high-precision' likely points to a long-read or high-accuracy system, not Illumina. I found no award record.
items.source_name: Taiwan PCC, Ministry of National Defense HE15001L162; NDMC HE15001L
items.why_new: The lot is new, but its platform is unknown and the dollar value is too small to move Illumina's volume.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: Even if GeneDx's new payer coverage lifted volume as guided, the extra exome/genome Gb would be only about 0.05–0.5% of Illumina's annual high-throughput Gb.
items.detail: GeneDx guides 33,200 exome/genome tests for Q3'26, versus 30,785 in Q2'26 (+32% y/y, or ~7.5K more tests than a year earlier). The y/y increment of ~7.5K tests per quarter, at ~8–11 Gb per exome up to ~100–125 Gb per genome, is ~0.06–0.94M Gb per quarter, or ~0.25–3.7M Gb a year. Against the ~800M Gb a year HT base used in the corpus, that is ~0.03–0.5%. Even at an all-genome mix, GeneDx's whole run-rate (33.2K × 125 Gb ≈ 4.2M Gb per quarter) is ~2% of HT Gb. So the Medicaid and Carelon payer openings are real, but they cannot by themselves reverse a volume slowdown.
items.source_name: GeneDx Q2 2026 earnings release; corpus Gb-per-test and HT base assumptions
items.quote: Expanded the total number of state Medicaid programs covering outpatient exome and/or genome sequencing to 39
items.why_new: It sizes the newly found payer openings (39 states, Carelon 56M lives, Medi-Cal) against Illumina's Gb base, which no known item does.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: At Taichung VGH's 2026 300-cycle reagent award, a non-Genetech distributor gave only ~9% off its opening bid overall (4% on small kits, 12% on large), below the ~15% settlement pattern seen with Illumina's main Taiwan distributor.
items.detail: Award 115A018 (15 Sep 2026, one bidder, Genomics BioSci): opening bids totalled NT$21.933M, and the award was NT$19.917M (−9.2%). By tier the cuts were P1 −4.2%, P2 −4.1%, P3 −12.2%, P4 −12.0%, and every line was awarded at or just under the hospital's own base price. D101 found Genetech single bids settling at ~85% of the opening bid (−15%) across 2022–26. This lot shows the discount is set by the buyer's reserve price and grows with kit size, but it does not show the discount accelerating. The platform is unconfirmed (the notice says only '300-cycle sequencing reagent kit').
items.why_new: It adds bid-to-award cuts by tier from the verified award notice and tests the D101 ~15% settlement pattern on a different distributor.
